With a 1,000 m travel budget and a 500 m limit on walking without an opportunity to rest, 99.5% of older residents in Feudenheim lived within 500 m of a rest, yet only 33.5% could reach at least one destination in each of five categories (food shops, pharmacies, primary healthcare, public transport, and community services) on ordinary shortest routes meeting this limit. Finding alternative routes with sufficiently spaced rests increased this share to 61.4%; allowing longer stretches with an added cost raised it to 76.2%, compared with 89.7% when resting needs were ignored. Across Mannheim, 20.2% of older residents lost access to a reachable category when routes required a resting opportunity every 500 m, versus 7.1% when longer stretches were allowed at extra cost. Compared with the shortest physical distance, the least burdensome routes incurred extra costs from seating gaps: a median of 7.3 m of equivalent walking distance across city areas (90th percentile: 45.9 m). Better-placed seating could reduce this burden without changing street layouts. These measures help planners identify deficiencies, test improvements and guide route choices.

authors.name: Nir Fulman, Himshikhar Mazumdar

papers.title: Embodied physical learning: a trained bacterial cell wall can guide organism behavior
papers.summary: Physical learning studies how physical systems themselves can be trained to perform learning tasks using physical laws. For instance, disordered spring networks can be trained by local rules to route a mechanical signal from one site in the network to another. Disordered spring networks play key roles in many facets of cell biology, not just in terms of mechanics, but also in terms of motility. How then can training on the substrate itself impact the action of an organism, such as a bacterium? Here, we train a spring-network model of the bacterial cell wall and embed it in a motile agent. The stimulus is the load the cell generates by colliding with a surface. The trained wall routes that load across the body to distant flagellar motors, where it drives stator release, and the resulting turn biases the cell toward escape and delays subsequent surface contacts. On the first near-wall tumble after entrapment, the trained cell recovers 89% of the advantage an ideal side-resolved controller provides. We call this arrangement embodied physical learning: the stimulus, the actuator, and the consequences all belong to the agent, and the training force scale is inherited from the agent's own sensing rather than imposed. An actuator with its own kinetics imposes a second, tighter constraint: the routed signal must switch the actuator within the stimulus window. We also find that behavior converges within a few hundred wall encounters, comparable to what a cell in sustained contact with structure experiences in a single generation, and that the routing survives continuous crosslink remodeling provided crucial, tension-bearing bonds are protected. Experimental tests of embodied physical learning are discussed.

authors.name: Nada Elmeligy, No Chen, J. M. Schwarz

papers.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
papers.summary: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $\zeta(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $\Delta_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $\kappa_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $\kappa_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-\chi r$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $\chi$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $\kappa$.

authors.name: Raul Jimenez, Svitlana Mayboroda, Camillo de Lellis, David N. Spergel, Max Engelstein

papers.title: Improving the accuracy of the momentum-exchange method in lattice Boltzmann methods
papers.summary: In the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), the momentum-exchange method (MEM) is widely used to evaluate hydrodynamic forces at fluid-solid interfaces due to its computational efficiency and geometric flexibility. However, when mapping complex geometries onto structured Cartesian grids, the physical boundary rarely intersects the lattice links exactly at their midpoints. This discrepancy violates an implicit assumption inherent to the conventional momentum-exchange (CME) formulation. In this study, we systematically analyze this geometric deficiency and demonstrate that it induces significant force inaccuracies, even in elementary flows where the solid boundary deviates from the midway position. To resolve this, we propose a modified momentum-exchange (MME) method that explicitly accounts for the exact boundary location along the lattice links, demonstrating enhanced accuracy for both flat and curved geometries. Furthermore, we address another critical issue with the interpolation-supplemented bounce-back (ISBB) schemes, and that is their inherent violation of local mass conservation. This mass leakage induces unphysical pressure buildup in the system, which compromises the accuracy and stability of the LBM. We propose a mass-conservative remedy for ISBB schemes that eliminates this leakage. Through a series of benchmark simulations of increasing complexity, we demonstrate that combining the proposed MME with the mass-corrected ISBB scheme drastically improves the fidelity of hydrodynamic force evaluations, establishing a robust framework essential for moving boundary problems and fluid-structure interactions.

authors.name: Abbas Fakhari

papers.title: The lattice Boltzmann machine
papers.summary: The lattice Boltzmann (LB) method is widely regarded as a very flexible and efficient solver for a broad class of transport phenomena in fluids, soft matter and related fields. In this paper, we posit that such flexibility is a direct result of its generative nature as a rule-driven information-processing machine. Its update, a relaxation toward a local target followed by a shift along the lattice, belongs to the same class of iterated relaxation dynamics as residual networks and transformers, with the difference that in LB the operators are fixed by conservation and symmetry rather than learned from data. We show that three properties of this update are sufficient to promote the emergence of closed macroscopic laws from the underlying iteration process, the physical content of the target deciding the specific law in question. A machine whose target is drawn at random generates the transport law predicted from its moments. A network given the same three properties on a graph, where there is no lattice, is trained on a traffic process and generates a conservation law of its own. The mechanism has a precise limit, where the damping of the non-conserved modes fails, and on the lattice the macroscopic law gives no warning of it. In this reading, LB is a lattice Boltzmann machine whose informing rules are supplied by physics rather than by training. Its three properties then state what a new ingredient should preserve when it enters an LB model, whether it comes from physics or from data.

authors.name: Hua-Dong Yao, Sauro Succi

papers.title: Convection in the interior of Cepheid variable stars
papers.summary: This paper is associated with a poster winner of a 2025 American Physical Society's Division of Fluid Dynamics (DFD) Gallery of Fluid Motion Award for work presented at the DFD Gallery of Fluid Motion. The original poster is available online at the Gallery of Fluid Motion, https://doi.org/10.1103/APS.DFD.2025.GFM.P005.

authors.name: Maxime Stuck, Jane Pratt

papers.title: Between Heisenberg and Feynman: Ettore Majorana's Reflections on the Meaning of Quantum Theory
papers.summary: Ettore Majorana is undoubtedly one of the most important figures in 20th-century Italian science. His contributions to nuclear physics and Quantum Mechanics (QM) included innovative ideas, and the search for Majorana-type neutrinos remains an ongoing experimental research question. However, very little is known about his perspective on the significance of the quantum state, the philosophical implications of the then-new mechanics, and the relationship between QM and other sciences. This chapter aims to address this gap. In more detail, here I present the standard interpretation of Majorana's view on the quantum state, according to which the Italian physicist anticipated the physical content of Feynman's path-integral formulation of quantum theory. In what follows, I critically examine this position and propose an alternative understanding of Majorana's beliefs on the nature of the quantum state and the wave function. Finally, I briefly discuss his reflections concerning the major conceptual revolutions introduced by QM, notably, in his view, the impossibility of extending the objectivity and determinism of classical mechanics to the quantum realm, and their consequences for the relation between physics and the social sciences, disciplines that Majorana deeply studied before his disappearance.

authors.name: Andrea Oldofredi

papers.title: A Theory of Partial Truth for Scientific Statements
papers.summary: Scientific representations often combine accurate and inaccurate components, which a single bivalent classification does not distinguish. This paper develops a restricted formal framework for estimating partial factual truth. For fixed content and valuation criteria, the target is adequacy to the facts, independent of the available evidence; its numerical assessment through evidence remains fallible. Quantitative claims are evaluated by normalized discrepancies between asserted and empirically supported values. Admissible finite conjunctions are assessed over a fixed basis of distinct elementary claims using arithmetic or relevance-weighted means. The resulting valuations preserve the contributions from accurate components and are independent of grouping when component counts or total weights are retained. Zero-relevance additions leave the contextual valuation unchanged, but compensation remains possible among components with positive relevance. Worked examples examine admissibility, changes of granularity, measurement indeterminacy, and sensitivity of comparisons to discrepancy scales and relevance weights. An astrophysical application connects the assessment to published observations. The framework applies to selected testable consequences of models and theories, without providing a numerical calculus for arbitrary formulas or a unique method for choosing scales and weights. It permits conditional comparisons of factual adequacy while distinguishing them from confidence, empirical coverage, and convergence toward a complete truth.

authors.name: Gustavo E. Romero

papers.title: The shear Alfv\'en continuum of optimized stellarators
papers.summary: The shear Alfv\'en continuum has been studied extensively in tokamaks, but its gap structure in modern optimized stellarators has received less attention, despite its importance for energetic-particle confinement in fusion pilot plants. We compute and compare the continua of five reactor-scale stellarator equilibria: two quasi-axisymmetric (QA), two quasi-helically symmetric (QH), and one quasi-isodynamic (QI). We present selective Fourier mode schemes that provide a sufficient resolution of eigenfrequencies within the frequency range of interest. In all five configurations, the widest gap is the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) gap, which is driven by rotating ellipticity. This gap lies in the frequency range of strong resonance with prompt fusion-born alphas in the QA configurations but not in the QH configurations, suggesting that QH configurations may be easier to optimize for alpha confinement. Near-axis theory predicts the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) and EAE gap widths well but overestimates the MAE gap widths and the gap widths of the QI configuration. These discrepancies likely arise from interactions between gaps, which depend on the rotational transform profile and are not captured by near-axis theory.

authors.name: Abdullah Hyder, Elizabeth Paul, Alexey Knyazev

papers.title: Reduced-order modeling of squeeze-film damped electrostatically actuated microbeams using complex modes of the coupled problem
papers.summary: A reduced-order model is developed for the nonlinear dynamics of electrostatically actuated microbeams, including the full squeeze film effect. The model uses Petrov-Galerkin projection on damped complex modes of the fully coupled fluid-structure problem. The Euler-Bernoulli theory for calmped-clamped and clamped-free microbeams, with mid-plane stretching and electrostatic nonlinearities, and the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation are discretized by the differential quadrature method for the static solution and eigenvalue problem. The calculated eigenmodes are either complex conjugates describing the coupled behavior of the device or real depicting the fluid relaxation. The natural frequencies and quality factors are compared to experimental and numerical results found in the literature. Depending on the ambient pressure, the geometry of the microbeam, and the fluid boundary conditions, squeeze-film effect can impact not only the effective damping of the device but also its dynamics. It is shown that in some cases dropping fluid relaxation modes cannot be compensated by any set of purely structural modes. The non-classical damping introduced by the fluid modes is a spatially distributed phase difference between pressure and deflection. The convergence analysis of the dynamic response resulting from the reduced-order model showed that a basis with one set of coupled modes and one fluid mode can reproduce the results of a fully discretized model within 1.5% error and at much faster computational time.

authors.name: Fehmi Najar

papers.title: Bearing, heading and the perceptual geometry of collective motion
papers.summary: Traditional models of collective motion commonly assume that animals turn to match their neighbours' directions of travel. In the harmonic theory, decisions follow from a neural representation of direction, and a neighbour enters only as a stimulus at a bearing, the direction in which it lies. Here we show that a neighbour's spatial extent allows its orientation to enter through projection geometry alone, and the theory generates a matrix of coupling coefficients indexed by the neighbour's bearing and aspect. Responses to bearing alone form one edge of this matrix, and classical heading matching is a special case on its diagonal, one ray through a two-parameter family. Independently, an animal that responds only to neighbour position, perceived with a delay, acquires an alignment coefficient set by the slope of its distance-weighted attraction profile, so that it can align, anti-align or reverse sign. Alignment need not be a rule to be measured. In schooling fish and walking pigeons with body orientation measured independently of travel, social responses are recovered, including bearing responses in the fish. Heading excess depends on how turning is measured, appearing in the fish with forward but not centred responses and remaining unresolved in pigeons. Controls show why neither outcome identifies a direct alignment rule. In fish recordings with motion-assigned body polarity, heading-dependent structure departs from Vicsek form and fails the coefficient test for a common angular potential. Whether animals align thereby becomes a measurable question, with geometric, perceptual and behavioural origins that can be distinguished.

authors.name: Mohammad Salahshour

papers.title: The dielectric tensor for a fully anisotropic regularized Kappa plasma
papers.summary: It has been known for some decades that the plasma in the Solar System is invariably in a state away from thermal equilibrium. In several plasma environments, be it in the Solar Wind or within planetary magnetospheres, the plasma has been found in a quasi-stationary nonthermal state, with a substantial fraction of its high-energy particles fitting along power-law distributions, instead of the exponential decay of thermal systems. Translating the observations in energy to velocity distribution functions (VDFs), the Kappa plasma model has been employed by the space plasma community, with the (standard) Kappa VDF (SKD) being the preferred choice. However, recent works have called attention to the limitations of the SKD model, proposing as a viable alternative the regularized Kappa VDF (RKD) model, which corrects the deficiencies of the SKD. The RKD model introduces a Gaussian-like dependency on the very high-energy part of the VDF that effectively cut-offs, via a regularization parameter, the Lorentzian profile of the intermediate-energy range. In this work, we employ a generalized RKD that supports anisotropies both in the thermal speed parameters and in the regularization parameters, including as well the possibility of drifts parallel to the magnetic field. This generalized RKD (called the bi-regularized Kappa with drift distribution, bRKd), is employed to derive for the first time the components of the susceptibility tensor for a suprathermal plasma species/population modelled by the bRKd. The tensor components are valid for waves with any propagation angle, frequency range and polarization. During the derivation, new special functions are defined and analyzed, which generalize previous expressions restricted to the parallel propagation limit.

authors.name: Rudi Gaelzer, Horst Fichtner, Dustin Lee Schr\"oder, Marian Lazar, Klaus Scherer

papers.title: Dispersive Corrections to Electromagnetic Energy and Power Flux Are Imprints of Eliminated Degrees of Freedom
papers.summary: In a spatially dispersive medium the electromagnetic energy and flux are given by the frequency and wave-vector derivatives of the constitutive parameters, a result known as the Agranovich--Ginzburg (AG) formulas. Here, we clarify the physical meaning of the derivative terms in these relations and show that they measure the energy and flux carried by the degrees of freedom of the internal field-matter dynamics that the Maxwellian constitutive description hides. We construct an extended state-space model of such dynamics for a wide class of temporally and spatially dispersive media, from which the Maxwellian constitutive relations follow upon elimination of the internal variables, the effective material operator resulting from the Schur complement of the eliminated internal block. A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a capacitively loaded wire medium is treated in the Supplemental Material.

authors.name: Stanislav Maslovski, Constantin Simovski

papers.title: Multireference perturbation theory with nonorthogonal determinants
papers.summary: We introduce NOCI-RSPT, a framework for constructing perturb-then-diagonalize multireference perturbation theories for model spaces defined by nonorthogonal determinants. NOCI-RSPT realizes order-by-order size consistency by orthogonalizing the effective Hamiltonian before perturbatively truncating it and removes problematic internal excitations through model-space projection. The resulting second- and third-order theories, NOCI-RS2 and NOCI-RS3, recover MP2 and MP3 in the single-reference limit and exhibit the same respective cost scaling at fixed model-space size. Calculations on assemblies of multireference $\mathrm{H}_2$ fragments demonstrate size consistency, while calculations of the low-energy states of $\mathrm{H}_2$ along its dissociation curve demonstrate improved numerical stability and characterize the influence of intruder states. The latter calculations demonstrate the exceptional accuracy achieved by NOCI-RS3 and illustrate how model-space expansion and amplitude regularization can mitigate the effects of large perturbative corrections. Altogether, NOCI-RSPT provides a systematic route to low-scaling multireference perturbation theories built from single-reference methods.

authors.name: Alex Krotz, K. Birgitta Whaley, Martin Head-Gordon

papers.title: A componentwise spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann closure for finite-volume MHD at finite magnetic Reynolds number
papers.summary: At finite magnetic Reynolds number, the field induced by a moving conducting fluid or solid extends into open space, so a finite mesh needs an outer boundary condition that represents the decaying exterior field. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) codes widely use pseudo-vacuum or truncation at a finite radius. Neither condition is physically correct for a vacuum exterior, but the exact alternatives are costly or limited to simple geometries. We present a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) closure on a fixed enclosing sphere and release it as part of the open-source multi-region finite-volume solver FreeMHD. The closure matches each Cartesian component of the vector potential to its decaying exterior solution, which retains all three decaying vector-Laplace families. A meshed vacuum buffer connects non-spherical conductors to the sphere. We verify the closure with manufactured modes, sphere free decay, sphere and oblate dynamos, and a freely braking rotor. Under refinement, oblate dynamo thresholds and sphere growth rates converge toward independent spectral references, and the rotor torque matches an exact transient reference. On the same sphere, pseudo-vacuum and truncation give the larger errors predicted by their exterior models.

authors.name: Min Ki Jung, Brian Wynne, Francisco Saenz, Yufan Xu, Yong-Su Na, Egemen Kolemen

papers.title: A nonlinear interface for phase transduction
papers.summary: Broadband nonlinear frequency conversion mixes multiple input frequencies, complicating the transfer of programmed spectral phase between widely separated spectral bands. Here we identify and experimentally realize a quasi-linear phase-transduction regime enabled by broad phase-matching acceptance and effective localization of the complex frequency-mixing response. This selectivity can arise from coherent interference without narrowing the pump spectrum. We implement this regime through dispersive four-wave mixing in an argon-filled hollow-capillary fiber, transferring spectral phase from 1032-nm near-infrared signals to 344-nm ultraviolet idlers. Transient-grating frequency-resolved optical gating reveals frequency-inverted, phase-conjugating transfer of quadratic dispersion, localized phase steps, and low-frequency sinusoidal modulation. After correction for the modeled pump-induced phase background, the quadratic and step responses exhibit approximately linear point-by-point correlations. With increasing pump chirp, the transferred phase steps become more sharply preserved, and the fitted phase-transfer gains approach unity, consistent with enhanced effective localization. These results demonstrate quasi-linear spectral-phase transduction in a co-propagating broadband nonlinear interaction without spatially separating its spectral components.

authors.name: Linshan Sun, Hao Zhang, Cameron Leary, Alex Amador, Sergio Carbajo

papers.title: Current frontiers in mobility and well-being
papers.summary: Human mobility has a profound impact on social structure and collective behavior, which allows individuals to reshape group structures in response to strategy information, acting as a double-edged sword for cooperative behavior. It can both disrupt existing cooperative communities and enable individuals to escape adverse environments and seek high-quality interaction partners. This paper surveys current research progress on the impact of mobility on cooperation within the framework of evolutionary game theory, focusing on specific mechanisms of passive escape, dynamic self-organization driven by active choice, and the core trade-off between migration costs and speed. Mobility, an individual's spatial response to local strategic information that turns location into strategic advantage, influences cooperative evolution by altering interactive information and environmental feedback, consequently affecting sustainable social well-being, such as collective benefits. Under specific conditions, this self-interested behavior at the individual level can foster macrosocial harmony, embodying the unity of individual rationality and collective cooperation. Furthermore, we also discusses inter-layer migration and information routing mechanisms in multilayer networks and extends the perspective to human-machine hybrid systems where mobile agents with information regulation capabilities can serve as information supernodes. Our paper aims to provide a unified framework for understanding mobility as a combined physical and informational driving force in the evolution of cooperation.

authors.name: Wen-Jing Li, Luo-Luo Jiang, Attila Szolnoki

papers.title: Evaluation of Image Noise from Computed Tomography in an Organ-Specific Anthropomorphic Phantom
papers.summary: Computed tomography (CT) is used ubiquitously for diagnostic imaging, with novel iterative reconstructions such as hybrid iterative reconstruction with partial model-based component (ASiR-V) and deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) increasingly utilized. In conjunction, CT vendors have developed a noise index (NI) to reduce radiation dose during protocol development. However, it is unclear how these reconstruction algorithms reduce noise as NI changes, particularly across multiple organs. The goal of this study was to utilize an anthropomorphic phantom to evaluate image noise against the prescribed NI across different organs, determine if DLIR reduces image noise compared to ASiR-V, and use this relationship to determine the maximum volume CT dose index (CTDIvol) reduction at equivalent noise levels. Repeat images were acquired on a GE HealthCare Revolution Apex CT scanner across NI values in an anthropomorphic adult-sized phantom from Kyoto Kagaku with ASiR-V and DLIR. Organs-of-interest were contoured using TotalSegmentator in 3D Slicer. The correlation between the CTDIvol and NI was determined. The standard deviation of the difference in the repeat images was used as a noise metric (NM), correlated with NI, used to determine the NI at equivalent NM between ASiR-V and DLIR, then applied to determine the dose reduction and difference in NM. The relationship between NI and the resulting CTDIvol was found to be proportional to a power law of exponent -2.23. The maximum potential absolute dose reduction from using DLIR was found in the liver at 1.3 mGy with an NI of 7.9. Across all organs, the relative dose reduction increased, the NM-to-NI ratio decreased, and the noise reduction increased across NI. The relationship between image noise and the prescribed NI differed between ASiR-V and DLIR and varied by organ, with model-based dose reductions of up to 1.3 mGy in the liver.

authors.name: Lucas McCullum, Mojtaba Zarei, Andy Tsai, Michael J. Callahan, Peng Sun, Da Zhang

papers.title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks(PINNs) offer a mesh-free and continuously differentiable approach to fluid simulation. However, standard monolithic PINNs for incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations often suffer from severe constraint coupling and spectral biases, limiting both convergence and accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a segregated, iterative, and multi-stage PINN (SIM-PINN) inspired by the classical projection method in computational fluid dynamics. In SIM-PINN, the nonlinear NS equations are decoupled into the linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations. Each is addressed separately using dedicated multi-stage neural networks and coupled through projection-based inner iterations. Each stage of the multi-stage neural networks for the momentum equations corresponds to one iteration of the projection method, in which the velocity fields are progressively refined at targeted frequencies. Upon iteration convergence, solutions to the fully coupled and nonlinear NS equations are recovered. By integrating the segregated and iterative framework with the multi-stage training, SIM-PINN alleviates the optimization difficulties of the incompressible NS equations arising from nonlinearity, constraint coupling, and spectral biases. The improved convergence and accuracy are demonstrated by simulations of steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flows.

authors.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Zhixiang Ling, Yinghao Huo, Huayong Liu, Yunde Su

papers.title: Stable dissipative topological solitons in media with even-order dispersion
papers.summary: The formation and dynamics of dissipative solitons are governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity, alongside the gain-loss balance. While it is known that dispersion orders beyond the conventional second order support stable solitons, the possibility of the creation of dissipative topological solitons in this setting was not explored. Here, we reveal a class of stable dissipative solitons enabled by the pure-high-even-order dispersion (PHEOD), with dispersion orders m=4, 6, 8, and 10. The resulting dissipative topological solitons (DTSs) and moving topological solitons (MTSs) are dark-type structures featuring a zero-amplitude point that separates two CW backgrounds with opposite signs. In particular, the PHEOD solitons feature oscillatory tails, which are not present in the conventional dark states. The linear-stability analysis confirms full robustness of the PHEOD-supported DTSs and MTSs. We also explore collision dynamics of MTSs, whose repulsive interactions are inelastic, leading either to rebound, accompanied by emission of dispersive radiation, or complete fusion. These findings establish PHEOD as a means for the generation of new species of dissipative solitons, and broaden the variety of nonlinear modes available to experimental studies in nonlinear optics.

authors.name: Xianan Sun, Dongdong Wang, Dumitru Mihalache, David Laroze, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li

papers.title: Suppression of the Laser Hosing Instability in a Parabolic Plasma Channel
papers.summary: We present an analytical stability analysis of the laser hosing instability in a parabolic channel in the weakly relativistic regime. We employ a variational principle approach to derive a set of coupled equations describing laser dynamics in a transversely inhomogeneous plasma. The quadratic Lagrangian formalism is applied to perform a stability analysis and to derive the growth rates for hosing in both long- and short-wavelength regimes. We find that a parabolic channel suppresses the long-wavelength hosing mode completely, for any channel depth, and that the unstable band of the short-wavelength mode is bounded below by a cutoff wavenumber set by the ratio of the channel frequency to the hosing coupling. A steeper channel narrows the unstable band and lowers the short-wavelength growth rate, but cannot stabilize the mode, since the dispersion relation forbids damping identically. The analysis is accompanied by two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, which reproduce the prediction in the nonlinear regime: the long-wavelength mode is absent in a channel, the surviving modulation shortens as the channel steepens, and its amplitude falls with channel depth. Further, our simulation results demonstrate the sensitivity of off-axis laser propagation to the plasma channel and distinguish the hosing instability from laser oscillations due to off-axis laser propagation in a plasma channel.

authors.name: Yash M Jogiya, Vishwa Bandhu Pathak

papers.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
papers.summary: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. Here, we experimentally demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption in both polarizations at the same wavelengths and angles from a single structure, wherein a germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on a doped InAs layer scatters TE-polarized light into near fields with components perpendicular to the magnetic field, allowing the magneto-optic response of the InAs to act on them. Under a 0.48 T field from a permanent Halbach array, this structure exhibits a difference in absorptivity between $+B$ and $-B$ of 0.035 in both TE and TM polarization at 16.6 $\mu$m. Our approach shows that the magneto-optic response of a planar semiconductor and the resonances of a dielectric metasurface can be designed together, offering a potential route to dual-polarization nonreciprocity at fields available from permanent magnets for emerging energy and heat transfer technologies.

authors.name: Mason Christiansen, Jae S. Hwang, Yi Jie Lin, Aryan Zaveri, Tianjun Li, Daniel Cui, Baolai Liang, Aaswath P. Raman

papers.title: Bayesian Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for trustworthy Reynolds-stress closures
papers.summary: Data-driven turbulence closures can improve Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) predictions, but their use is limited by two issues: learned constitutive relations are often difficult to inspect, and predictions typically lack reliable uncertainty estimates. We develop a Bayesian tensor-basis Kolmogorov-Arnold network (BKAN) for Reynolds-stress anisotropy that addresses both within a single closure. Learnable univariate spline functions on network edges provide an inspectable representation that can, where sufficiently simple, be approximated symbolically. Variational posteriors over spline coefficients yield a predictive distribution separating epistemic uncertainty, due to limited training data, from aleatoric uncertainty, the irreducible scatter of high-fidelity targets at given inputs. Galilean and rotational invariance, symmetry, and tracelessness are enforced through the tensor basis, while physical realisability is treated separately through soft regularisation. A controlled regression benchmark assesses predictive accuracy, calibration, and Bayesian parameterisation. Placing the posterior on spline coefficients gives the best overall balance of accuracy, calibration, parameter cost, and interpretability. Applied to Reynolds-stress anisotropy, the BKAN is accurate in distribution, with calibrated, informative uncertainty that tends to identify larger prediction errors. Under geometric extrapolation, however, the model becomes overconfident: epistemic uncertainty increases but does not fully account for growing prediction errors. Finally, the framework is extended to three-dimensional wind-farm wakes, where the learned correction transfers to unseen layouts and posterior samples are propagated through the RANS solver, with the aleatoric component injected as a spatially correlated field, to obtain uncertainty bounds on the predicted wake flow.

authors.name: Ali Eidi, Kherlen Jigjid, Tyler Buchanan, Richard P. Dwight

papers.title: Evolutionary dynamics of collective-risk social dilemma game with risk uncertainty and adaptive strategy
papers.summary: The collective-risk dilemma game constitutes the leading metaphor for studying the evolution of cooperation in populations of selfish individuals. Although most theoretical studies often consider the risk level as a fixed parameter, this may not fully reflect the uncertain nature of risk detected in real-world scenarios. Motivated by the observation that individuals can infer their game environment and accordingly adjust their actual behavior, here we investigate this game with uncertain risk. In particular, we introduce a type of adaptive agents who incur an observation cost to infer the risk level during game interactions, and subsequently decide whether to cooperate or defect based on their tolerance thresholds. We first calculate the fixation probabilities of three different strategies in a mutation-free regime. Our results show that adaptive agents are favored by natural selection at low observation costs and moderate tolerance thresholds. Moreover, the fixation of adaptive agents results in higher levels of cooperation when both parameters are relatively low. We then consider behavioral mutation and systematically explore how average cooperation level and group achievement vary with observation costs, tolerance thresholds, and mutation rates. Importantly, the main results remain intact when the mutation is considered. Furthermore, when the tolerance threshold is small, the presence of adaptive agents results in a higher cooperation level and group achievement compared to the traditional setup when only unconditional cooperators and defectors are present. This advantage, however, gradually erodes with an increasing tolerance threshold and these two quantities fall below the levels observed in the classic two-strategy case.

authors.name: Chuanzhi Zhou, Ju Han, Xiaojie Chen, Attila Szolnoki

papers.title: Triaxial $\mu$-PIC for resolving Multi-Hit Ambiguity
papers.summary: The micro pixel chamber ($\mu$-PIC), a type of micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGD), features pixel electrodes structured similarly to a sliced proportional counter. Conventionally, $\mu$-PIC electrodes are connected to orthogonal strip electrodes to reduce the number of readout circuits; however, this configuration introduces multi-hit ambiguity when tracing winding tracks or during high-rate operations. A well-known solution to this problem is the adoption of an additional readout axis. To this end, we designed a new electrode structure using Garfield++ simulations and fabricated a triaxial $\mu$-PIC based on through-glass-via (TGV) technology. This triaxial $\mu$-PIC achieved a high gas gain of $1.1\times 10^4$ and the energy resolution of 22\% (FWHM) at 5.9~keV, Furthermore, the false-hit probability was less than 0.78\% at a 95\% confidence level for two clusters separated by a distance of over 3 mm, consistent with Garfield++ predictions. With this triaxial $\mu$-PIC, single avalanche signals are collected from three independent readout strip electrodes (the anode and two cathodes). The charge ratio among these electrodes remains nearly constant at anode:U-cathode:V-cathode=3:2:1. In addition, we successfully achieved an enhanced gain of $3.2\times 10^4$ without increasing the discharge risk by employing an alternative operation mode.

authors.name: A. Takada, M. Abe, Y. Yoshida, T. Okeda, J. D. Parker, K. Miuchi, K. Ohta, T. Motomura, T. Tanimori

papers.title: Non-axisymmetric MHD equilibria with an arbitrary number of field periods
papers.summary: Several closed-form non-axisymmetric magnetic fields with nested toroidal flux surfaces have recently been discovered as exact benchmarks for verifying three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium codes. However, all of these solutions have at most two field periods ($N \le 2$), i.e., identical segments that repeat toroidally. Here, we derive closed-form non-axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic equilibria for an arbitrary integer number of field periods $N \geq 1$. The equilibria have non-constant pressure and closed magnetic field lines with either zero rotational transform ($\iota = 0$) for $N \geq 1$ or integer rotational transform ($\iota = \pm N$) for $N \ge 3$. For the reflection-symmetric $\iota = 0$ equilibria, we also construct a matched exterior vacuum field with continuous magnetic field across the plasma boundary, providing a benchmark for free-boundary equilibrium codes.

authors.name: Opal Issan, Lucas Jos\'e, Matt Landreman, Jonathan Citrin, Brendan Tracey

papers.title: Simulation of Refraction Through Voxel Volumes
papers.summary: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. We first validate this method compared to a model with an analytical solution, and then investigate the effects of voxel size, interpolation choice, and illumination to grid alignment on a few simulated test objects. From these investigations, we make several recommendations to guide simulations using these techniques.

authors.name: Rainier Mobley, Jean Michel L\'etang, Max Langer

papers.title: Vibration patterns and reed - pipe coupling in the free reeds of the hulusi
papers.summary: The hulusi is a free-reed instrument from Yunnan, Western China, known for its unique sound. Its reed and frame are cut from a single brass sheet in a symmetric shape, the free end narrower than the clamped end. Its free reeds are coupled to tubes that determine the instrument's pitch during normal playing. With reduced playing pressure, the reed frequency takes over the instrument sound. We report point-by-point laser Doppler vibrometry on the reeds of six handmade hulusi, two each in the keys of F, B$\flat$ and C, measured at 29 points on every reed or tongue over nine fingerings and two supply pressures. Steady-state spectra carry two components: a tube-dominant frequency $f_\mathrm{tube}$, locked to the air-column resonance and carrying a complete harmonic series, and a reed-dominant frequency $f_\mathrm{reed}$, which is not an integer multiple of it. Their difference $\Delta = f_\mathrm{tube} - f_\mathrm{reed}$ runs from 38 to 523~Hz across the dataset, from about three semitones to more than an octave. The reed-dominant frequency rises with the pressure at the reed, by $28.0 \pm 10.3$ Hz/kPa once $f_\mathrm{tube}$ is controlled for. At low pressure supply the oscillation loses its lock to the air column, falls silent for about 100~ms, and returns at the reed frequency within 0.1 Hz. The spatial patterns are forced oscillation shapes of one limit cycle at its fundamental and harmonics rather than eigenmodes: the measured frequencies stand in strict 1:2:3 ratios, far from the bending ratios of a cantilever. The reed-dominant pattern is pure bending and holds across fingerings and supply pressures, whereas the tube-dominant pattern breaks up near the oscillation threshold.

authors.name: Yang Xia, Rolf Bader, Simon Linke

papers.title: Graph Symbolic Distillation: Decoding Graph Data into Interpretable Formulas across Materials and Chemistry
papers.summary: Graph data provide a natural representation of the interconnected structures and interactions underlying many chemical and materials systems. Graph neural networks (GNNs) can learn complex relationships from such data, yet translating these representations into interpretable descriptors and scientific insights remains challenging. Here we introduce graph symbolic distillation (GSD), a framework for decoding graph data into interpretable symbolic formulas. GSD identifies task-relevant message-passing architectures and distills their learned transformations while preserving graph connectivity and aggregation operations. Across three case studies spanning bulk materials, molecules, and surfaces, GSD not only recovers expert-defined descriptors from elementary node and edge features, but also reveals relationships emerging from their organization in complex graphs: extremal local geometric descriptors for band gap variations in $\gamma$-CsPbI$_3$, a local polarity--size relationship underlying hydration free energy, and site-specific electronic--connectivity coupling in multidentate adsorption. GSD thus provides a general route from graph data to interpretable descriptors and new, testable scientific insights.

authors.name: Yuxuan Yao, Harald Oberhofer, Karsten Reuter, Wenbin Xu

papers.title: Unified design of short mode-evolution couplers
papers.summary: Short mode-evolution couplers have been designed with several seemingly different approaches, including fast quasi-adiabatic dynamics (FAQUAD), counter-diabatic (CD) driving realized by tailoring waveguide widths and spacing, CD driving realized by axis bending, and numerical optimization of the coupler geometry. Using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers--Henneberger frame of the bent coupler, we show that these approaches belong to the same design space. The three geometric parameters, width difference, spacing, and axis tilt, act on the light through two functions only: the coupling strength, set by the spacing, and an effective detuning, set by the width difference and the axis curvature. The gauge, bent, and mixed realizations of a CD coupler are therefore the same device and have the same bandwidth. The bandwidth is set by the angle $\chi$ between the light and the field that steers it on the Bloch sphere, integrated along the device as $\int\sin^2\chi dz$, and for a CD coupler this integral is set by the reference alone. This leads to a lithography-aware design rule: make the reference as adiabatic as the minimum gap allows, by narrowing its spacing at the anticrossing, and let exact CD suppress the remaining nonadiabatic coupling. In beam propagation method (BPM) simulations on a polymer platform, a 500\um{} coupler designed this way, without numerical optimization, maintains ${>}99\%$ transfer over 274~nm at a minimum edge gap of 1.05\um, compared with 150~nm for the CD coupler of a fixed-spacing reference at nearly the same gap. Particle swarm optimization of the geometry with BPM in the loop does not exceed the design rule. Three-dimensional BPM of the BCB channel waveguides also confirms these conclusions.

authors.name: S. -Y. Tseng

papers.title: A continuum model of a diffusive compressible gas - Kinetic theory and real gases
papers.summary: Using kinetic theory of gases, we derive the diffusive compressible Euler (dcE) model for ideal gases. The derivation covers all steps from the particle description of a gas, to macroscopic averages, to a discrete system of conservative balance equations in finite volumes, to the system of partial dif- ferential equations. Along the way, we discuss the modelling assumptions, and derive approximations of the diffusion coefficient. In the next part, we discuss the modifications needed to model real gases. In particular, we propose a tentative model for intermolecular friction forces.

authors.name: Magnus Sv\"ard

papers.title: Laser fabrication of vibrating microcavities on silicon: Formation dynamics and frequency tunability
papers.summary: Laser processing of silicon has long since become a standard method for wafer dicing, surface texturing, re-crystallization after ion implantation, as well as surface amorphization, to name a few examples. Here, we introduce a novel concept, the fabrication of vibrating microcavities in a commercial platform, Si wafers covered by a thick SiO2 layer, acting as a membrane. We demonstrate that by exposing our material system to single ultrashort laser pulses above the evaporation threshold of Si, a controlled delamination of the cover layer without fracture can be achieved, leading to the formation of a microcavity accompanied by a surface bulging up to 1.5 micrometer. The formation dynamics of the microcavities has been investigated by time-resolved optical probe techniques. Ultrafast pump-probe microscopy resolves the initial stages of substrate melting, the onset of layer expansion followed by relaxation. Real-time reflectivity measurements with nanosecond resolution resolve the long lived, highly complex oscillation process of the membrane, extending over tens of microseconds. The formed cavities can be re-excited at low fluence without damage or degradation, featuring vibrations at single frequencies with high Q factors. The frequencies can be tuned continuously from 8 MHz up to 19 MHz by adjusting the fabrication fluence. A simple classical model is found to well describe the behavior of the membranes. Our results pave the way for applications in micro- and nanooptics and acoustics, in great part due to the commercial availability of the Si-SiO2 platform and the simplicity of the fabrication method. An extension to the field of microelectromechanical system (MEMS) of this technology is proposed.

authors.name: Belen Valiente, Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Mario Garcia-Lechuga, Irene Solana, Fernando Agull\'o-Rueda, David Grojo, Angel Rodriguez-Fernandez, Javier Solis, Jan Siegel

papers.title: Bringing Dark States to Light after Frustrated Tunneling Ionization
papers.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gases is typically regarded as a sub-laser-cycle process, well described by the semiclassical three-step model. In this work, we report the extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) emission observed in an HHG experiment arising from a longer temporal process associated with dark states populated through frustrated tunneling ionization. The emission exhibits a larger spatial divergence than typical high-order harmonics, resembling the polarization decay of optically bright states. Supported by the time-frequency analysis of the theoretical calculations, we show that the emission originates from the nonradiative capture of the tunneling electrons into excited dark states of the neutral atom, followed by Floquet-like laser-dressing effects induced by the extended tail of the driving pulse. Our results reveal a largely unexplored pathway for XUV generation through laser-dressed dark states, thereby enabling the enhancement of coherent XUV emission at targeted wavelengths with high repetition rates.

authors.name: Yu He, Eleni Tzima, Gergana D. Borisova, Noah L. Wach, Aaron T. Bondy, Juan C. Del Valle, Klaus Bartschat, Christian Ott, Thomas Pfeifer

papers.title: Continuous Space-Time Finite Element Simulations for Biomedical Flows with Large Boundary Motion and Time-Periodicity
papers.summary: We present an axisymmetric continuous simplex space-time finite element method for incompressible fluid flow. Compared to conventional time-stepping methods, the space-time approach has several advantages. First, the motion of the domain is incorporated into the space-time geometry, allowing for large boundary motion without remeshing or projection of the solution. Second, the method allows for time-periodic solutions to be computed directly, without the need to simulate multiple cycles. Third, the space-time mesh can be partitioned in time as well as in space, which enables parallelism in time. The method is demonstrated on an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in a rigid tube. The balloon inflation is modelled based on measured data, and includes a travelling wave along the balloon. The method is able to resolve complex flow features such as jets and recirculation zones. A refinement study shows convergence under temporal, spatial and combined space-time refinement. In weak scaling tests up to 960 ranks, the cost per solver iteration remains approximately constant, and partitioning the mesh into time slabs improves the convergence of the linear solver compared to partitions that cut through both space and time.

authors.name: Nico Dirkes, Marek Behr

papers.title: Atomic Transition Rates on a Quantum Annealer
papers.summary: Electric-dipole (E1) transition rates underlie applications across many areas of physics and demand more accurate wavefunctions than ground-state energies do. We report the first calculation of E1 transition rates on a D-Wave quantum annealer, for neutral Li, Li-like Be, neutral Na, and Na-like Mg. We use a zooming-and-sigma-annealing scheme with floating-point encoding within the Quantum Annealer Eigensolver (QAE) algorithm, which yields ground-state eigenvectors accurate to the chosen three decimal places. Treating the lowest even-parity ($^2S_{1/2}$) and odd-parity ($^2P_{1/2}$, $^2P_{3/2}$) states as separate angular-symmetry sectors gives QAE access to excited atomic configurations for transition-rate calculations. Our results reproduce relativistic configuration-interaction values obtained classically to within numerical precision, demonstrating that the QAE framework extends to a broader class of atomic properties on near-term quantum hardware.

authors.name: Boni Paul, Subimal Deb, Per J\"onsson, J\"orgen Ekman, Bhanu Pratap Das

papers.title: Exascale-ready HemeLB for large-eddy simulation of full-human arterial blood flow
papers.summary: Direct numerical simulation (DNS) of blood flow through the whole human arterial tree is limited by the number of lattice sites that must be advanced on a high-performance computer. We address this limit by combining the lattice Boltzmann solver HemeLB with Smagorinsky large-eddy simulation (LES). HemeLB runs with the same scaling behaviour on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs) and sustains about 10 trillion lattice-site updates per second (TLUPS) on both the Frontier and Aurora exascale supercomputers. In stenotic aortic flow, LES on lattices five and ten times coarser than a 20~$\mu$m DNS reproduces the wall pressure and the cross-sectional pressure and velocity, and its plane-averaged pressure differs from that of the DNS by at most 0.75~mmHg, below 1\% of the local pressure. At 100~$\mu$m, LES reduces the estimated cost of a full-human simulation by a factor of about 625 relative to DNS. We use this resolution to compute blood flow from the head to the feet in a full-human arterial model with 295 million fluid sites, one inlet at the aortic root and 432 Windkessel outlets, at about 15--18 node-hours per cardiac cycle on two Frontier nodes. A single simulation resolves every region simultaneously, from the cerebral arteries to the arteries of the feet. The pressure pulse grows as it travels from the aorta to the feet, the shear stress concentrates in the branches rather than in the aorta, the pulse reaches the outlets later with increasing distance from the heart, and the flow in the legs and feet is triphasic, as in Doppler measurements of the human leg. These results bring patient-specific whole-body lattice Boltzmann simulations within reach of current supercomputers and pave the way for ensemble simulations towards a standard human model.

authors.name: Xiao Xue, Ioannis Zacharoudiou, Peter V. Coveney

papers.title: On the aerodynamics of an accelerating and decelerating propeller in hover at low Reynolds numbers
papers.summary: Small unmanned aerial vehicles commonly regulate propeller thrust through rapid changes in rotational speed, yet it remains unclear how the inflow, the wake, and the near-surface velocity respond to these changes at low Reynolds numbers. A commercial two-bladed propeller was tested in hover with custom blade holders at three additional pitch offsets relative to the original blade geometry, $\Theta =\,$0, 5, and $10^\circ$, and accelerated and decelerated between 3000 and 5000 RPM with open-loop step responses. The resulting nondimensional acceleration and deceleration numbers, below 0.011 and 0.007, suggest negligible acceleration effects. Phase-locked particle image velocimetry (PIV) at 40, 60, and $80\,\%$ rotor radius and in the meridian plane was combined with load measurements. The thrust coefficient responds quasi-steadily at $\Theta = 10^\circ$, but shows hysteresis at the higher pitch offsets, with lower values during acceleration and higher values during deceleration than under steady conditions. This trend opposes expectations from dynamic inflow theory. The effect is largest at $\Theta = 5^\circ$, with deviations from the steady values of up to 8\,% during acceleration and $5\,\%$ during deceleration, compared with $4\,\%$ and $3\,\%$ at $\Theta = 10^\circ$. PIV reveals that the rotor-disk inflow, blade deformation, and sectional circulation remain largely quasi-steady, whereas velocity fluctuations, blade-wake vorticity, and tip-vortex circulation vary strongly, with the largest deviations at low rotational speeds rather than at peak acceleration or deceleration.

authors.name: Manuel Ratz, Christophe Schram, A. Sciacchitano, Miguel A. Mendez

papers.title: Estimating ensemble-mean anomaly correlations and the ratio of predictable components using an unbiased estimate of the predictable signal variance
papers.summary: The correlation ($r$) between ensemble mean forecasts and observations is a frequently-used metric of forecast quality in the weather and climate prediction communities. However, uncorrected estimates of $r$ are biased towards zero at finite ensemble size due to the influence of unpredictable noise that contaminates the sample ensemble mean. This note summarises established ensemble-size adjustment methods and characterises the behaviour of $r_{\infty}$, a correlation estimator that is constructed from an unbiased and ensemble-size-independent estimate of the signal variance. The only requirement is that forecast members are exchangeable with one another such that they can be interpreted as independent draws from a case-specific predictive distribution. The estimator $r_{\infty}$ does not require forecasts and observations to be statistically exchangeable, only that the unpredictable component of each member is uncorrelated with the observed truth, and thus works for both reliable and unreliable forecasts. In some situations, $r_{\infty}$ may be undefined (i.e. the estimated signal variance is negative) or fall outside the admissible range $-1 \leq r_{\infty} \leq 1$ when the predictable signal is small relative to the sampling uncertainty. These inadmissible values can be interpreted as evidence that the true predictable signal cannot be resolved with the available ensemble size and number of cases. The same unbiased signal variance can also be used to estimate the correlation between the predictable signal and individual members to yield an ensemble-size-invariant estimator of the ratio of predictable components (RPC). In contrast, variance-based RPC estimates, including forms that correct only the model predictable component, are biased low by a factor that depends only on the ensemble size and model signal-to-noise ratio.

authors.name: Christopher David Roberts

papers.title: Spectrotemporal imaging of ultrafast electron dynamics
papers.summary: We demonstrate a spectrotemporal imaging technique that maps ultrafast electron dynamics onto energy- and angle-resolved photoelectron distributions in a single measurement. The underlying principle is to encode the probing time into the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons, while the evolving quantum dynamics is retrieved from their angular distributions. We experimentally demonstrate this concept by imaging spin-orbit wave packet dynamics in resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization of potassium atoms using two complementary approaches. In the first, three spectrally distinct probe pulses sample the dynamics at selected delays and map the corresponding wave packet configurations onto separate photoelectron energy channels. In the second, a single broadband chirped probe pulse establishes a continuous time-to-energy mapping through its time-dependent instantaneous frequency, thereby encoding the evolution of the wave packet across a broad photoelectron energy band. The resulting photoelectron momentum distribution exhibits a characteristic fork-shaped pattern. Combining supercontinuum pulse shaping with velocity map imaging, we experimentally resolve the spin-orbit dynamics over a time window exceeding 300 fs, in good agreement with quantum dynamical simulations. Our results establish spectrotemporal photoelectron imaging as a versatile approach to time-resolved spectroscopy, replacing sequential delay scans by parallel acquisition of ultrafast quantum dynamics.

authors.name: Darius K\"ohnke, Kai Ebken, Tim Bayer, Matthias Wollenhaupt

papers.title: Continuum Photonic Axion Insulators
papers.summary: Here, I study the conditions for realizing an axion topology in a homogeneous inversion-symmetric electromagnetic continuum, in the absence of a crystalline lattice. I introduce a continuum inversion invariant expressed solely in terms of the spectral properties of the material response in the zero- and infinite-wave-vector limits. Surprisingly, it is found that standard gyrotropic-type material responses are strongly constrained and, under fairly general conditions, cannot open an axion gap within first-order perturbation theory. Based on an analogy between the effective response of crystalline photonic axion insulators and the optical response of centrosymmetric altermagnets, a class of spatially dispersive odd magnetoelectric couplings that can open an axion gap is identified. These findings suggest an interesting hierarchy of nonreciprocal mechanisms in electromagnetic continua: while uniform gyrotropy relates to Chern phases, odd magnetoelectric coupling relates to axion phases.

authors.name: Mario G. Silveirinha

papers.title: A Passive Intelligent Metasurface: A Network Model
papers.summary: Intelligent metasurfaces enable advanced wave manipulation, including negative refraction, focusing, beam splitting and beam steering, with significant potential for practical applications. However, conventional approaches often rely on active metamaterials with gain, or demand computationally intensive solutions of inverse problems to find the optimal configuration. In this work, we use the scattering framework of quantum graph theory to derive an exact, analytic expression for configuration of a passive metasurface that produces a prescribed reflected wave field. The metasurface terminates a periodic lattice of waveguides and consists of an array of channels, each a tube of length $\ell_m$ ending in a vertex whose scattering parameter $\lambda_m$ sets how much of the wave is lost to the wall. For any prescribed incident and reflected field, the exact lengths and scattering parameters follow channel by channel, in closed form, from the ratio of the wave amplitudes returning to and leaving the lattice, and the metasurface is passive whenever this ratio does not exceed unity in modulus. We demonstrate the construction for both a one-dimensional and a two-dimensional metasurface. The one-dimensional metasurface terminates a two-dimensional lattice and steers, splits or perfectly absorbs Gaussian beams. The two-dimensional metasurface terminates a three-dimensional lattice and generates a prescribed image in a plane inside the lattice. In each case, we obtain the exact boundary properties that produce the effect.

authors.name: Tristan Lawrie, Gregor Tanner, Luke Bennetts

papers.title: A Study of Side Jet Interactions over a Hypersonic Cone Flow using Kinetic Methods
papers.summary: The interaction between the hypersonic flow over a cone and a side jet creates complex multiple recirculation regions as well as separation, reattachment and bow shocks known as Edney-Type IV shock-shock interactions. The interactions between these multi-scale structures are shown to be well captured with the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method, a particle-kinetic approach. This computational technique was used because even though the free stream conditions were continuum-like, sufficiently strong gradients in the shock and jet expansion were observed to cause continuum breakdown. The time-accurate DSMC approach has been shown in previous work to capture the multi-scale structures and unsteadiness in the shock structure that occurs in such flows, as was also observed in this work. These sources of unsteadiness in the shock system are shown to locally affect surface parameters such as heat transfer and skin friction as well as predict a low frequency unsteadiness consistent with earlier values in the literature.

authors.name: Irmak Taylan Karpuzcu, Deborah A. Levin

papers.title: Modeling the wall-normal velocity spectra in channel flow
papers.summary: A model is proposed for the wall-normal Reynolds stress and its one-dimensional spectrum in channel flows. The model is tested for friction Reynolds numbers from 550 to 5200. The formulation for the stress is a simple modification of the one devised for boundary layers by Kunkel & Marusic (J. Fluid Mech. 548, 2006), and holds for $y/\delta < 0.75$. The model for the spectrum holds for all wall distances. It is constructed in wavenumber space, and comprises two principal contributions to the spectrum: energy-containing motions and viscous-dominated motions. It is in accord with the attached eddy model where that applies, and the viscous contribution scales on the Kolmogorov length and velocity. Its extension to boundary layers, with no change to the constants, appears promising, including at Reynolds numbers well above those of the channel data.

authors.name: Jonathan Massey, Alexander J. Smits

papers.title: Bouncing or Merging in Drop-Bath Impacts
papers.summary: When a liquid drop impacts a liquid surface, it deforms the surface, trapping a thin layer of air between drop and bath. The drop then either bounces off the bath or, if the gas film ruptures, merges with it. We present a model for drop-bath impacts that can accurately predict whether a drop will bounce or merge, and compare it to theory-driven experiments. The model incorporates a lubrication description of the deforming trapped gas film, which accounts for its significant curvature, within a finite-element framework. Capturing this outcome requires micro- and nano-scale physics: van der Waals-driven disjoining pressure and gas-kinetic effects that depend on the mean free path of the gas. Using only independently measured material parameters, we obtain the first quantitative agreement with experiment for the critical impact speed separating bounce from merge. We explore the behaviour of drop-bath impacts at low ambient air pressure, and then investigate the bounce-merge threshold for impacts onto shallow baths and thin films, finding a bounce-merge-bounce-merge transition as the bath depth decreases.

authors.name: Peter Lewin-Jones, Daniel M. Harris, Radu Cimpeanu, Duncan A. Lockerby, James E. Sprittles

papers.title: High resolution 3D localization of ultrasound sparse sources using a SAGE algorithm
papers.summary: Reliable localization and characterization of cavitation activity are central to many ultrasound imaging and therapy monitoring applications. Passive acoustic mapping (PAM) can estimate cavitation distributions without prior assumptions but remains limited by the system point spread function. While advanced PAM methods improve spatial resolution, their performance may degrade for transient emissions with uncertain emission times. In this work, we propose a parametric source localization framework based on the Space-Alternating Generalized Expectation-Maximization (SAGE) algorithm to estimate source positions and emitted waveforms directly from array channel data. A greedy source extraction and localization procedure is first used to initialize the model order and source parameters, after which SAGE iteratively refines each source estimate. The proposed method was validated on 49 simulated acquisitions containing up to seven simultaneously emitting sources with emission time uncertainties of 12 microseconds, achieving a source localization precision of 0.24 mm (standard deviation of the total localization error). Experimental evaluation on proton-induced nanodroplet vaporization data acquired with an ultrasound matrix array demonstrated improved spatial resolution compared to a beamforming-based approach and sub-millimeter agreement between vaporization maps and the proton distribution in all three spatial dimensions. These results highlight the potential of parametric source localization for high-resolution proton therapy monitoring and provide a general framework for the localization of simultaneously emitting sparse ultrasound sources.

authors.name: Sophie V. Heymans, Fran\c{c}ois Rottenberg, Tatiana Gelvez-Barrera, Adrian Basarab, Barbara Nicolas

papers.title: Estimating Vertical Ocean Velocity from Horizontal Currents: Linear and Depth-Conditional Neural-Network Approaches on a High-Resolution Regional Ocean Model
papers.summary: The vertical component of the ocean velocity, w, is several orders of magnitude smaller than the horizontal components u and v, yet it controls vertical tracer transport, upwelling, and mixed-layer ventilation. Because w is extremely difficult to measure directly and is normally obtained only diagnostically from the continuity equation, predicting it from the horizontal velocity field is a problem of both practical and physical interest. We address this problem with two data-driven methods, a physically-motivated linear baseline and a convolutional neural network conditioned on depth through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM). Both methods are applied to a high-resolution regional simulation of the Coastal and Regional Ocean Community model over the Western Mediterranean, using a sub-region of the south-west Mediterranean Sea as a training region and two independent, out-of-sample regions for validation: the Alboran Sea, with a distinct dynamical regime driven by Atlantic inflow through the Strait of Gibraltar, and a transition region between Almer\'ia and Cartagena, between the Alboran Sea and the open western Mediterranean. Once the FiLM network is regularized enough to avoid overfitting to a single training domain, we find that its comparison with the physically interpretable linear baseline is domain- and depth-dependent rather than uniform: near the reference depth, essentially all of the achievable out-of-sample performance on both validation domains is already captured by the linear model, but at the deepest levels tested the FiLM network outperforms the linear baseline on the transition domain, whereas on Alboran it does not.

authors.name: Francesco M. Ventrella, Crist\'obal L\'opez, Emilio Hernandez-Garcia

papers.title: Orientation and slip statistics of spheroids settling in turbulence
papers.summary: Small spheroids settling through turbulence are turned broadside-on by fluid inertia and tilted away by velocity gradients. We describe their orientation and slip statistics through the crossover from random orientation to alignment, in the overdamped limit. With quasi-static Stokes drag the leading inertial torque is an exact gradient flow on the orientation sphere, its potential quadratic in the cosine of the tilt and only rescaled by mobility anisotropy. The orientation performs an overdamped random walk in a quadratic well, and isotropic Gaussian white noise gives exactly a Boltzmann distribution. For forcing of finite correlation time, a closure keeps this form with its width set by linear response; it recovers the uniform density as settling vanishes and, for fixed-orientation forcing statistics, the aligned coefficient of rapid-settling theory, and errs most in the crossover. The root-mean-square lateral slip peaks where the alignment rate approaches the Kolmogorov rate, as faster settling strengthens the sideways drift at a given tilt but suppresses the tilt; the nearly shape-independent ratio, which tensor-forced simulations reproduce, lets a measured peak constrain the torque coefficient or dissipation rate for given forcing statistics. Dissipation intermittency enters as a lognormal superposition of Boltzmann distributions, which fattens the tails but leaves the leading aligned mean-square tilt unchanged. The superposition reproduces the shape of plate orientation distributions from direct numerical simulations, where a single Boltzmann distribution fails; published moments confirm the predicted spread beyond the weakest torques, and at strong alignment the measured fourth-order tilt moment lies between the two predictions.

authors.name: Anubhab Roy

papers.title: Direct calculation of dipole moment surfaces through second-order symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties
papers.summary: Interaction-induced dipole moment surfaces are vital for calculating line intensities and collision-induced absorption coefficients for van der Waals complexes. We introduce the perturbative corrections, of second order with respect to the interaction operator, to the dipole moment (or, in general, any one-electron property) change due to noncovalent interactions. These are obtained in the spirit of the symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties (propSAPT) method, developed recently by some of us [B. Tyrcha et al., JCTC 21(9), 4562--4578 (2025)]. When orbital relaxation effects due to the external property field are properly introduced, these can be understood as analytical derivatives of the second-order SAPT interaction energies. We apply the newly introduced formalism to calculations of dipole moment surfaces for three light van der Waals complexes: He...Ar, He...H$_2$ and the H$_2$ dimer. The propSAPT method is compared against finite-field SAPT calculations and finite-field supermolecular CCSD(T) as the reference.

authors.name: Bartosz Tyrcha, Marcin Stachowiak, Konrad Patkowski, Piotr S. \.Zuchowski

papers.title: Atomic Parity Violation: Standard Model Tests
papers.summary: Atomic parity violation (APV) offers a sensitive high-precision, low-energy test of the Standard Model and a powerful probe of new physics. It played a significant role in confirming the nature of the neutral weak currents, and gives unique information about fundamental weak parameters and possible new physics, reaching energies well into the TeV scale and beyond. In this chapter, we provide a pedagogical introduction to the fascinating field of APV. The underlying mechanisms are introduced, an overview of past and ongoing experiments is presented, including prospects for measuring parity violation in molecules, and the critical role of electronic structure theory in interpreting the experiments is described. The importance of the nuclear anapole moment and other nuclear-spin-dependent parity-violating contributions for understanding nuclear structure and weak nuclear forces is highlighted. We discuss the current challenges and identify the most important and pressing goals in this field, which promises exciting discoveries in the coming years.

authors.name: Jacinda Ginges, Anastasia Borschevsky

papers.title: Quantum transport of vortex electrons in bending magnets and circular accelerators
papers.summary: Controlling the sizes and phase structure of single-particle wave packets in accelerators remains an experimental challenge and requires understanding how bending magnets transform these states. An important example is transporting relativistic vortex electrons through the magnets to a collision point while keeping a narrow orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distribution. We derive an effective Hamiltonian that accounts for the packet acceleration, employ it to obtain a generalized BMT-like equation, match the electron state at both magnet boundaries, and calculate the mean OAM and its variance. A half turn can reverse the mean OAM relative to the momentum while broadening its distribution, so recovering the mean does not ensure state recovery. We identify windows in packet sizes and bend angles for a small OAM spread and show that weak bends can produce narrow distributions with the mean OAM tilted relative to the momentum, making these states candidates for spatiotemporal vortices. For a few MeV electrons, we propose to use half-turn magnets that leave the mean OAM nearly antiparallel to the momentum while keeping its distribution narrow. For a circular orbit in a uniform field, the OAM variance after the exit grows as $N^2$ over $N$ turns, favoring linear accelerators, such as LINAC at JINR, for first experiments in MeV range.

authors.name: D. Karlovets, I. Pavlov, A. Murtazin, D. Grosman, X. Chen

papers.title: Closed analytical formulas for the Ashley-Ritchie-Brandt and Jackson-McCarthy polarization functions
papers.summary: The $Z_{1}^{3}$ correction in the Bethe-Bloch formula that quantifies the electronic stopping power of matter for heavy charged particles is revisited. This correction accounts for the Barkas-Andersen effect. Ashley, Ritchie and Brandt (ARB) wrote it in terms of a non-relativistic polarization function, and Jackson and McCarthy (JM) obtained the relativistic counterpart. Both expressions involve intricate triple integrals. The present manuscript describes how the polarization functions of JM and ARB can be reduced to compact analytical formulas. The corresponding asymptotic behaviours are also found. The accuracy of two currently-used empirical fits to the ARB and JM polarization functions is assessed.

authors.name: J. M. Fern\'andez-Varea, A. Fern\'andez-Mrosko

papers.title: Fast prediction of electron-beam parameters using transfer maps and machine learning in a digital model of a MeV $\gamma\gamma$ collider
papers.summary: Tuning the electron beam of a MeV-scale $\gamma\gamma$ collider, first in the design and later in a digital twin of the machine, requires the beam parameters at the interaction point (IP) for many injector states. Start-to-end particle tracking is too slow for this and needs the full particle distribution, which an operating machine cannot measure. We address this problem for the 200-MeV transport line of the collider with two fast predictors.
