Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.

authors.name: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie, Dakota Braaten, Matthew W. Day, Denis R. Candido, Deyu Li, Richard F. Haglund, Joshua D. Caldwell, Richarda Niemann

papers.title: Integration of Silica in G4CMP for Phonon Simulations: Framework and Tools for Material Integration
papers.summary: Superconducting detectors with sub-eV energy resolution have demonstrated success setting limits on Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) physics due to their unique sensitivity to low-energy events. G4CMP, a Geant4-based extension for condensed matter physics, provides a comprehensive toolkit for modeling phonon and charge dynamics in cryogenic materials. This paper introduces a technical formalism to support the superconducting qubit and low-threshold detector community in implementing phonon simulations in custom materials into the G4CMP. As a case study, we present the results of a detailed analysis of silica phonon transport properties relevant for simulating substrate backgrounds in Beryllium Electron capture in Superconducting Tunnel junctions (BeEST)-style experiments using G4CMP. Additionally, Python-based tools were developed to aid users in implementing their own materials and are available on the G4CMP repository.

authors.name: Caitlyn Stone-Whitehead, Israel Hernandez, Connor Bray, Allison Davenport, Spencer Fretwell, Abigail Gillespie, Joren Husic, Mingyu Li, Andrew Marino, Kyle Leach, Bismah Rizwan, Wouter Van De Pontseele, Grace Wagner

papers.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
papers.summary: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.

authors.name: Sayantan Choudhury, Swapnil Kumar Singh, Satish Kumar Sahoo

papers.title: Nonperturbative regime of low-order harmonic generation in intense low-frequency laser field
papers.summary: We find the atomic response to the intense femtosecond laser pulse via solving numerically the three-dimensional non-stationary Schr\"odinger equation (TDSE) for a model atom and calculating its dipole moment. For weak quasi-static fields, the response is well described by a perturbation approach, but for intensities higher than about $0.6 \, \, 10^{14}$ W/cm$^2$ the accuracy of this description is unsatisfactory, regardless of the order of non-linearity taken into account. We suggest fitting the numerical TDSE solution results with a Pad\'e expansion, and show that this approximation describes the response well both in the perturbative regime and beyond it for intensities approximately up to $1.4 \, \, 10^{14}$ W/cm$^2$. To consider the non-perturbative nonlinearity beyond the quasi-static limit we use the model of nonlinear oscillator with the restoring force defined by the found Pad\'e expression. Our model fails to predict the behaviour of the nonlinear refractive index in the nonperturbative domain, but it describes well the nonperturbative growth of the efficiency with the laser intensity for other nonlinear optical processes, namely, the third and fifth harmonic generation in the IR field and the optical rectification in a two-color field.

authors.name: S. A. Bondarenko, V. V. Strelkov

papers.title: Heraclitean Dialectical Concept Space
papers.summary: We introduce Heraclitean Dialectical Concept Spaces (HDCS), a topological framework for modelling stagewise structural change in systems of concepts. A stage consists of a nonempty concept set, a feasible family generating an external topology, and a neighbourhood assignment carrying additional relational structure. Neighbourhood overlap induces adjacency and channel ideals. Candidate emergence is represented by the CCER construction: an interaction profile, finite admissible cores, and anchored witnesses determine nonempty open candidate regions in uncovered remainder structure. Selected candidates may be reified as new atomic concepts at a later stage, while partial injective carry maps separately track persistence of existing identities. The resulting history space is obtained as a quotient of the disjoint union of stage spaces with the corresponding final topology. Product concept spaces extend the construction to cross-domain interaction. We derive support characterizations, mediated-interaction components, canonical CCER envelopes, monotonicity and impossibility criteria, product-space factorization, and invariance under concept-space isomorphism. Applications to monetary transformation, zero and representation, mammalian middle-ear evolution, and AI-related labour change illustrate the framework. HDCS is intended as a structural formalism rather than a causal or predictive theory of historical change.

authors.name: Volkan Yildiz

papers.title: Learning Stiff Dynamical Operators: Scaling, Fast-Slow Excitation, and Eigen-Consistent Neural Models
papers.summary: Stiff dynamical systems represent a central challenge in multi scale modeling across combustion, chemical kinetics, and nonlinear dynamical systems. Neural operator learning has recently emerged as a promising approach to approximate dynamical generators from data, yet stiffness imposes severe obstacles: training errors concentrate on slow manifold states, collapse of fast dynamics occurs, and the learned operator may fail to reproduce the true eigenstructure. We demonstrate three key advances enabling accurate learning of stiff operators and preserving spectral fidelity: (i) stiffness aware scaling of time derivatives, (ii) fast direction excitation via local trajectory cloud bursts, and (iii) autograd-based Jacobian diagnostics ensuring eigenstructure fidelity. Applied to the Davis-Skodje system, the approach recovers both slow and fast modes across stiffness regimes, reducing fast eigenvalue error by an order of magnitude while improving rollout fidelity. These results argue that spectral fidelity - not trajectory accuracy alone - should be a first-class target in data driven learning of stiff operators.

authors.name: Mauro Valorani

papers.title: Discovering Governing Spatial Interaction Equations in Dynamic Urban Systems
papers.summary: Governing equations are fundamental for describing and predicting dynamic urban geographic systems. Unlike physical systems guided by first principles, urban spatiotemporal phenomena emerge from coupled geographic processes that lack deterministic theoretical foundations, making the discovery of governing equations elusive and largely heuristic. Spatiotemporal dynamics in urban systems are often observed as sequential snapshots of spatial distribution, while the spatial interactions, or the flows, that cause such dynamics are often implied or unknown. In this study, we propose a general differential equation formalism that decomposes urban dynamics into a spatial interaction process and a self-dynamic component. Building on this formalism, we introduce the Urban Discovery Framework, which integrates hypothesis generation, neural fitting, and governing equation identification for discovering the governing equations of spatial interaction. U-Discovery leverages Large Language Models and literature-based reasoning to propose differential equation candidates. Each candidate was calibrated from the observed spatiotemporal dynamics using a neural fitting method. The candidates are evaluated and ranked based on the fitting error and mathematical complexity. Empirical experiments examine real-world active population dynamics in Hennepin County, Minnesota. Drawing on both literature-derived scientific priors and broader knowledge from LLMs, U-Discovery proposes original candidate equations and identifies those that best reproduce observed population dynamics. The discovered equations show an ability to recover the underlying mobility flows, while their varying performance across spatial scales suggests that different interaction mechanisms may dominate at different scales.

authors.name: Zhongfu Ma, Di Zhu

papers.title: Network Reconstruction via Jeffreys Prior under Missing Sufficient Statistics
papers.summary: Methods for the reconstruction of economic networks from aggregate information are important for modeling, analysis and policymaking. The traditional Fitness Model (FM) achieves good performance by using node-specific variables that are easily accessible (e.g., GDP for countries or total assets for banks or firms) and the overall link density as the only sufficient statistics. However, it often ignores additional contextual or mesoscopic features which may be more difficult to observe. Here we extend the framework by incorporating block structure as in the Fitness-Corrected Block Model (FCBM), which allows for heterogeneous densities within and across blocks, but in the deliberately more challenging setting where such block-specific densities are not empirically available. Our method uses a Jeffreys prior to provide an unbiased distribution of all compatible solutions and associated entropies, that are otherwise left unidentified, and selects a single reconstruction at the median of this entropy distribution to compensate for the missing sufficient statistics. We evaluate the procedure on nine international-trade networks using GDP as node fitness and World Bank regions as an externally specified partition. The method systematically outperforms the baseline Block-Agnostic FM (which uses the same observed network input statistic) and sometimes even the FCBM (which always uses more information). Controlled synthetic networks confirm that the median is the best of four entropy-based representatives for a range of densities and regional effects similar to the empirical ones, while other representatives can perform better when parameters are pushed far from their realistic range. Overall, our method compensates for missing sufficient statistics via a median-entropy estimate that is empirically very robust within a realistic range of parameters.

authors.name: Minh Duc Duong, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Energies and lifetimes of the 9p and 10p excited states in atomic francium
papers.summary: We present the first measurement of 9p 2P1/2,3/2 and 10p 2P1/2,3/2 excited levels absolute wavenumbers and radiative lifetime in francium. We used the Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy (CRIS) technique, applied on a beam of 221Fr atoms. Prior to this work, no experimental data existed for francium p-states with n > 8. The results provide a precision experimental test of relativistic coupled-cluster theory for the heaviest alkali, showing good agreement for lifetimes and relative excitation energies, despite a residual global offset in absolute energies.

authors.name: Pierre Lass\`egues, A. Chakraborty, R. P. de Groote, B. K. Sahoo, O. Ahmad, C. M. Fajardo-Zambrano, A. McGlone, J. Warbinek, A. Ajayakumar, M. Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, M. Au, J. Berbalk, D. Bettaney, B. van den Borne, T. E. Cocolios, M. Duggan, K. T. Flanagan, R. F. Garcia Ruiz, D. Gonzalez-Acevedo, A. Kastberg, \'A. Koszor\'us, L. Lalanne, K. M. Lynch, D. T. McElroy, G. Neyens, L. Nies, L. Quanjel, A. Raggio, J. R. Reilly, J. Snikeris, S. G. Wilkins, X. F. Yang

papers.title: A stochastic agent-based extension of the GSM$^2$ model for particle therapy: cell-cycle dynamics, dose-rate dependence, and fractionation effects
papers.summary: We present a stochastic agent-based extension of the Generalized Stochastic Microdosimetric Model (GSM$^2$) that links microscopic energy deposition by ionizing radiation to population-scale response. Each cell is represented as an agent whose DNA damage, cell-cycle phase, and fate evolve as a continuous-time Markov process. Particle arrivals, repair, misrepair, division, death, and migration are treated as competing stochastic events in an event-driven algorithm, enabling track-structure simulations of spheroids with up to $1.5\times10^5$ cells in minutes on a single workstation. For static populations, the model reproduces the Lea--Catcheside dose-rate dependence of survival for proton and carbon-ion irradiation over four orders of magnitude in dose rate. Dose-rate sparing decreases with increasing LET and disappears for low-energy carbon ions. After calibration to a single survival curve for aerobic X-ray irradiation of V79 spheroids, the model predicts without further fitting survival under anoxia and after carbon-ion irradiation in aerobic and anoxic conditions, reproducing measured oxygen enhancement ratios and relative biological effectiveness. Applied to three-dimensional tumor spheroids, the framework resolves responses to single, split, and fractionated irradiations, separates the effects of repair, reassortment, and repopulation, and quantifies stochastic variability between realizations. The model provides a mechanistic single-cell framework for studying time-dependent effects and uncertainty in particle irradiation.

authors.name: Francesco G. Cordoni, Marco Battestini, Marta Missiaggia

papers.title: Two-point enstrophy dynamics in homogeneous isotropic turbulence
papers.summary: In the present work we investigate the multiscale dynamics of enstrophy in homogeneous isotropic turbulence by exploiting the two-point formalism provided by the K\'arm\'an-Howarth-Monin-Hill approach. The study is conducted on direct numerical simulations with a Taylor-based Reynolds number in the range of $140 \lesssim Re_{\lambda} \lesssim 400$. The two-point enstrophy budget at scales $r > 10 \eta$ appears to be entirely determined by production via vortex stretching, which balances enstrophy destruction, and to be dominated by the diffusive transport at smaller scales, thus preventing the emergence of a range dominated by the inertial transport of enstrophy. The decomposition in longitudinal and transverse contributions also highlights a dual nature of the inertial enstrophy flux. In particular, enstrophy appears to be transferred across scales through a non-trivial combination of direct and reverse interscale transfer. It is shown that the dual nature of this transfer is strictly related to the vortex stretching mechanism, which, in addition to producing enstrophy through vorticity amplification, also transfers longitudinal vorticity towards larger scales (by stretching the vortical elements) and transverse vorticity towards smaller scales (by contracting these vortical elements in the radial direction). The sum of these two contributions results in an overall transfer of enstrophy from large towards small scales. We propose the use of the pressure transport term as a proxy to obtain some information on the dynamics of relevant events of inertial energy and enstrophy transport. The new findings highlight the relevance of inertial compression events in longitudinal energy transport. At the same time, a good correlation between transverse energy transport events and the radial contraction of vortical elements due to vortex stretching mechanisms is also found.

authors.name: Gabriele Boga (DIEF, University of Modena and Reggio Emilia), Carlos B. da Silva (LAETA, IDMEC, Instituto Superior T\'ecnico, Universidade de Lisboa), Sergio Chibbaro (Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, UMR 9015, LISN), Andrea Cimarelli (DIEF, University of Modena and Reggio Emilia)

papers.title: Geometry-induced self-excited dynamo in a regular tetrahedron
papers.summary: We present a rotation-free magnetohydrodynamic dynamo driven by laminar thermal convection in a regular tetrahedral cavity. The tetrahedral boundaries organize the convective flow into a robust pattern of helical convection cells without global rotation or turbulence. Direct numerical simulations demonstrate exponential amplification of a weak seed magnetic field followed by nonlinear saturation. In the reference calculation, the saturated magnetic energy exceeds the kinetic energy. The velocity field develops $D_4$ dihedral symmetry, while the self-generated magnetic field exhibits a corresponding signed $D_4$ symmetry, including antisymmetry under $\pi$ rotations about the two horizontal axes. Analysis of the velocity and magnetic-field structures reveals a closed induction cycle sustained by geometry-induced helical convection. This system provides a conceptually simple setting for isolating and understanding the fundamental physical processes underlying magnetohydrodynamic dynamo action.

authors.name: Akira Kageyama

papers.title: Finite Standard-Model Carrier from Timelike Codazzi Defects
papers.summary: The inverse problem of whether protected data carried by a local Lorentzian defect can determine a finite internal gauge-and-matter carrier before microscopic dynamics are chosen is considered. For a codimension-three timelike Codazzi defect, a marking-preserving reconstruction fixes a five-dimensional complex carrier $V=C\oplus W$ with $\dim_{\mathbb C}(C,W)=(3,2)$, the global gauge form $S(U(3)\times U(2))$, a chiral $16$-dimensional exterior packet with $k_Y=5/3$, and a norm-seven family structure. The chiral packet has the standard algebraic $SU(5)$-Spin$(10)$ envelope without assuming grand unification. Within a declared regularized-domain class, one constrained microscopic realization is constructed. Its distinguished branch ends at a single intrinsic terminal where the strict charge minimum and the first simple invariant-sector fixed-charge degeneracy coincide; soft-coupled readouts acquire a rank-one critical-response pole. On the rank-two exact-five moment stratum, four native matrix moments reconstruct a five-dimensional cyclic operator up to hidden unitary. The resulting scale-free observables lie on a one-dimensional solution manifold with a discrete conjugate orientation. With $W/Z$ used to set its longitudinal coordinate, direct CKM and reactor/solar data are consistent with the same manifold, while first-row CKM normalization remains a separate transverse structural test. Existence within the stated class is established, not uniqueness. A blind determination of the longitudinal coordinate still requires the unresolved centered-response incidence; physical transport remains an independent microscopic gate.

authors.name: Piotr Ogonowski

papers.title: A Land-Sea Contrast Pattern in Surface Temperature and Atmospheric Circulation Trends in Recent Decades
papers.summary: We argue land-sea contrast is an important driver of spatial patterns of observed surface temperature and atmospheric circulation trends, including the negative Inter-Decadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO)-like tendency across the Pacific basin. Observed and modeled trends display an overall decline in sea level pressure over the faster-warming land, with a spatial pattern that resembles the seasonal cycle and modeled response to land heating. Coupled historical forcing climate model simulations underestimate the land-sea warming ratio. It is only in the early response of abrupt CO2 quadrupling climate model simulations that climate models are able to recreate the observed land-sea warming ratio, in which case a negative IPO-like sea level pressure trend and surface warming pattern over the Pacific comparable to observed trends are seen. We propose that some discrepancies between observed trends and those predicted by climate models are explained by the underestimation of the land-sea warming ratio by climate models.

authors.name: Benjamin O. Johnson, Maria Rugenstein

papers.title: Restarts of bursts in turbulence in a log-minimal channel
papers.summary: Recent evidence on the sustainment of wall-normal-velocity bursts in wall-bounded turbulence challenges the classical streak-dependent picture, suggesting that the problem should be approached relying on no a priori knowledge regarding other flow structures. This paper discusses the restarts of bursts in a log-minimal channel within the framework of a linearised Navier-Stokes system with forcing terms encapsulating the nonlinear effects of all other structures. Two generic issues are addressed. The first concerns the conditions for burst-restart-like solutions for the forced linearised system itself. We formulate optimisation problems to understand the 'minimal requirements' for burst restarting. The solutions illustrate three conceptual periods in a typical restarting process, distinguished by the behaviour of spanwise vorticity structures: breakup, counter-rotating catch-up, and co-rotating catch-up. External forces promote this process by breaking up forward-inclined vortices and merging co-rotating, catching-up vortices. A quantity termed linearly available energy (LAE) is accordingly proposed to parameterise the restarting process. The second issue concerns the contributory features to the observed burst restarts in real turbulence. We show that an essential role of nonlinearity in restarting a burst is to increase a decaying state's LAE to a level sufficient for the onset of the subsequent burst. Flow patterns extracted during the restarting stage exhibit breakup and merging effects, both facilitated by nonlinearity. This suggests that the two effects observed in both the linearised models and real turbulence are manifestations of real flow structures that cause burst restarts.

authors.name: Zengrong Hao, Javier Jim\'enez

papers.title: Small but Tubby: A Magnetic Loop Antenna Made from 100 mm Copper Tubing
papers.summary: This paper presents the electrical model, key equations, and practical construction of a small transmitting magnetic loop antenna built from unusually large 100 mm diameter copper tubing. The large conductor surface area and wide-area transitions to the vacuum capacitors were designed to minimize resistive losses. The frequency range from 1.8 MHz to 31 MHz is unusually wide. Frequency, impedance matching, and azimuth are all adjusted automatically by servo motors. Indoor losses originate predominantly from near-field coupling to the environment rather than from the antenna itself. Temperature-rise measurements confirm that the bulk of the dissipated power is absorbed by the environment, not by the antenna components. The conducted H-field measurements demonstrate good agreement between the measured H-field and the theoretical free-space H-field calculated from the antenna geometry and an estimated loop current. The loop current was estimated from the measured antenna bandwidth and the applied transmit power. The antenna was developed for indoor operation where outdoor installation is not possible.

authors.name: Peter M\"arki, Markus Niese

papers.title: Exact Solution of the Direct and Inverse Quasi-stationary Dynamo Problem in the Expanding Plasma Ball
papers.summary: It is shown that differential equation of the quasi-stationary dynamo effect (i.e., generation of the electric fields and currents) in a uniformly-expanding plasma ball with strongly anisotropic conductivity possesses the unique mathematical property: namely, the spectrum of its eigenvalues is universal and independent of physical parameters of the medium. As a result, it becomes possible to introduce a special set of eigenfunctions - which we called the generalized spherical functions - that can be used to solve the dynamo problem in exactly the same way as ordinary spherical functions are used to solve the Laplace equation. The corresponding exact solutions should be especially valuable for treating the inverse dynamo problem, i.e., determination of the plasma parameters from the experimentally measured electric fields and currents.

authors.name: Yurii V. Dumin

papers.title: Wave collapse proliferation as a mechanism for anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity
papers.summary: Anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity are signatures of the roughness of the inviscid limit in fluid turbulence. Spontaneous stochasticity describes the selection of a probability distribution over possible solutions rather than a single deterministic trajectory. We investigate these phenomena in a nonlinear dispersive equation undergoing finite-time blowup, known as wave collapse. Collapse is arrested by two regularization mechanisms, one dissipative and one conservative. Heuristic arguments supported by numerical simulations show that an isolated collapse has a vanishing effect in the inviscid limit and cannot alone account for either phenomenon. However, simulations reveal that the number of collapse events diverges as the regularization vanishes. Their proliferation enables sustained dissipation in the dissipative case and prevents either regularization from selecting a single inviscid solution. We then introduce vanishingly small random perturbations and find numerical evidence for a well-defined statistical limit in which randomness persists. These results identify collapse proliferation as a mechanism connecting anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity in dispersive waves, allowing a formally deterministic equation to acquire a truly random limiting evolution.

authors.name: Wandrille Ruffenach

papers.title: An unstructured-grid, nonhydrostatic, GVC ocean model Part I: Model description and application of vertical hybrid coordinates to internal solitary waves
papers.summary: We present a nonhydrostatic ocean model with a horizontally unstructured, C-grid and a moving, generalized vertical coordinate (GVC) designed for the simulation of nonhydrostatic processes in realistic ocean domains. The GVC system can represent any of the well-known z-level, terrain-following, or isopycnal coordinates while also being able to employ hybrid vertical coordinates. In this paper we outline the specific steps needed to incorporate the GVC system into the unstructured, C-grid, nonhydrostatic, z-coordinate SUNTANS model of Fringer et al. (2006). The approach is adapted from the nonhydrostatic, isopycnal-coordinate method of Vitousek and Fringer (2014), yet our model differs from that implementation through the development of a conservative momentum advection scheme and a positivity-preserving layer height scheme for horizontally unstructured grids. We validate the momentum advection implementation with simulations of a turbulent channel flow and demonstrate the advantages of the hybrid vertical coordinate approach over z- or terrain-following coordinates through simulations of internal solitary waves and the associated bottom boundary layer instability.

authors.name: B. J. Pauken, L. Yue, Y. Zhang, S. Vitousek, O. B. Fringer

papers.title: Explainable AI for Geoscientific Regression: Evaluating Sensitivity and Attribution Methods with the Lorenz-63 System and Applications
papers.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) moves from research prototypes to operational tools in Earth system science, trust in its predictions becomes increasingly important. Explainable AI (XAI) offers insight into how AI models make predictions. However, many influential XAI methods were developed or popularised for classification, and their interpretation for regression, which dominates geoscience, is less well established. A central obstacle is the lack of ground truth for judging explanations. We show that, for a dynamical system with known governing equations, matched references can be built directly from the physics. We extend established sensitivity methods to provide physical references for both sensitivity and attribution, separately for methods with implicit and explicit baselines, all computed from the governing equations independently of the network. Applied to an AI emulator of the Lorenz-63 system, these references show that method families answer distinct questions rather than approximating one ``true'' explanation. The emulator's sensitivities and attributions can depart most from their physical references where it forecasts best, so predictive skill is not a substitute for the physical realism of what a model has learned. We then review XAI applications to Earth system regression, organised by method family, extending to issues an idealised system cannot address: computational scalability, strongly correlated high-dimensional predictors, and reliance on expert judgement where no physical reference exists. We also discuss how an XAI method can be mathematically valid yet only partially relevant to a given stakeholder group. We close with future directions and practical recommendations for responsible XAI use in geoscientific modelling and forecasting.

authors.name: Ieuan Higgs, Todd Jones, Kieran Hunt, Anna-Louise Ellis

papers.title: GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump
papers.summary: We implemented on GPU a mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics simulation based on a momentum-jump-free theory. The trajectory spawning that was previously implemented on CPU for sampling enhancement was eliminated to avoid the overhead of thread divergence and dynamic memory allocation on the GPU. The method was applied to a three-dimensional spin-boson model and a three-mode model of $S_2 \to S_1$ internal conversion in pyrazine involving a conical intersection. A speedup of an order of magnitude compared to the CPU computation with spawning was achieved, as well as a linear scaling with respect to the number of sampling trajectories.

authors.name: Koji Ando

papers.title: Scaling-law-informed neural point processes for earthquake sequence forecasting
papers.summary: Earthquake sequence forecasting requires models that can learn nonlinear history dependence while retaining robust statistical structure. We develop a scaling-law-informed neural marked point process, termed Fusion, that combines neural representations of catalog history with temporal features derived from the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence model and magnitude information derived from the Gutenberg--Richter law. The model separates the magnitude cutoff applied to the input catalog from the fixed target-event threshold, allowing lower-magnitude earthquakes to inform forecasts without changing the target-event set. For the 2016--2017 Amatrice--Visso--Norcia sequence, Fusion achieves the highest target-event temporal likelihood when lower-magnitude events are retained, outperforming both ETAS and a purely neural point-process baseline. Event-wise and cumulative analyses show sustained timing gains through substantial portions of the Visso and Norcia sequences. Across five benchmark catalogs, catalog-specific neural training with a fixed ETAS prior yields the highest temporal likelihood at the minimum evaluated magnitude cutoff. Magnitude likelihood shows no consistent predictive gain beyond the Gutenberg--Richter-based ETAS reference, indicating that the additional information captured by Fusion is primarily temporal. These results show that lower-magnitude catalog histories and empirical scaling-law information complement neural sequence learning for target-event timing.

authors.name: Tianlu Xiong, Zaibo Zhao, Yunrui Li, Wenqi Liu, Yosef Ashkenazy, Yongwen Zhang

papers.title: The Same and Not the Same: A Machine-Checked Genealogy of Photochemical Theory
papers.summary: Chemistry's phenomenological theories multiply with its observables: the same physical reality is repeatedly named in different measurement contexts, and the relations among theories have never had an auditable carrier. Here we present PhotoLean, a machine-checked genealogy of seventeen photochemical and photophysical theories formalized in Lean 4 over a shared kernel. Every pair of theories carries either a verified relation (equivalence, implication, composition with registered premises, definitional certificate) or a registered reason for its absence, covering all 136 pairs. Three adjudications resolve inherited conflations with if-and-only-if boundaries and witnesses: the symmetry factor $\beta$ equals one-half exactly when reactant and product force constants coincide; Kasha's rule and the Kasha-Vavilov rule agree only under closed quantification with a loss channel; and intensity-only Stern-Volmer data cannot distinguish static from dynamic quenching, whereas the lifetime channel discriminates exactly. As proposition generation shifts to machines, such machine-checked relational ledgers offer a replicable audit layer for theory itself.

authors.name: Junyi Gong, Zijie Qiu, Ben Zhong Tang

papers.title: Digitally enhanced Multi-wavelength Stabilization using a Passive Fiber Frequency Reference
papers.summary: High-stability frequency stabilization between lasers is essential for applications such as precision metrology, frequency dissemination, and quantum communications. We demonstrate the use of code-based multiplexing of a passive fiber-based interferometer for frequency stabilization and transfer between lasers separated by 85 GHz in frequency using a single shared passive reference. Out-of-loop characterization places an upper bound of sub-kHz/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ on the transferred frequency noise at Fourier frequencies above 40 mHz, with a differential fractional stability of $7\times10^{-13}$ at 1 second. We also demonstrate continuous laser tunability and characterize the residual length noise coupling. Finally, we provide a framework for scaling the architecture to higher laser counts, offering a pathway to scalable, frequency agile stabilization of multiple light sources without the overhead of an optical frequency comb.

authors.name: Hilma Karlsson, Vaishali Adya, Robert L. Ward, Chathura P. Bandutunga

papers.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
papers.summary: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

authors.name: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

papers.title: Vectorized and Symbolically Optimized Seminumerical Exchange for Large-Scale Quantum Chemistry
papers.summary: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions). For smaller molecules, comparisons are also made against the more efficient occ-RI-K method showing a break-even point around 50-100 atoms beyond which SNK dramatically outperforms due to its superior sub-quadratic (between linear and quadratic) time complexity as well as its effectively negligible memory demand.

authors.name: Jesse DiCenso, Henryk Laqua, Martin Head-Gordon

papers.title: Optical Coherent Combining in Multi-Aperture Free-Space Receivers through Atmospheric Turbulence via Optically Computed Alignment Gradients
papers.summary: Multi-aperture reception yields a coherent-combining gain only if the aperture fields are aligned in phase and polarization, which in a downlink must track the atmosphere. We show that the exact gradients of the combined power with respect to the phase and polarization angle of each branch can be measured optically, before photodetection: a passive tap of the combined field, split one-to-$N$, is the common self-reference and, interfered with a branch tap on a 3 dB coupler, yields the phase gradient; with a $90^\circ$ Faraday rotator and a static $\pi/2$ offset it yields the polarization gradient. Each branch then runs fixed-gain phase and polarization loops, without division, perturbation, dither, reference laser, or per-branch receiver, as analog integrators or a low-rate processor. We derive the gradients, their optical readout, and the loop stability condition. A phase-only simulation with identical disturbances, a common 100 MS/s clock, and retuning of every scheme compares the loop with centralized and distributed stochastic parallel gradient descent and with dither locking at the OSNR where ideal four-beam combining reaches the 28 GBd DP-QPSK FEC threshold. Up to $10^5$ rad/s of multi-tone disturbance the loop keeps the lowest residual loss, at most $5.6\times10^{-4}$ dB for four beams and 13 to 160 times below the alternatives, and reaches $90\%$ efficiency in 0.6 $\mu$s for up to 64 beams. The taps leave the receiver OSNR unchanged and every retuned scheme stays within 0.06 dB of ideal combining, whereas brief dither misalignments cost 0.14 dB. Up to $10^7$ rad/s it preserves the ideal-combining bit-error ratio for four, sixteen, and sixty-four beams while every baseline crosses the threshold and slips carrier recovery. In fades it loses $4\times10^{-3}$ dB where the others lose 0.2 to 0.9 dB. Assumptions and limitations are stated; experimental validation remains open.

authors.name: Chen Cheng (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Tong Luo (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Siyu Gong (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Qun Zhang (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Linsheng Fan (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Qi Wu (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Yanfu Yang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, China), Jiayin Xue (Pengcheng Laboratory, Shenzhen, China)

papers.title: On Algebraic Background-Independence
papers.summary: It has recently been claimed that algebraic methods can be used to give a background-independent description of semiclassical gravity. This paper aims to provide an entry point into recent algebraic approaches to quantum gravity and to analyse and critically assess the conception of background-independence here involved. We discuss an algebraic framework for formulating an algebra of observables along the worldline of an observer in a cosmological setting. By 'gravitationally dressing' the observables to the observer's worldline, the reference to the spacetime background can be set aside at the level of the abstract *-algebra. Thus this *-algebra is taken to be independent of any particular spacetime realisation, with different states on the algebra corresponding to different backgrounds. We compare this algebraic framework to three influential notions of background-independence in the literature and argue that none of these fully captures the sense in which the *-algebra is taken to be background-independent. Building on this, we extract a novel notion of algebraic background-independence tied to the representation-independence of the *-algebra. This algebraic conception motivates two further concepts of background-independence tailored to semiclassical theories: semiclassical background-independence and perturbative background-independence. We suggest that these provide useful tools for evaluating the scope and limitations of semiclassical approaches to quantum gravity.

authors.name: Luka Vinck, Sebastian De Haro

papers.title: Generative marginal learning for finite-size molecular simulation with application to stress calculation
papers.summary: We propose generative marginal learning (GML), a framework for equilibrium sampling and local observable estimation in molecular simulations. By training a conditional diffusion model on large-system simulations, GML learns the marginal distribution of a retained region, enabling configuration generation without explicitly simulating the surrounding environment or imposing periodic boundary conditions on the retained region. We derive a marginal effective potential and the associated conditional mean-force identity, which provide the basis for both denoising and force-alignment training. As an application, we estimate the spatially averaged Irving--Kirkwood stress near a vacancy defect. Numerical tests on a two-dimensional Lennard--Jones crystal and three-dimensional BCC Fe under combined tension and shear demonstrate improved local stress accuracy relative to small periodic molecular dynamics simulations.

authors.name: Zhao Ding, Cheng Yuan

papers.title: Probing Flow-Induced Chain Scission in Shear-Banding Wormlike Micelles
papers.summary: We investigate the microstructural dynamics of wormlike micellar (WLM) solutions based on CPyCl/NaSal/D\(_2\)O under shear flow using spatially resolved rheo-diffusion NMR, velocity-compensated diffusion measurements, and rheo-optical imaging in a Taylor--Couette geometry. Two viscoelastic systems were examined: a non-shear-banding WLM with a molar salt-surfactant concentration ratio of \(R=0.4\) and a shear-banding WLM with \(R=0.53\). Rheo-optical and velocity measurements confirm homogeneous flow for the non-shear-banding system and the coexistence of low- and high-shear bands within the stress-plateau regime for the shear-banding system. Despite the pronounced heterogeneity in velocity and shear rate associated with shear banding, the local surfactant self-diffusivity remains spatially uniform across the gap and throughout the stress-plateau regime. Furthermore, analysis of the mean-squared-displacement scaling reveals no measurable difference between the high- and low-shear bands. These results demonstrate that the micellar microstructure remains largely unchanged despite the formation of shear bands and provide direct experimental evidence that flow-induced micellar chain scission is not a dominant mechanism governing shear banding in this WLM system.

authors.name: Alfredo Scigliani, Samuel C. Grant, Hadi Mohammadigoushki

papers.title: Drift wave turbulence and transport analysis of hot ion L-mode plasma with fishbone instability on HL-3 tokamak
papers.summary: An integrated analysis of the HL-3 hot-ion L-mode (shot \#11972, $T_i/T_e\approx3$, $T_i(0)\approx9.8$\,keV) establishes the cross-scale coupling by which a single $m=1,n=1$ fishbone mode governs both toroidal rotation and ion-scale drift-wave turbulence. Multi-diagnostic measurements, OMFIT integrated modeling, and TGLF quasilinear simulations show that a steep fast-ion pressure gradient under 2.5\,MW co-injected NBI excites the fishbone. Its outward redistribution of resonant fast ions decouples the NBI torque, and the sawtooth crash it triggers collapses the rotation from above $100$ to $60$\,krad/s. The same fast ions that drive the fishbone also stabilize ion-scale ITG/TEM turbulence, so their redistribution removes the ITG stabilization carried by the high temperature ratio, fast-ion dilution, and $E\times B$ shear, and erodes the internal transport barrier. Two-dimensional flux and one-dimensional eigenvalue scans confirm that the high temperature ratio and the fast-ion population together suppress particle, energy, and momentum transport. These findings close one cross-scale coupling loop spanning MHD, fast-ion transport and microturbulence, in which one mode drives both momentum balance and turbulence stability. The results offer a predictive framework for fast-ion confinement and rotation sustainment in the upcoming deuterium tritium phase, and for burning plasmas where alpha particles likewise drive MHD activity and damp turbulence.

authors.name: Y. K. Shu, W. Chen, Z. J. Li, S. Xu, Y. F. Liu, B. L. Hao, Z. Wang, D. L. Yu, S. S. Yang, W. Y. Zhai, X. L. Zhu, P. W. Shi, X. L. Xu, T. Wu, Z. B. Shi, HL-3 Team

papers.title: Switching off a high-harmonic polarization channel by anti-unitary symmetry
papers.summary: We study polarization-resolved high-harmonic generation in a laser-driven two-leg Su--Schrieffer--Heeger ladder with asymmetric dimerization under periodic boundary conditions. A field linearly polarized along the ladder can generate both longitudinal and transverse radiation, whose harmonic content is controlled by lattice symmetry and electronic filling. Using symmetry analysis of the time-dependent density matrix, we show that reflection symmetry enforces odd-order harmonics in the longitudinal response and, when the transverse response is nonzero, even-order harmonics in the transverse direction. At half filling, an additional anti-unitary symmetry relating the occupied and empty bands suppresses the transverse current completely. A unitary chiral symmetry in the clean ladder relates the same bands but fails to enforce this cancellation, showing that band swapping alone is insufficient: the suppression requires both a density-matrix constraint that persists during the driven evolution and the appropriate transformation of the transverse-current operator. Moving away from half filling lifts this cancellation and allows transverse emission, while the reflection selection rule remains whenever reflection symmetry is preserved. Numerical calculations at quarter and half filling, combined with onsite potentials that selectively break the relevant symmetries, confirm these two distinct mechanisms. Thus, reflection symmetry determines which harmonic orders occur, whereas the interplay of anti-unitary symmetry and filling controls whether the transverse HHG channel is present at all.

authors.name: Milad Jangjan, Francisco Navarrete, Dieter Bauer

papers.title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
papers.summary: The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma^3, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.

authors.name: Jose L. Rivera

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flatband Superlattices
papers.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

authors.name: Amin Zamani, Lihang Feng, Jianji Liu, Ze Zheng, Gabriel Sanderson, Mohsen Rahmani, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu

papers.title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
papers.summary: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

authors.name: R Datta, C Clauser, G Hu, A Braun, N Ferraro, R Sweeney, R A Tinguely

papers.title: FA-Agent: An extensible multimodal agent framework for first-arrival picking in mountainous seismic data
papers.summary: First-arrival traveltimes underpin near-surface velocity modeling and static corrections, but in low signal-to-noise mountainous land data the first arrival is often weak, intermittent, and masked by strong direct waves and noise. Energy-based pickers then pick later arrivals or noise, and deep-learning pickers usually require retraining for a new survey. Because erroneous picks bias first-arrival tomography, many difficult zones are still inspected and corrected manually. We present FA-Agent, an agent framework for first-arrival picking built on a multimodal large language model. It combines a model that performs visual recognition and makes decisions, tools that process the data, and skills that carry experience of processing mountainous data. The framework is open and extensible: new pickers, denoising methods, and quality-control tools can be added, and new experience can be written into the skills. It is restricted neither to mountainous data nor to a particular model. Emulating a seismic data processor, the agent first surveys the whole gather to find zones needing attention, then examines them in enlarged views, and finally keeps, corrects, or removes the initial picks. On semi-synthetic gathers with known first arrivals and real mountainous noise, the agent picked the first arrival with high accuracy where it was clearly visible and removed the picks where it was invisible and could not be judged. Applied to randomly sampled gathers from a mountainous survey, it corrected picks onto weak first-arrival branches and removed picks where no first arrival could be confirmed, and it performed well on the most difficult data. Cases reviewed by experts are added to the skills automatically, so the agent improves with use, and a locally deployed model keeps confidential data on site. FA-Agent can thus become an essential component of future automated seismic data processing workflows.

authors.name: Wenda Li, Congcong Yuan

papers.title: Modeling Rainwater Harvesting Systems with Covered Storage Tank on A Smartphone
papers.summary: A model for simulating rainwater harvesting systems with a covered storage tank is described. The model is simple enough to serve as the simulation engine of a smartphone app for designing such systems. The results of the simulation can be used to find the optimum tank size and the reliability of the system in meeting a given demand. This is illustrated by using the model for designing two such systems, one in an urban environment and the other in an arid rural location. The Python scripts used for the simulations are included as ancillary material.

authors.name: Vikram Vyas

papers.title: Optimizing the statistical power of negative-partial-transpose-based entanglement tests
papers.summary: A key requirement of any separable quantum state is that its density matrix has a non-negative partial transpose. For continuous bipartite quantum states, violation of this condition may be tested via the hierarchy of negative-partial-transpose (NPT) based entanglement criteria introduced by Shchukin and Vogel [Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 230502 (2005)]. However, even for a known state, a procedure to determine the optimal NPT-based criterion within the hierarchy has, thus far, remained outstanding. Here, we introduce a theoretical framework and numerical toolbox NPyT to compare criteria performance via the statistical power of hypothesis testing for a known input state to enable the optimal entanglement criterion to be determined. Our framework takes into account environmental noise and finite number of measurements, and optimally allocates measurement resources. To demonstrate the utility of our approach, we apply our statistical framework to prominent examples of Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including the two-mode squeezed vacuum state, the quanta-subtracted two-mode squeezed vacuum state, and the two-mode Schr\"odinger-cat state. We discuss the optimal criteria identified for these states and compare them to other commonly employed criteria. For example, we identify an entanglement test for the two-mode squeezed vacuum state that has high statistical power and outperforms Simon's criterion. This work illustrates that the non-Gaussianity of the entanglement test distribution increases with test matrix size, and highlights that smaller test matrices generally provide better performance. Beyond bipartite inseparability, our framework can be extended to a wide variety of other matrix-based tests of nonclassicality and multi-mode entanglement.

authors.name: Lydia A. Kanari-Naish, Amaya Calvo-S\'anchez, Jack Clarke, Arjun Gupta, Sofia Qvarfort, Michael R. Vanner

papers.title: A General Solution for Network Models with Pairwise Edge Coupling
papers.summary: Network Models with couplings between link pairs are the simplest models for a class of networks with Higher Order interactions. In this paper we give an analytic, general solution to this family of Random Graph Models extending previous results obtained for specific interaction structures. We use the Hubbard-Stratonovich transform to show that such higher order models can be decoupled into families of effectively separable random graph models, which might be enhanced with auxiliary, possibly multi-valued, parameters identifying the thermodynamical phase of the system. Moreover, given the diagonalizability of couplings between links, we carry out the full computation of the partition functions and discuss why in some cases they can effectively reduce to the one for the Mean-Field case.

authors.name: Alessio Catanzaro, Subodh Patil, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Metastable phase separation and information retrieval in multicomponent mixtures
papers.summary: Liquid mixtures can separate into phases with distinct composition. This phenomenon has recently come back to prominence due to its role in complex biological liquids, such as the cytoplasm, which contain thousands of components. For simple two-component mixtures phase-separated states are global free energy minima. However, local free energy minima, i.e., metastable states, are known to play a dominant role in complex systems with many components. For example, Hopfield neural networks can retrieve stored information from partial cues via relaxation to metastable states. Under what conditions can phase separated states be metastable, and what are the implications for information retrieval in multicomponent liquids? In this work we develop the general thermodynamic formalism of metastable phase separation. We then apply this formalism to an illustrative toy example inspired by recent experiments, binary mixtures with high-order interactions. Finally, as core application of the formalism, we study metastability in Hopfield liquids, a class of multicomponent mixtures capable of storing information on the composition of phases. We show that these phases can be nucleated from partial cues via metastable phase separation. Spatial simulations of liquids with a large number of components match our analytical solution. Our work suggests that complex biological mixtures can retrieve information through metastable phase separation.

authors.name: Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, Pablo Sartori

papers.title: Bond-resolved STM with density-based methods
papers.summary: Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy (BRSTM) provides intramolecular contrast with CO-functionalized tips, but its interpretation requires a description of both probe relaxation and orbital-dependent tunneling. We introduce a simulation framework that combines the Full-Density-Based Model (FDBM) for CO-tip relaxation with Chen's derivative rules applied directly to real-space density-functional-theory (DFT) wave functions. We test the method against a series of constant-height BRSTM images of perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) on Ag(111), acquired in 10~pm tip-height increments, and published data for 1,5,9-trioxo-13-azatriangulene (TOAT) on Cu(111). The simulations reproduce the principal intramolecular contrast features and their evolution with tip height. The comparison identifies distinct roles for the substrate: it modifies the partially occupied molecular states and probe--sample forces in PTCDA/Ag(111), while its influence on the TOAT/Cu(111) contrast remains relevant even without substantial changes in molecular-orbital occupation. Our framework thus provides a practical and accurate route to interpreting BRSTM images that incorporates, from a single DFT calculation, the separate contributions of electronic structure and CO-tip relaxation.

authors.name: Emiliano Ventura-Macias, Jose Martinez-Castro, Guillermo Haas, Jara Trujillo-Mulero, Pablo Pou, Taner Esat, Markus Ternes, Ruslan Temirov, F. Stefan Tautz, Ruben Perez

papers.title: Statistical properties of quantum jumps between macroscopic states of light: reading an operational coherence record
papers.summary: We propose an experimental apparatus to reveal the quantum coherence manifested in downward quantum jumps of amplitude bistability. The underlying coherent superposition of macroscopic quantum states is translated into the statistical properties of the integrated charge deposited in the detector circuit of a mode-matched heterodyne/homodyne detection scheme. At first, the dynamical evolution of a signal transmitted from an auxiliary cavity is employed to pinpoint a macroscopic switching event in a bistable main cavity subject to direct photodetection. Once the decision is made on the occurrence of a downward switch, the main cavity mode is let to freely decay to the vacuum, monitored to the production of an integrated charge. In the long-time limit, the charge distribution over an identical collection of pure states generated during the jumps converges to the Q function (heterodyne detection) or marginals of the Wigner function (homodyne detection) dictated by the phase of the local oscillator. When fluctuations over the ensemble step in, we connect the statistical properties of several switching events and the ensuing production of current records, to the cavity field correlations associated with the breakdown of photon blockade.

authors.name: Th. K. Mavrogordatos

papers.title: Controlling microalgae populations by phototactic memory
papers.summary: Motile microorganisms navigate environments that vary in space and time by coupling sensory inputs to internal physiological states and active motion. In photosynthetic microorganisms, such coupling can be mediated by phototaxis, yet how temporal sensing combines with spatial variations of the environment to shape population organisation remains poorly understood. To probe this coupling, we expose populations of the phototactic microalga \textit{Chlamydomonas reinhardtii} to structured light landscapes. Under ring-shaped illumination, cells robustly accumulate at the center of the illuminated region, rather than at the light-intensity maximum. Single-cell tracking shows that cells steer relative to local intensity gradients and undergo a non-trivial phototactic response, where, on average, cells outside the ring perform positive phototaxis while cells inside perform negative phototaxis. Population experiments, numerical simulations and analytical modelling show that this trapping cannot be reproduced by an instantaneous switching rule, but requires a finite phototactic memory acting on the transition between positive and negative phototaxis. This internal timescale couples to the geometry of the light field and to the persistence of active motion, enabling controllable spatial localisation without physical confinement. Our results generically show how memory in a single-cell sensory response can control population-level organisation in a living active system.

authors.name: Gianni Jacucci, Davide Breoni, Pierre Illien, Luca Tubiana, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Allemand, Sylvain Gigan, Rapha\"el Jeanneret

papers.title: SesQ: A Surface Electrostatic Simulator for Precise Energy Participation Ratio Simulation in Superconducting Qubits
papers.summary: An accurate and efficient numerical electromagnetic model for superconducting qubits is essential for characterizing and minimizing design-dependent dielectric losses. The energy participation ratio (EPR) is the commonly adopted metric used to evaluate these losses, but its calculation presents a severe multiscale computational challenge. Conventional finite element method (FEM) requires 3D volumetric meshing, leading to prohibitive computational costs and memory requirements when attempting to capture singular electric fields at nanometer-thin material interfaces. To address this bottleneck, we propose SesQ, a surface integral equation simulator tailored for the precise simulation of the EPR. By applying discretization on 2D surfaces, deriving a semi-analytical multilayer Green's function, and employing a dedicated non-conformal boundary mesh refinement scheme, SesQ accurately resolves singular edge fields without an explosive growth in the number of unknowns. Validations with analytically solvable models demonstrate that SesQ accelerates capacitance extraction by roughly two orders of magnitude compared to commercial FEM tools. While achieving comparable accuracy for capacitance extraction, SesQ delivers superior precision for EPR calculation. Simulations of practical transmon qubits further reveal that FEM approaches tend to significantly underestimate the EPR. Finally, the high efficiency of SesQ enables rapid iteration in the layout optimization, as demonstrated by minimizing the EPR of the qubit pattern, establishing the simulator as a powerful tool for the automated design of low-loss superconducting quantum circuits.

authors.name: Ziang Wang, Shuyuan Guan, Feng Wu, Xiaohang Zhang, Qiong Li, Jianxin Chen, Xin Wan, Tian Xia, Hui-Hai Zhao

papers.title: Metastability Landscapes in Nonlinear Ghost-Normal Scalar Fields
papers.summary: We investigate finite time dynamics in nonlinear classical scalar field systems containing one ghost and one normal kinetic sector. Using a spacetime finite element formulation, we study the dependence of threshold crossing and numerical continuation times on initial amplitude, characteristic wavenumber, spectral tilt, phase structure, and spatial localization. In the quartic model, larger amplitudes generally lead to earlier growth, while higher wavenumbers and ultraviolet-biased spectra favor longer resolved bounded evolution. Smooth compact initial data exhibit a broad region with no observed growth threshold crossing over the simulated interval. A direct comparison of two Gaussian evolutions shows that enhanced low-wavenumber power can precede rapid field growth, although this observation does not establish a universal spectral-transfer mechanism. We also compare the quartic interaction with a lifted $\phi^6$ potential. The latter gives a markedly different continuation landscape, with a broad long-converged region followed by shorter accessible terminal times at larger amplitudes. Localization diagnostics do not identify a persistent oscillon core in the selected cases. By distinguishing amplitude growth, spectral reorganization, solver-limited termination, and finite-time censoring, our results characterize a nontrivial metastability landscape without implying global or quantum stability.

authors.name: Jax Wysong, Samara Overvaag, Hyun Lim, Jung-Han Kimn

papers.title: Reflective Metastructure Q-plate for Ultrashort Laser Pulses
papers.summary: The orbital angular momentum of light is an intriguing property for developing light driven applications. It emerged as an independent degree of freedom by which to manipulate light and, consequently, the interaction of light with matter. Several methods exist for the generation of light carrying orbital angular momentum, mostly employing transmitting or reflecting optical components, which radially modulate the phase profile of the light. As one of such components, transmissive q-plates established themselves as standard elements due to their usability over a broad wavelength range. Here, we present our approach to building a highly reflective q-plate with a diameter of 4.5 mm based on a plasmonic metasurface capable of converting orbital angular momentum from the nanostructure to ultrashort laser pulses without measurable temporal broadening under the investigated conditions. We highlight its working principle over a wide range of wavelengths for reflection under normal and grazing incidence.

authors.name: Christopher G. O. Wei{\ss}, Ellen Brennfleck, Bert L\"agel, Laurenz Rettig, Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann, Tobias Eul

papers.title: Localized oscillations of an Euler--Bernoulli beam with time-varying parameters on a visco-elastic foundation: asymptotics, adiabatic invariant, and equivalent Hamiltonian system
papers.summary: We consider localized oscillations of an Euler--Bernoulli beam on a visco-elastic foundation coupled to a damped discrete oscillator. All system parameters vary slowly and independently in time. For the conservative case, we employ three different analytical approaches: an asymptotic method, a technique based on the adiabatic invariance of the action of a trapped wave, and an analysis of the equivalent Hamiltonian system. All three approaches yield the identical formula for the oscillation amplitude. In the dissipative case, the oscillation amplitude is obtained solely via the asymptotic approach. Finally, we validate our analytical findings against numerical simulations, demonstrating excellent agreement.

authors.name: Ekaterina V. Shishkina, Serge N. Gavrilov, Yulia A. Mochalova

papers.title: Emergent odd response in active chiral films
papers.summary: Active chiral fluids can support an anomalous transport coefficient known as odd (or Hall) viscosity. Hydrodynamic descriptions of such fluids typically introduce odd viscosity phenomenologically. How such a response emerges from specific microscopic interactions remains incompletely understood. Here, building on classical shear rheology, we microscopically derive an odd rheological response in active chiral films: thin layers of torque-exerting, elongated particles anchored to a no-slip surface. A canonical realization of such a film is the bacterial carpet, in which flagellated bacteria are tethered head-down to a solid surface while their flagella remain free to spin and inject angular momentum into the surrounding fluid. Using a Smoluchowski kinetic theory for the orientational dynamics of these anchored particles, we derive their stress response to an imposed shear flow. We reveal that shear-induced reorientation leads to a flow-aligned polarization and a transverse surface traction from which the odd-viscosity tensor follows in closed form. This approach stands in contrast with existing microscopic theories, in which the axis of torque injection is insensitive to the flow rather than set by it. Numerical solutions of the kinetic theory further highlight saturation of the transverse traction at strong shear, driven by this orientation dynamics -- signaling departure from linear response. Our results demonstrate how odd viscosity can emerge self-consistently as a coarse-grained rheological signature of active fluid-structure interaction and establish active chiral films as a new controllable setting for odd hydrodynamics.

authors.name: Seema Chahal, Naveen Kumar D, Brato Chakrabarti

papers.title: Inclined surfaces bias bacterial swarming expansion and edge organization
papers.summary: Bacterial swarming is the collective expansion of dense populations of motile cells across hydrated soft surfaces, yet gravity is usually treated as a fixed background condition in standard horizontal assays. We used surface inclination to examine how agar-surface orientation relative to gravity affects the expansion of Enterobacter sp. SM3 swarms. At macroscopic scales, we found that colony expansion depended non-monotonically on inclination, with the strongest spreading at intermediate inclinations and weaker expansion under shallow or near-inverted conditions. Paired up-facing acute and down-facing obtuse configurations with the same tilt magnitude showed different expansion responses, suggesting that swarm expansion depended on both tilt magnitude and which side of the agar surface faced upward relative to gravity. Inclination also produced downhill-biased colony morphologies. For microscopic scales, particle image velocimetry (PIV) analysis showed generally lower mean activity under inclination than in the flat references, with a non-monotonic angular response. The downhill tip showed slower motion, shorter spatial correlations and smaller vortex cores than the upper region. To interpret the macroscopic trends, we extended a two-phase thin-film model by introducing an effective gravity coupling projected normal and tangential to the agar surface. Simulations suggest that the surface-tangential component mainly drives lateral redistribution, whereas the surface-normal component modifies film pressure and helps distinguish up-facing from down-facing configurations.

authors.name: Pengxi Gu, Zixiang Lin, Hui Ren, Jin Zhu, Anqi Li, Omar Said, Weijie Chen, Zijie Qu

papers.title: FCC-\mu e: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
papers.summary: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $\mu^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$\mu e$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$\mu e$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.

authors.name: K. Piotrzkowski

papers.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
papers.summary: Radiomic features derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are sensitive to scanners; therefore, they require harmonization across scanners. In a radiomic feature dataset, some batches may be severely underrepresented compared to the others e.g., the Erasmus Glioma Database, which may provide harmonized features biased towards the larger batches in the dataset. We investigated whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before empirical-Bayes ComBat estimation improves feature harmonization and reduces residual scanner association while retaining grade-related information. In this retrospective, the Erasmus Glioma Database included 733 eligible patients acquired at a single center across nine vendor-by-field-strength configurations. Structural MRI acquired at 1 T, 1.5 T, and 3 T; four structural MRI sequences were analyzed. From four structural MRI sequences, 428 features were computed using an IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics implementation. The sample sizes of some scanner batches were very small compared to others, which may produce unequal precision and shrinkage of batch-effect estimates. We proposed a data augmentation approach to overcome the limitation of ComBat. We provided exploratory evidence, along with confirmatory Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction to assess the proposed method. Before harmonization, 392/428 features (91.6%) differed significantly across scanner batches (median eta-squared=0.463). Standard ComBat reduced this to 13/428 (3.0%), whereas batch-augmented ComBat reduced it to 8/428 (1.9%); the median residual effect size was <0.001 for both harmonized conditions. Batch augmentation appeared to be a useful strategy to improve the performance of ComBat for feature harmonization under severe batch-size imbalance.

authors.name: Rifa Sajda Tasnim, Yushuf Sharker, Md Forhad Hossain, Rakibur Rahman, Enamul Hoque Bhuiyan

papers.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
papers.summary: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

authors.name: Laia Domingo, Daniil Tarpanov, Arsenii Senokosov, Asel Sagingalieva

papers.title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
papers.summary: Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa.
