papers.title: The retirement party of GRS 1915+105: the radio fading to quiescence of the archetypal microquasar
papers.summary: After more than 25 years of near-Eddington activity and over six years in a Compton-thick obscured phase, the black-hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 has begun to fade in the radio to a level lower than ever previously recorded, possibly marking the onset of its final descent towards quiescence. With the accretion flow hidden in the X-rays, the radio emission is currently the best tracer of the accretion activity. We aim to establish whether the fading marks the end of the outburst that began in 1992 or a temporary switch-off. We present the long-term MeerKAT monitoring of the source from the ThunderKAT and X-KAT programmes up to 2026 July, deep dual-band (L- and S-band) MeerKAT Director's Discretionary Time observations, and three Einstein Probe/FXT X-ray pointings bracketing them. Following a last Jy-level flare in early 2025, the 1.28 GHz flux density declined monotonically to $\sim$0.2-0.4 mJy by 2026 March, and after 2026 May 9 it was no longer formally detected in our 10-min monitoring observations. Deep MeerKAT observations in 2026 July detect the source at $\sim$150 $\mu$Jy in L band and $\sim$90 $\mu$Jy in S band, the lowest radio flux densities ever recorded from the system, corresponding to $L_{\rm R}\simeq2\times10^{28}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz, with a spectral index $\alpha=-0.67\pm0.41$ across 1.28-2.62 GHz. The radio decline is the first direct evidence that the central engine itself is fading rather than merely receding further behind the absorber. The steep spectrum is consistent with either a combination of optically thick and thin emission, or an unusual, intrinsically steep core-jet spectrum. Should this mark the onset of quiescence, disc-instability models predict it to last of order $10^4$ yr. The switch-off of the central engine may shed light on the nature of the donor star and on the origin of the very-high-energy gamma-ray emission in this system.

papers.title: DOWSING, Dust Observations With SCUBA-2 In Nearby Galaxies: I. Dust in M81
papers.summary: We present a resolved far-infrared/sub-millimetre study of dust in the nearby spiral galaxy M81 using Herschel PACS/SPIRE and JCMT SCUBA-2 observations from 70 to $850\,\mu\mathrm{m}$. We model the dust emission using both single-temperature modified blackbody (SMBB) fits and point process mapping (PPMAP), comparing pixel-by-pixel SED-fitting with image cubes of dust surface density as a function of position and temperature. For fixed $\beta = 1.9$ and a dust opacity of $\kappa_{350\,\mu\mathrm{m}} = 1.92\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$, SMBB gives an integrated dust mass of $(1.77 \pm 0.09) \times 10^{7}\,M_\odot$, while PPMAP gives $(2.65 \pm 0.13) \times10^{7}\,M_\odot$. The higher PPMAP mass is expected because real lines of sight contain dust over a range of temperatures, whereas SMBB assumes a single effective temperature and can underestimate the dust mass. Both methods show enhanced dust surface densities along the spiral arms and a radially declining dust temperature, with the warmest dust in the central region. Variable-$\beta$ fits indicate only moderate spatial variation in $\beta$ for well-constrained pixels, but the strong $T$-$\beta$ degeneracy motivates a fixed emissivity index for the main analysis. Combining the dust maps with HI data, we find a positive radial gas-to-dust ratio gradient, with $d\log_{10}(\mathrm{GDR})/dR = 0.065\,\mathrm{dex}\,\mathrm{kpc}^{-1}$. Comparison with M81's metallicity gradient implies a declining dust-to-metals ratio, potentially consistent with more efficient grain growth in the inner disc. The star formation rate is modest, $\sim 0.27\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, and is strongly concentrated along the spiral arms. These results suggest that the dust, gas, and star-forming structures of M81 are strongly shaped by its spiral arms, while the central region hosts the warmest dust in the disc.

papers.title: The HST-Hyperion Survey: X-ray AGN Enhancement in the Hyperion Proto-supercluster
papers.summary: Dense environments can influence both galaxy evolution and supermassive black hole growth, but whether they enhance or suppress (or both) active galactic nuclei (AGN) activity at high redshift ($z\gtrsim2$) remains uncertain. As one of the most massive structures identified in the early universe, the Hyperion proto-supercluster at $z\approx2.5$ provides a unique opportunity to investigate this connection during an epoch near the peak of both cosmic star formation rate and AGN activity density. To examine the impact of galaxy environment on AGN activity, we measure the fraction of X-ray-selected AGN in Hyperion as a whole, its highly overdense peaks, and its outskirts, comparing these measurements to a coeval field sample. We identify X-ray AGN using the deep Chandra COSMOS-Legacy Survey and combine optical/near-infrared (NIR) photometry and photometric redshift information from COSMOS2020 with extensive ground-based spectroscopy and HST-grism observations. Redshift information is incorporated statistically using a Monte Carlo framework. We find a higher X-ray AGN fraction in Hyperion ($7.4^{+3.2}_{-1.8}\%$) than in the coeval field ($3.2^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\%$), corresponding to a $\sim2.3\sigma$ difference. Strikingly, this enhancement is concentrated in the overdense peaks, where the X-ray AGN fraction reaches $12.3^{+5.5}_{-3.4}\%$ ($15.0^{+6.9}_{-4.4}\%$ in the most massive peaks versus $6.2^{+11.9}_{-2.1}\%$ in the less massive peaks), while the lower-density Hyperion outskirts ($2.1^{+3.6}_{-1.1}\%$) show no evidence of enhancement relative to the field. These results add to the limited but growing evidence for enhanced AGN activity in high-redshift protostructures, suggesting that the dense environments at these epochs may preferentially trigger AGN during the early stages of cluster assembly.

papers.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: The Tully-Fisher Relation at $z = 4-6$
papers.summary: The Tully-Fisher relation provides a fundamental link between galaxy mass and their kinematics. Although its evolution is relatively well constrained up to cosmic noon, observational probes at higher redshifts remain scarce. In this work, we investigate the stellar and baryonic Tully-Fisher relations (TFRs) at $z=4-6$ by analyzing JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of 18 main-sequence star-forming galaxies belonging to the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey. We apply a morpho-kinematic disk classification scheme, finding five disk-like galaxies and a survey disk fraction of $0.28\pm0.11$. These disk galaxies span stellar masses of $10^{9.5-10.5}\,M_\odot$, intrinsic rotational velocities of $91-127\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and intrinsic velocity dispersions of $66-129\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. For both versions of the TFR, we find that the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST disks lie below the local relations and are likely offset from those reported at cosmic noon ($z\approx2.3$). By fixing the TFR slope to the $z=0$ value, we measure zero-point offsets for the stellar-mass TFR of $-0.96\pm0.18$ dex and $-0.50\pm0.18$ dex relative to the local Universe and cosmic noon, respectively. For the baryonic TFR, we find zero-point offsets of $-0.57\pm0.20$ dex and $-0.30\pm0.20$ dex with respect to the local Universe and cosmic noon relations. Our measurements are consistent with the redshift evolution of the zero-points of both TFRs being driven by the evolution of dark matter halo properties with cosmic time, modulated by a reduced contribution of dark matter to the dynamical mass on the galaxy scale.

papers.title: On the importance of medium-resolution continuum spectroscopy for JWST's extragalactic legacy
papers.summary: We argue for a significant investment of JWST time into an extremely deep medium-resolution NIRSpec MSA survey targeting a large, representative sample of high-redshift $(z>1.5)$ galaxies, specifically intended to obtain high-SNR continuum detections. This is only possible with JWST, and no planned future instrumentation has similar capabilities, meaning that obtaining such observations with JWST must be urgently prioritised. The vast majority of existing archival NIRSpec observations are not deep enough for continuum science, being focused on the detection of emission lines. Deeper continuum data opens up the ability to constrain a much wider range of key galaxy physical parameters, including stellar population ages and metallicities, stellar kinematics and neutral gas physical properties, inflows and outflows. Such measurements will provide crucial insight into quenching physics, galaxy dynamical masses, merger histories, pristine early star-formation, reionization and the physics of Little Red Dots, as well as enabling all of the emission-line science that can be achieved with shallower observations. To facilitate future survey planning, we present an empirically derived relationship between rest-optical continuum SNR in JWST NIRSpec medium-resolution data, rest-optical apparent magnitude and exposure time, which we show to be independent of redshift (and hence the grating used). We then provide a 1000-hour sketch survey plan based on achieving the continuum SNR $=20$/pixel necessary to constrain key physical properties and scaling relations for a large galaxy sample at $z>1.5$. We finally discuss NIRSpec sky subtraction strategies, which are of critical importance for continuum SNR.

papers.title: Detection of Differential Chromatic Refraction with LSST Camera data
papers.summary: The Earth's atmosphere acts like a prism, deflecting blue light towards the zenith more than red light. Airmass-dependent changes in astrometry can therefore be used to infer additional information about the wavelength distribution of light within a photometric passband. The Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will observe each point in the southern sky several hundred times, with observations spread across a range of airmasses. Using commissioning data from the LSST camera released in LSST Data Preview 2, we report the detection of this differential chromatic refraction (DCR) effect in observations of galaxies and quasars in the COSMOS field. We show how information from DCR can complement the six-band colour information from LSST and help break degeneracies when selecting extragalactic samples and estimating their photometric redshifts. DCR will be a valuable resource for scientific studies and care should be taken not to remove useful DCR information from future LSST data releases.

authors.name: Matthew J. Temple, Phoebe N. Lister

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Coupling Photoionization & Multi-Frequency Radiation Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: We use machine learning (ML) to couple photoionization microphysics to radiation hydrodynamic simulations of line-driven winds. ML models are trained on outputs from the photoionization code XSTAR to predict the line-driving force multiplier as a function of gas ionization, optical depth, and the blackbody temperature of the irradiating spectral energy distribution (SED). We implement the trained models within Athena++, enabling rapid runtime evaluation of the radiative acceleration without directly solving the photoionization problem during the hydrodynamic evolution. We find that random forest models provide the highest accuracy and reproduce the force multipliers over a three-dimensional parameter space more accurately, and with less training data, than traditional precomputed tables using trilinear interpolation. Because the framework treats the force multiplier as a function of the evolving local SED, it can be generalized to more complex radiation fields and arbitrary spectral shapes. More broadly, this work demonstrates how ML can serve as a computational framework for embedding expensive microphysical calculations within large-scale dynamical simulations.

authors.name: Sergei Dyda, Randall C. Dannen

papers.title: MapHub: Daily Relevance Heatmaps of New arXiv Preprints for a Research Community
papers.summary: MapHub, the MIDAS arXiv Preprint Hub, assesses each day's new arXiv submissions for every participant in a research community, with a large language model reading each paper against portfolios built for the participants. It publishes the relevance scores, from 0 to 100, as a heatmap that shows whose work each paper touches. In the authors' blind ratings, the top 10\% of papers by MapHub's scores held about 70\% of the raters' own top 5\%, pooled, against about a third for a text-matching baseline. About 6\% of a day's astro-ph papers reach 30 for each participant, and one every three days reaches 60. MapHub runs on a standard Claude subscription and is designed to be useful for any field: https://github.com/kailicao/maphub-public.

authors.name: Kaili Cao, Camille Avestruz, Feige Wang

papers.title: Systematic Study of Cosmic Rays in Star-Forming and Starburst Galaxies using Fermi-LAT and Multiwavelength Data
papers.summary: The majority of $\gamma$ rays from star-forming galaxies (SFGs) and starburst galaxies (SBGs) are expected to originate from interactions between high-energy cosmic rays (CRs) and the interstellar medium, making $\gamma$-ray observations a powerful tool for probing CR populations and interstellar environments. Using 15 years of Fermi-LAT data, we conducted a systematic study of seven sources. The $\gamma$-ray spectra of the bright SBGs M82 and NGC~253 exhibit a decrease in energy flux below a few hundred MeV, suggesting a substantially smaller contribution from CR electrons than previously inferred. Detailed fits of the spectral energy distribution, which combine our GeV $\gamma$-ray measurements with reported radio and TeV $\gamma$-ray results, indicate that the electron-to-proton ratios in M82 and NGC~253 are comparable to that of the Milky Way. In contrast, energy densities of CRs in these two SBGs are 2.5--8 times lower than that of the magnetic field, unlike the Milky Way. For the nearby Local Group galaxy M31, we decomposed the $\gamma$-ray emission into two components, revealing a central source with a soft spectrum and a compact size of less than 0.33 degree, which indicates a considerable contribution from unresolved sources. Our new analysis also reduces the $\gamma$-ray fluxes of several SBGs, bringing all SBG sample members to levels comparable to or below the calorimetric limit, with calorimetric efficiencies ranging from 0.33 to 1.20. In contrast, all SFG sample members exhibit low efficiencies at the 10\% level. We developed a theoretical model of interstellar $\gamma$-ray emission that successfully reproduces the observed calorimetric efficiencies, providing a robust framework for interpreting and predicting $\gamma$-ray emission from SFGs and SBGs.

authors.name: Hinako Ochi, Tsunefumi Mizuno, Yasushi Fukazawa, Noemi Barnier, Susumu Inoue, Wataru Iwakiri, Junling Chen, Tomonori Totani

papers.title: CosmicGrain: An On-the-fly Dust Physics Module
papers.summary: We present CosmicGrain, a dust physics module built on Gadget-4 that models explicit dust superparticles that experience resolved gas-dust drag and radiation pressure, undergo collisional heating and cooling with gas, and are further shaped by subgrid treatments for grain growth, thermal sputtering, coagulation, shattering, supernova shock destruction, and astration. We run an eleven-rung physics ladder (S0-S10) at 1024^3 resolution to isolate the contribution of individual processes to a Milky Way-mass halo's dust population. Because dust is evolved as active on-the-fly particles, individual grains retain distinct histories producing results inaccessible to passive dust models such as the strongly asymmetric silicate-to-carbon shattering destruction ratio driven by silicate grains' smaller birth size. Gas-dust drag is the dominant driver of ISM dust enrichment, increasing dust levels by ~100 times while every other process changes the R200 dust abundance by only 10-30%. We find reasonable agreement with the Milky Way's radial dust-to-gas and dust-to-metal ratios, with carbon dust preferentially enriching the CGM relative to silicates. The code is freely available at https://cosmicgrain.space.

authors.name: E. Huscher, K. Finlator

papers.title: GetGaia 2.0: automatic membership and systemic motions of stellar systems with Gaia
papers.summary: We present GetGaia 2.0, a public Python package that retrieves the Gaia data around a stellar system and selects its member stars automatically. The membership is a probabilistic model fitted by expectation maximization that combines the astrometry of every source, with its full covariance, the color-magnitude diagram, the sky distribution and, when available, the line-of-sight velocities, from Gaia or from an external catalog. The local systematic errors of the Gaia reference frame are measured on the quasars of each field. The code returns the systemic proper motion (PM) and parallax with their full covariance, a detection significance, a contamination estimate and the structural parameters of the system. We validate it on synthetic catalogs, where it recovers the members with 90-100 percent purity, and run it on Gaia DR3 for the known dwarf galaxies of the Local Group within 850 kpc and for 95 Galactic globular clusters, in tiers that add one piece of literature information at a time. It measures the systemic PMs of 55 dwarf galaxies and 93 globular clusters at a significance of at least $3\sigma$; 29 of the dwarfs and 86 of the clusters are recovered from their position alone. The dwarfs include every Milky Way satellite within 300 kpc brighter than $M_V=-5.4$, ultra-faint systems down to $M_V=-0.8$, and nine galaxies at 370-820 kpc. The PMs agree with the published values within 0.1 mas/yr for 47 of the dwarfs and for all the clusters (median differences of 0.032 and 0.009 mas/yr), with uncertainties equal to those of dedicated studies, and none deviates by more than $3\sigma$. The Gaia line-of-sight velocities alone give the systemic velocity of 71 clusters, within 1 km/s of spectroscopy. GetGaia 2.0 delivers, without manual intervention, the systemic motions and the members of the stellar systems within the reach of Gaia, and is ready for the forthcoming Gaia data releases.

authors.name: Andr\'es del Pino

papers.title: Dust Survival in Lensed Quiescent Galaxies at $z>1$ Depends on How They Quench
papers.summary: The interstellar medium of massive quiescent galaxies holds key clues to how they quench, yet remain poorly understood. Although dust is expected to be depleted rapidly ($\lesssim$100 Myr) after quenching, some quiescent galaxies host substantial dust reservoirs, raising the question of whether dust survives quenching or is replenished afterward. We present ALMA Band 6 continuum observations ($\lambda_{\mathrm{rest}}$$>$250$\mu$m) of eight strongly-lensed, spectroscopically-selected quiescent galaxies at z$\sim$1-2.5 from the COOL-LAMPS and REQUIEM surveys, plus five archival REQUIEM systems. The sample spans more than two orders of magnitude in dust-to-stellar-mass ratio ($f_{\mathrm{dust}}10^{-3}$), and two galaxies host extended, resolved dust. Comparing $f_{\mathrm{dust}}$ with time since quenching, roughly half the sample, preferentially at higher redshift, is consistent with rapid quenching and harsh dust destruction, while lower-redshift, more slowly quenched systems are consistent with milder destruction, possibly reflecting an evolving dominant quenching mode. The two most dust-rich galaxies exceed even the mildest model destruction tracks, with J1201-3952 retaining the highest $f_{\mathrm{dust}}$ $\sim$1.8 Gyr after quenching. If these systems are truly quiescent, their dust masses approach maximum stellar yields, pointing to ISM grain regrowth and/or TP-AGB dust production. However due to our single-band continuum data, $f_{\mathrm{dust}}$ is uncertain ($\pm$0.3 dex systematic uncertainty from the unknown dust temperature) and we cannot rule out obscured star formation in these two galaxies. Our results suggest that dust survival depends on how galaxies quench: rapid, harsh quenching efficiently destroys dust, while slower, milder quenching can leave dust reservoirs that persist or are replenished long after star formation ceases.

authors.name: Sarah Bodansky, Katherine E. Whitaker, Gourav Khullar, Michael D. Gladders, Keren Sharon, Viraj Manwadkar, Yunchong Zhang, Jacqueline Antwi-Danso, Dylan Berry, Rachel Bezanson, H\r{a}kon Dahle, Carlos Garcia Diaz, Darko Donevski, Alex J. Geiger, Massissilia L. Hamadouche, Joel Leja, Guillaume Mahler, Alexandra Pope, Justin Spilker, Ezra Sukay, Francesco Valentino

papers.title: Coordinated Space and Ground Monitoring of Accretion Bursts in a Protoplanetary Disk: MIRI and iSHELL observe the long-term modulation of gas within a small inner disk cavity
papers.summary: DQ Tau is a TTauri eccentric binary with pulsed accretion bursts regulated by its $\sim 16$-day orbital period. We have monitored this system with seven instruments from ground and space over 40 days. We present results on molecular gas variability from nine JWST-MIRI and nine IRTF-iSHELL epochs over three sequential accretion bursts with accretion luminosity pulses increasing by factors of $\sim 9$-80. A fundamental new measurement from this analysis is the line broadening of CO (from iSHELL) and H$_2$O (from MIRI) lines, which we use to estimate Keplerian radii and their variability in parallel to the line luminosity. This unprecedented dataset clearly shows that the molecular emission does not react like HI and the 5-$\mu$m continuum with each accretion burst: the line luminosity and width of all hot molecular gas tracers decrease over $\sim30$-35 days, consistent with an emitting region decreasing in temperature and mass as it recedes to larger radii within the $\sim 0.2$-0.4 au inner cavity perturbed by the binary. The infrared molecular spectrum of DQ Tau is affected more by disk dynamics then by chemical changes triggered by variable accretion, supporting model expectations for chemical relaxation timescales that are much longer than the duration of these accretion bursts ($\gg 10$ days). The variability observed in all tracers in this study is consistent with a scenario where gas mass builds up near the disk edge to modulate the burst peak intensity and gas density in the inner cavity every $\sim4$-5 orbital periods. The origin of this modulation is still unclear.

authors.name: Jacob Hyden, Andrea Banzatti, Benjamin M. Tofflemire, Sebastiaan Krijt, Till Kaeufer, Klaus M. Pontoppidan, Carlo F. Manara, Christian Rab, John M. McCaskill, Guillaume Bourdarot, Emma T. Whelan, Joan Najita, Adrien Houge, Adwin Boogert, Catherine Dougados, Myriam Benisty, James Muzerolle Page

papers.title: The 10 Mpc Volume
papers.summary: Accurate distances are now known for most unobscured galaxies brighter than MB = -13 mag within 10 Mpc from Hubble Space Telescope observations of their luminous stars. Complementary mid-infrared observations with the Wide-field Infrared Explorer provide global stellar mass estimates for these galaxies. Consequences are detailed knowledge of the properties of the Universe in a volume-limited space. Galaxies tend to lie within groups, within filaments. The filaments experience bulk motions in response to well defined gravitational attractors such as the Virgo Cluster and repulsors such as the Local Void. The groups are inevitably dominated by a single galaxy, with 10 galaxies between one and nine Mpc containing most of the stellar mass within the sample. There is a curious lack of galaxies in an interval fainter than these dominant galaxies. The dominant galaxies in halos tend to have gas reservoirs and ongoing star formation, a property extending to dwarf galaxies in separate halos. Secondary galaxies in halos are frequently gas depleted and lack evidence of star formation. With one notable exception, all galaxies in the complete sample have well formed red giant branches indicative of early-onset star formation.

authors.name: R. Brent Tully, Gagandeep S. Anand, Helene M. Courtois, Igor D. Karachentsev, Valentina E. Karachentseva, Ehsan Kourkchi, Dmitry I. Makarov, Lidia N. Makarova, Daniel Pomarede, Edward J Shaya

papers.title: Using Structure Functions to Characterize Protoplanetary Disk Velocity Residuals
papers.summary: Protoplanetary disks, the birthplace of planetary systems, are highly dynamic environments. High angular and spectral resolution observations have revealed non-Keplerian motions in nearly every source studied, indicative of (magneto-)hydrodynamical instabilities or planet-disk interactions. However, these velocity perturbations rarely exhibit ordered structure, limiting our ability to attribute them to a specific mechanism. We propose the second-order structure function as a tool for recovering structural properties of velocity perturbations in the presence of significant noise. Using morphological models, we demonstrate how easy-to-calculate heuristics and parametric model fits together identify structure in noisy data and recover its properties, including correlation lengths, their radial scaling where genuinely present, and the anisotropy. We further outline a workflow to de-noise the data and to build a matched null model against which inferences are compared. Applying the framework to one numerical simulation each of the gravitational, magneto-rotational and vertical-shear instabilities, we recover their structure at high significance and the structural heuristics separate all three pairs, with the gravitational and vertical-shear instability simulations remaining the hardest to distinguish once observationally degraded. As a demonstration on real data, 12CO observations of TW Hya reveal azimuthally elongated velocity structure that persists once the large-scale m=1 component is removed. We also delineate where a Gaussian description breaks down for coherent features such as spiral arms, and how inclination affects the recovered heuristics. The methodology is implemented in the eddy package and provides a foundation for statistically characterizing turbulent velocity structure in high-resolution disk observations.

authors.name: Richard Teague, Sean M. Andrews, Jaehan Bae, Marcelo Barraza-Alfaro, Abigail Bodner, Jonathan D. Henshaw, Giovanni Rosotti

papers.title: Double Neutron Star Mergers and Fast Blue Optical Transients: A Circumbinary Disk Connection
papers.summary: Post-common-envelope evolution (CEE) circumbinary disks (CBDs) form when part of the ejected envelope remains bound and circularizes around the stripped core and its companion. Leveraging results of scale-free hydrodynamical simulations, we develop a framework to model the effect of such disks on subsequent binary evolution, and implement it in the population synthesis code COMPAS. Applying our framework to double neutron star (DNS) merger progenitors, we find that CBDs generally induce substantial orbital shrinkage, changing the merging DNS population and lowering the overall merger rate. We explore an extensive grid of binary-evolution and disk models, and find that CBD interactions reduce the DNS merger rate by up to $28\%$, primarily through 'premature' mergers between the neutron star (NS) and the giant's core. These mergers may power luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), occurring at a fiducial rate of $\simeq11 \:\rm Gpc^{-3} \rm yr^{-1}$. Our results indicate that natal kicks contribute little to LFBOT offsets, and that they should be associated with young stellar populations, though not necessarily active star-forming regions. Since LFBOT progenitors would otherwise produce short-delay DNS mergers, CBDs further challenge DNS mergers as the source of early r-process enrichment. For surviving DNS mergers, accretion from the disk leads to higher chirp masses, potentially explaining the puzzling mass of GW190425. Our framework provides a general tool for studying CBD-binary interactions in post-CEE systems.

authors.name: Aldana Grichener, Ruggero Valli, Mathieu Renzo, Ilya Mandel, Kaitlin M. Kratter, Magdalena Siwek, Koushik Sen, Neev Shah

papers.title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
papers.summary: We develop an algebraic classification of canonical single-field inflationary dynamics using an exact depressed cubic equation for the inflaton velocity. Its root structure identifies a branch-swap boundary distinct from the limiting boundary of downhill motion, where ultra-slow-roll inflation naturally emerges. Independently, the conservation of momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation in the long-wavelength limit provides a criterion for the growth or decay of the gauge-invariant difference between comoving and uniform-density curvature perturbations. Combining these criteria, we construct a unified dynamical chart in terms of the Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, illustrating its applicability to constant-roll inflation and simple toy models. Our classification shifts the emphasis from assigning models to fixed categories toward understanding the dynamical regimes traversed by inflationary trajectories and their implications for primordial perturbations.

authors.name: Jinn-Ouk Gong, Wei-Chen Lin

papers.title: Magnetic contribution to outer-disk rotation in the spiral galaxy NGC 5055
papers.summary: We test whether fields of galactic strength enhance NGC~5055's outer gas rotation. Finite analytic disk decompositions yield consistent rotation--density pairs and a blended gravitational reference approximately retaining inner rotation while its density approaches the measured outer HI+He profile. This reference is modelled, not an independently measured stellar curve. Its difference from fitted gas rotation gives the required purely toroidal field for circular, axisymmetric midplane motion. The prescribed field strength at the reconstruction's inner radial boundary is $B_s$. With hydrogen inertia, no pressure and $B_s=0$, constant exponential heights of 1~kpc and 250~pc give approximate peaks of 5.47 and 10.95~$\mu$G near 34.9~kpc; 0.2~kpc gives approximately 12.24~$\mu$G. Extrapolated flaring exponential and Gaussian profiles peak at approximately 5.25 and 5.96~$\mu$G, respectively, near 33.8~kpc. For $B_s=$8~$\mu$G, their fields decline overall to approximately 5.73 and 6.30~$\mu$G near 39.7~kpc. These estimates are conditional on the gravitational reference, vertical structure and prescribed boundary field. Comparison with total radio fields supports the field scale without establishing a magnetic origin for the rotation excess.

authors.name: Natalia Wo\'zniak, Joanna Ja{\l}ocha, {\L}ukasz Bratek, Szymon Sikora

papers.title: The Milky Way-like radial structure in nearby galaxies
papers.summary: The Milky Way exhibits a distinctive plateau in its inner surface brightness profile around one effective radius, challenging the traditional view of a purely exponential disk. To explore the origin of this feature, we identify 65 nearby galaxies ($<50$ Mpc) with similar plateau structures and analyze their multi-band surface brightness and color profiles using SDSS, DESI, 2MASS, and Mephisto data. Of the 65 galaxies with Milky Way-like plateaus, 42 have bar classifications (25 barred, 17 non-barred). Barred galaxies show radial color variations more consistent with stellar population ageing, while non-barred galaxies align more with the dust reddening direction, suggesting dust attenuation contributes to plateau formation in non-barred systems. The broad range of color gradients among barred galaxies suggests bars influence plateaus through multiple pathways, including stellar population variations and dynamical stellar-mass redistribution. Environment may also contribute: both barred and non-barred galaxies tend to reside in denser environments than a comparison sample without plateaus. The low occurrence rate ($\sim$3.6\%) may indicate that plateau structures mark a relatively uncommon evolutionary stage. The Milky Way, with both strong stellar population dependence and a persistent stellar mass profile feature, may represent an intermediate case where both stellar population variations and dynamical processes associated with the bar shape its plateau.

authors.name: Yuze Zhao, Jianhui Lian, Zheng Zheng, Cuihuan Li, Jie Song, Tao Wang, Zhenkang Tang, Dezi Liu, Xiangkun Liu, Yuan Fang, Guowang Du, Jinghua Zhang, Xufeng Zhu, Xiaowei Liu, Xinlei Chen, Yu Pan, Xingzhu Zou, Ye-Hao Cheng, Shuai Xie

papers.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
papers.summary: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe, as well as their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieve phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conduct a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters with broadly improved precision, some reported for the first time. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351 and J2043+1711, we determine their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and infer their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examine the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819 and J1741+1351, and estimate their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125-2327 and J1741+1351, we detect the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allows us to derive a strongly favored, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125-2327, and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we use the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar-timing-array analyses in the future.

authors.name: K. Liu, A. Chalumeau, H. Hu, S. Chen, L. Guillemot, J. Jang, M. Keith, J. Antoniadis, C. Bassa, A. Carleo, D. J. Champion, I. Cognard, G. H. Janssen, W. Jiang, R. Karuppusamy, E. F. Keane, M. Kramer, Y. Liu, M. B. Mickaliger, A. Parthasarathy, D. Perrodin, B. W. Stappers, G. Theureau, L. Wang

papers.title: Is Morphology All You Need? Quantifying Imprints of Past Star Formation in the Present-Day Morphologies of Galaxies
papers.summary: The next generation of galaxy surveys will bring a plethora of new observations, a vast majority of which will be observed with a few photometric broadbands, limiting the information we can infer from traditional SED fitting methods. To maximize the scientific value of these surveys, techniques that can go beyond traditional summary statistics in extracting information from galaxy observations are needed. Moving beyond integrated photometry, we introduce the Katachi-PRIME method to do spectral energy distribution (SED) based inference that jointly incorporates morphological and SED information. Katachi-PRIME uses implicit likelihood inference (ILI) to incorporate realistic morphological priors from gri broadband images, to make predictions of: stellar mass (M$_*$), specific star formation rate (sSFR), redshift (z), age (t$_{50}$), dust attenuation (Av), and gas-phase metallicity (12+log(O/H)) of the galaxy. We find that this improves constraints compared to traditional 5-band photometry. We then use the learned morphological priors to examine the extent to which morphology encodes information about past star formation, finding a stark dichotomy in how morphology encodes star formation history. While the stable morphologies of main-sequence and quiescent galaxies can predict past star formation out to $\sim 4-7$ Gyr and $\sim3-5$ Gyr, respectively, starburst and green-valley populations above and below the main sequence tend to experience structural disruptions that obscure all but the most recent star formation activity. Methods like Katachi-PRIME maximize the scientific value of future telescopes by providing broad-baseline SED-level property estimates by incorporating morphological information.

authors.name: Juan Pablo Alfonzo, Kartheik G. Iyer, Masayuki Akiyama, Camilla Pacifici, Abdurro'uf, Suchetha Cooray, Novan Saputra Haryana, Marc Huertas-Company, Christopher C. Lovell, Rachel Somerville, Joshua S. Speagle, John F. Wu, Mikaeel Yunus

papers.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
papers.summary: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band~6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.

authors.name: Yuto Hiraide, Mastaka Aizawa, Munetake Momose

papers.title: Prospects for detecting hot-Jupiter tidal decay through transit timing with the mission Earth 2.0
papers.summary: Orbital decay of hot Jupiters provides a unique opportunity to probe tidal dissipation in star-planet systems. However, despite extensive observational efforts, only one hot Jupiter, namely WASP-12b, currently exhibits conclusive observational evidence for orbital decay. Expanding this sample is therefore crucial for establishing a statistical understanding of tidal interactions in planetary systems. Long-term transit timing variations (TTVs) provide a direct observational probe of orbital decay induced by tidal dissipation between a hot Jupiter and its host star. The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission will revisit the original Kepler field, delivering high-precision transit timing measurements and extending the observational baseline to approximately 24 years (2009--2033). In this work, we aim to assess the capability of ET to detect orbital decay in hot Jupiters previously observed by Kepler. We generate four years of simulated ET light curves based on the expected photometric precision and observing cadence of the mission and analyze them jointly with archival Kepler and TESS observations. Using these combined datasets, we perform long-term TTV analyses and predict the achievable precision for measuring orbital period variations. We find that ET can substantially improve the precision of orbital decay measurements in hot Jupiter systems by a factor of 7.2. Assuming the stellar tidal quality factor inferred from previous observations, ET is expected to detect orbital decay in three additional hot Jupiter systems. The expanded sample of hot Jupiters with measured orbital decay will establish ET as a powerful probe of tidal dissipation in star-planet systems, providing tighter constraints on stellar tidal quality factors and new insights into the tidal evolution of hot Jupiters.

authors.name: Wenqin Wang, Yue Wang, Di-Chang Chen, Hui Zhang, Jian Ge, Bo Ma

papers.title: Preliminary Goniopolarimetric Simulations for Space Weather Radio (SWARA) Polarimeter
papers.summary: Goniopolarimetry is a technique that measures the direction-of-arrival (DoA) using the polarization properties of the incident electromagnetic (EM) waves. This study aims to incorporate the technique of Goniopolarimetry for our proposed polarimeter, Space Weather Radio (SWARA) Polarimeter, to provide early warnings for space weather or solar events. We have performed preliminary simulations for a tri-monopole antenna configuration. The behaviour of the tri-monopole antenna with varying signal-to-noise (SNR) ratios along the field-of-view (FOV) was investigated using simulations. The angular localization error (ALE) variations, along with SNRs, were simulated to quantify the sensitivity of the Goniopolarimetric algorithm to galactic background noise. Future work will focus on determining the optimum effective length of the individual monopoles to maximize sensitivity and localization accuracy while ensuring efficient impedance matching with the receiver. The optimized antenna will be evaluated under realistic plasma environments through electromagnetic and plasma simulations to investigate the influence of plasma parameters.

authors.name: Poorva Singh, Mugundhan V., Anshu Kumari

papers.title: MP-DualNet: A Dual-Branch Deep Learning Approach for Magnetopause Boundary Detection Using Simulated SXI Images
papers.summary: The Earth's magnetopause is a key boundary governing solar wind-magnetosphere coupling. The Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer (SMILE) mission will provide global soft X-ray imaging of the magnetosphere through solar wind charge exchange (SWCX) emission, offering a new opportunity for remote sensing of magnetopause dynamics. However, the limited field of view (FOV) and variable observation geometry of the Soft X-ray Imager (SXI) pose challenges for reliable magnetopause detection. In this study, we develop MP-DualNet, an end-to-end dual-branch deep learning framework for automated magnetopause detection from simulated SXI observations. The framework jointly performs coarse localization to determine magnetopause visibility and relative position within the FOV, and fine-scale boundary localization through pixel-level segmentation. The model is trained and evaluated using line-of-sight magnetopause envelope maps derived from global hybrid simulations under different solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field conditions. The results demonstrate stable and consistent performance, with a classification accuracy exceeding 0.94 and a segmentation IoU above 0.97. For the test set, the mean absolute angular displacement from the reference boundary was 0.488 degrees. The model maintains robust performance across a wide range of noise levels and generalizes well, as demonstrated by its application to an independent storm event. These results indicate that MP-DualNet provides a reliable and generalizable approach for magnetopause detection in SXI observations, supporting future 3D reconstruction and space weather studies in the context of the SMILE mission.

authors.name: Cheng Zhong, Zhongwei Yang, Tianran Sun, Chengyan Huang, Jiajia Liu, Jingnan Guo, Yuming Wang, Chi Wang

papers.title: Systematic Search for Cataclysmic Variables in Radio Surveys: First Radio Detection of IX Velorum
papers.summary: We present a systematic search for radio emission from cataclysmic variables (CVs) across four wide-field radio surveys in the 0.7-4 GHz frequency range: VLASS; RACS; VAST; and EMU. We generated a reliable catalog of 2225 optically-identified CV candidates using a multi-stage cross-match, combined with systematic and manual verification; 1374 are matched to Gaia sources within the radio surveys' footprints. Among these, we detected six CVs in at least one epoch (at 1e16.5-1e17.5 erg/s/Hz, consistent with the typical population of radio-detected CVs); five had been detected in radio before. IX Vel, the closest nova-like CV, is detected in radio for the first time and shows quasi-persistent low-level emission across a 10 hr EMU (943.5 MHz) observation. Given most epochs detected no CV, we stacked images without radio detections to better constrain time-averaged brightnesses. We created co-added images and placed upper limits on low-level radio emission from each of the 423 individual CVs within the VAST footprint. To constrain the median brightness for the entire CV population, we combined all Gaia-matched CVs in each survey into single population-wide stacked images, detecting no statistically significant emission. Finally, we created population-wide image stacks of the CVs within 100 pc, using 14 epochs from 5 CVs in EMU to constrain their median persistent specific luminosity to <3e14 erg/s/Hz.

authors.name: Suhasini S. Rao, Gregory R. Sivakoff, Craig O. Heinke, Akash Anumarlapudi, Laura Driessen, David L. Kaplan Patrick A. Woudt

papers.title: First Results from JACKS: A VLA Ammonia View of Gas Heating and Star-forming Cores in the Central Molecular Zone
papers.summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) combines warm molecular gas, strong turbulence, and a star-formation rate below that expected from its dense-gas reservoir. The JVLA Ammonia C-configuration K-band Survey (JACKS) is designed to connect these environmental conditions to the thermal and kinematic structure of compact, potentially star-forming gas. JACKS follows the footprint of the ALMA Central Molecular Zone Exploration Survey (ACES) with 31 Very Large Array mosaic fields. Its K-band setup covers the metastable NH$_3$ $(1,1)$--$(5,5)$ inversion transitions, five non-metastable NH$_3$ lines, the 22-GHz H$_2$O maser transition, H64$\alpha$ and H66$\alpha$, and broad continuum windows. The nominal resolutions are approximately $1.5''$ ($0.06$ pc at the Galactic Centre) and $0.4$ km s$^{-1}$ for the NH$_3$ lines. We present preliminary imaging products that demonstrate water-maser self-calibration, compact and extended continuum emission, filamentary NH$_3$ structure, and complex compact sources with multiple velocity components. Tests that combine JACKS with the SWAG and HOPS ammonia surveys recover progressively larger angular scales. These early products establish the survey's ability to connect core-scale gas heating and kinematics to the cloud-scale CMZ environment; quantitative temperature, opacity, and core-population measurements will follow from the uniformly reduced data set.

authors.name: Xu Zhang, Xing Lu, Elisabeth A. C. Mills, Qizhou Zhang, Daniel L. Walker, Natalie O. Butterfield, Namitha Issac, Annika Schmiedeke, Suinan Zhang, JACKS collaborations

papers.title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
papers.summary: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. This expanded sample provides an unprecedented opportunity to test the predictions of cosmological simulations and discriminate between competing physical prescriptions.

authors.name: Shen Li, Yiping Shu, Lin Nie

papers.title: Constraining the timescale of activity in Mrk 1018
papers.summary: We present analysis of an extended emission line region projected 3.77 kpc from the nucleus of the canonical changing-look AGN Mrk~1018, found in MUSE integral-field observations from the Close AGN Reference Survey. Emission-line ratios show that the region exhibits AGN ionisation but has a very low velocity dispersion, $77 \pm 1$ kms$^{-1}$, ruling out an ionised outflow. The lower limit on the light travel time is $12{,}300 \pm 2{,}300$ yr, implying that the nucleus has therefore been active for at least this long. This is much longer than the duration of either observed changing-look transition, which occurred over several years. This implies that Mrk 1018's multi-year variations are occurring within a longer term active phase.

authors.name: Rebecca McElroy, Scott M. Croom, Thomas Dunn

papers.title: Violent relaxation in hierarchical stellar systems: pathways toward massive black hole formation in the early Universe
papers.summary: Massive stellar systems have been detected in the high-redshift Universe via the James Webb Space Telescope using gravitational lensing techniques. Such stellar systems may evolve on short dynamical timescales, despite a formally large 2-body relaxation time. If the stellar system consists of a large number of gravitationally bound clusters, a 2-body relaxation time can be defined for the star clusters in analogy to the 2-body relaxation time for stars, implying a faster evolution determined by the number of stars per cluster. At their formation, clusters will go through a process of "cold collapse" as part of their early, non-collisional, evolution. This phase enhances the mass segregation between the more massive and less massive population of stars. We derive a criteria based on the mass of the two components that determines under which conditions the massive component may even decouple from the cluster itself. Mergers of clusters and multiple mergers on average tend to produce systems with larger cluster radii. For the formation of massive black holes via dense stellar systems, the most promising pathway consists in the cold collapse of a dense massive cluster, after few mergers (or possibly none). In such a cluster with a sufficient number of massive stars, the massive population of stars will dynamically decouple in the central region and go through core collapse, leading to the formation of a central massive object. In the case of multiple mergers, massive but more spatially extended stellar systems will form.

authors.name: Dominik R. G. Schleicher, Francesco Flammini Dotti, Mat\'ias Liempi, Tommaso Zana, Andr\'es Escala, Muhammad A. Latif, Roberto Capuzzo-Dolcetta, Marcelo C. Vergara, Lorenzo Paparella

papers.title: The Pristine survey XXXI. A stream offset from the Stream: very metal-poor stellar debris trailing 100$^{\circ}$ from the LMC-SMC system
papers.summary: Context: The stellar counterpart to the $200^\circ$-long HI Stream from the Clouds probes their tidally stripped stellar populations and constrains their interaction history and structure before infall into the Milky Way. Aims: We investigate the chemodynamics and possible origin of very metal-poor (VMP; [Fe/H] $<-2$) stars in the stellar Stream, targeting distant red giants selected from the Pristine--Gaia synthetic metallicity catalogue. Methods: We obtained high-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidate members, deriving radial velocities and metallicities. We combine these data with literature red giant members and assess their association with the Clouds using orbital integrations in a time-dependent Milky Way--LMC potential. We also compare their distribution with collisionless test particles initially placed in a diffuse LMC stellar halo. Results: We identify 12 high-confidence members based on energy and angular momentum: one intermediate metal-poor star ([Fe/H] $\sim-1.6$), ten VMP stars, and one extremely metal-poor (EMP) star ([Fe/H] $<-3$). The new VMP stars trace over $100^\circ$ of the trailing Stream, follow the Clouds' kinematics, and lie $\sim20^\circ$ from both the HI Stream and previously known, more metal-rich debris, suggesting a metallicity-dependent spatial distribution. Combined with the literature, they approximately double the known red giant sample and extend its metallicity range from [Fe/H] $\sim-0.5$ to $-4.3$. Orbital integrations support an association with the Clouds, while test particles reproduce the debris' broad spatial distribution. Conclusions: VMP and EMP stars contribute to the Clouds' tidal debris. They may originate in the extended stellar halos of the LMC or SMC, or in disrupted satellites. Their spatial and kinematic properties can constrain future simulations of the Milky Way--LMC--SMC interaction.

authors.name: Akshara Viswanathan, Kim A. Venn, Julio F. Navarro, Daniel A. Boyea, Federico Sestito, Camila Navarrete, Hanneke C. Woudenberg, Tadafumi Matsuno, Vinicius M. Placco, Madeleine McKenzie, Triana Cornejo, Anya Dovgal, Anke Ardern-Arentsen, Manuel Bayer, Amanda Bystr\"om, Vanessa Hill, Pascale Jablonka, Jaclyn Jensen, Georges Kordopatis, Nicolas F. Martin, Rub\'en S\'anchez-Janssen, Simon E. T. Smith, Else Starkenburg, Daria Zaremba, Giuseppina Battaglia, Salvatore Taibi

papers.title: The Influence of the Inclination of the Accretion Disk in Black Hole X-Ray Binaries on the Energy Spectrum Characteristics
papers.summary: During the ascending and descending phases of some black hole X-ray binaries(BH XRBs), it was found that the X-ray Eddington ratio ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $) and the photon spectral index $\Gamma$ had an anticorrelation when the X-ray Eddington ratio was less than a specific value, and a positive correlation when it was greater than that value. Moreover, the cross points of the anticorrelation and positive correlation are different for different BH XRBs ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $ of cross point is between $ 0.1 \% $ and $ 10\% $). The reason why the cross points are different for different BH XRBs were still uncertain. So we processed the light curve and energy spectrum of 15 outbursts of eight BH XRBs during their descending phases. We found that for the same BH XRB, the values of the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point are basically consistent for different outburst times. However, for different BH XRBs, there is a positive linear correlation between the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point and the cosine of the accretion disk inclination. Therefore, We think that the geometric effect of the inclination has a significant impact on the evolution of the energy spectrum of the BH XRBs.

authors.name: Aijun Dong, Shangyao Jing, Weilong He

papers.title: A Large-Sample Study of Interstellar Reddening in Galactic Star Clusters
papers.summary: The interstellar reddening (extinction or absorption) is caused mainly by the dust grains of different sizes and compounds. All astrophysical observations are somehow affected by this effect, depending on the wavelength and location of the observed object. Different methods and techniques have been developed over the last nearly one hundred years to determine the reddening and to map the solar neighbourhood. The members of open clusters are a consistent population of stars formed together with a homogeneous metallicity. Therefore, the reddening can be estimated in a statistical way, avoiding all problems of single stars and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, for example. Other than for most available works, we can also use more massive upper main-sequence stars for the analysis. We used classical colour-colour diagrams (also known as the Q-method) for (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G) to determine consistent mean reddening values and their errors. The corresponding standard lines for the fitting are independent of the age and metallicity. We determined colour excesses for 5377 Galactic open clusters covering Galactocentric distances from two to twenty kpc, respectively. The derived values were checked with existing dust and extinction maps. In general, we found good agreement. The solar neighbourhood of +-1500 pc shows a very patchy structure of the dust composition. Our results lay the foundations for constructing a new map of the reddening (dust) distribution and estimating clusters' metallicities by isochrone fitting, keeping the distances and reddening values fixed.

authors.name: Ernst Paunzen, Teja Begari

papers.title: Discovery of the redback pulsar PSR J2053+6905 and multi-epoch optical observations of the system
papers.summary: Using the Green Bank Telescope, we discovered the 1.68-ms binary pulsar PSR J2053+6905. The discovery resulted from a targeted search for radio pulsations from a redback candidate, previously identified through optical and X-ray observations and spatially coincident with the $\gamma$-ray source 4FGL J2054.2+6904. We report the first results from the pulsar timing, including the spin period, dispersion measure, precisely measured Keplerian binary parameters, and the pulsar mass function. We also found potential evidence of scintillation and long radio eclipses. To constrain the system parameters, we performed multi-epoch time-series photometric observations using the 2.1-m telescope at the Observatorio Astron\'omico Nacional on the Sierra San Pedro M\'artir (Mexico) and the 1.5-m telescope of the Maidanak Astronomical Observatory (Uzbekistan), complemented by time-series optical spectroscopy with the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias. The optical light curves revealed a pronounced asymmetry, as well as significant long-term variations. From the spectra, we derived a radial velocity curve semi-amplitude $K = 337(4)$ km s$^{-1}$. Combining it with the pulsar mass function, we constrained the ratio of pulsar and companion masses to $M_{\rm p}/M_{\rm c} = 7.05(8)$. By fitting the stable segments of the light curves with a symmetric direct heating model, we derived constraints on the component masses ($M_{\rm p} \approx 2.1\ {\rm M}_\odot$ and $M_{\rm c} \approx 0.3\ {\rm M}_\odot$), the Roche lobe filling factor, and the companion's day- and night-side temperatures. The long-term evolution of the light curve profiles is likely driven by the dissipation or migration of a cold stellar spot.

authors.name: A. V. Karpova, J. D. Taylor, A. V. Bobakov, A. Kirichenko, D. A. Zyuzin, E. Fonseca, S. V. Zharikov, D. K. Romanov, M. Lucio-Mendoza, R. Karimov, A. Cabrera-Lavers

papers.title: Thorium and Europium production in the early Galaxy: Implications for nucleocosmochronology
papers.summary: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology, with the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio providing a promising chronometer. We assess the reliability of log(Th/Eu) as an age indicator by testing whether thorium and europium were co-produced in a constant ratio in metal-poor stars, and evaluate the uncertainties affecting stellar ages. We present new Th and Eu abundance measurements for eight TITANS reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. Combining these measurements with homogeneous literature samples, we investigate the behaviour of log(Th/Eu) as a function of metallicity. We derive ages adopting a theoretical initial r-process production ratio and assess the effects of observational uncertainties and sample statistics. At low metallicity, the observed Th/Eu ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity after excluding stars with anomalous actinide abundances, supporting broadly uniform Th and Eu co-production in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are consistent with expectations for an old, metal-poor halo population, although individual uncertainties remain substantial. Higher spectral resolution is needed to improve Th measurements, while combining stars in coeval populations can provide additional statistical gains. Nucleocosmochronology offers an independent approach to dating the oldest stellar populations. Homogeneous samples of coeval stars, particularly in globular clusters, observed with future high-resolution multi-object spectrographs could provide stronger constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

authors.name: L. Magrini, R. E. Giribaldi, M. Palla, S. Randich, L. Pasquini, C. J. Hansen, R. Smiljanic, M. Racca, M. Tsantaki, J. Schiappacasse-Ulloa, A. Skuladottir, G. Kordopatis, L. Berni, T. Matsuno, G. Casali, V. Hill, F. Matteucci, G. Cescutti, F. Rizzuti, E. Spitoni

papers.title: FALCON (FERMI-ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN): Cross-matching ALMA Calibrators with Fermi-LAT Blazars
papers.summary: Blazars are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets closely aligned with our line of sight, producing Doppler-boosted emission from radio to gamma rays. Millimeter emission near the synchrotron self-absorption turnover probes compact regions at the jet base, yet large statistical studies in this regime remain limited. We construct the FALCON (FERMI--ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN) catalogue, a millimeter-selected blazar sample by cross-matching the ALMA Calibrator Source Catalogue with the Third Data Release of the Fourth LAT AGN Catalog (4LAC-DR3). After removing duplicates, we obtain 949 unique gamma-ray-associated sources, corresponding to approximately 25 % of the 4LAC-DR3 blazar population. For the subset with available redshift measurements, we compute millimeter and gamma-ray luminosities and find a strong, statistically significant correlation that remains robust after accounting for redshift effects. Fermi-detected blazars exhibit systematically flatter millimeter spectral indices than gamma-ray non-detected ALMA calibrators, while the redshift-controlled luminosity correlation becomes progressively weaker from high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacs toward flat-spectrum radio quasars. These results indicate an intrinsic connection between millimeter and gamma-ray emission, consistent with a common origin in relativistic jets governed by Doppler boosting and time-averaged jet power.

authors.name: Kanako Narita, Yoshiyuki Inoue, Bunyo Hatsukade, Yasushi Fukazawa

papers.title: GALI Localization of Off-Grid GRB Directions: A Comparison of Rectangular and Triangular Calibration Meshes
papers.summary: Rapid localization of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) is essential for multi-wavelength and multi-messenger follow-up, but combining wide sky coverage with accurate localization remains challenging. GALI (GAmma-ray burst Localizing Instrument) determines source directions from count-rate modulations caused by internal shadowing in a three-dimensional scintillator array. We investigate a triangular calibration mesh based on an icosphere tessellation of the hemisphere and compare it with the rectangular mesh used previously. The triangular mesh samples the hemisphere more isotropically and gives better interpolation between calibration points. Laboratory measurements with the full-scale GALI detector yield an average angular separation of $0.86^\circ \pm 0.14^\circ$ for random source directions, compared with $1.19^\circ \pm 0.28^\circ$ for the rectangular mesh. Monte Carlo simulations of 50,000 randomly distributed GRBs in realistic low-Earth-orbit background conditions, each with 1000 detected counts, give average angular separations of $1.91^\circ \pm 1.20^\circ$ and $2.73^\circ \pm 2.18^\circ$ for triangular and rectangular meshes, respectively. The better laboratory performance is partly attributed to its approximately 3-4 times higher detected counts. Additional simulations indicate sensitivity from 10 keV to $\sim$1 MeV, with a peak effective area of about 130 cm$^2$ near 100-150 keV. A compact 1U GALI implementation also achieves degree-scale localization in simulations, demonstrating the concept's potential for CubeSat-based GRB and multi-messenger missions.

authors.name: Julia Saleh-Natur, Ehud Behar, Omer Reich, Shlomit Tarem, Zvika Tarem, Alex Vdovin, Amir Feigenboim, Roey Evental, Solomon Margolin

papers.title: Multi-epoch monitoring of the faint northern component in 3C 84 during 2016-2021
papers.summary: We present the results of multi-epoch very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations of the sub-parsec-scale northern jet component of 3C 84 (known as the N1 component) at 7 mm from 2016 to 2021. The peak position of the N1 component exhibits positional variations of approximately 0.2 mas at a distance of about 2.5 mas from the central radio core (C1) throughout the observation period. Although a linear fit yields a small proper motion of $\mu_{\rm{Dec}}=0.054\pm0.019~\rm{mas}~\rm{yr}^{-1}$, corresponding to an apparent velocity of $\beta_{\rm{app}}=0.062\pm0.021$, this displacement is comparable to the observed positional scatter, and the hypothesis that N1 exhibits systematic motion is not statistically supported. In contrast, the peak flux density varies by approximately a factor of two on timescales of several months. We propose two possible explanations for the observed behavior of N1. One is that N1 is the counterpart of the southern hotspot C3, but its motion has been halted by a collision with a compact and dense cloud along its path; in this case, the flux variability may be caused by changes in the free-free absorption opacity of the non-uniform cloud. The other possibility is that N1 is part of the northern jet that is heavily obscured by foreground free-free absorption and is observed through a gap in the absorbing medium; in this case, the variability may reflect intrinsic changes in the jet and its interaction with a non-uniform ambient medium. These results provide new constraints on the physical origin of N1 and on the circumnuclear environment of 3C 84.

authors.name: Kotaro Niinuma, Motoki Kino, Nozomu Kawakatsu, Hiroshi Nagai, Gabriele Giovannini, Filippo D'Ammando, Monica Orienti, Kazuhiro Hada, Kiyoaki Wajima, Marcello Giroletti

papers.title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
papers.summary: Karchev et al. (2026) derived a value of H0 by combining the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with SH0ES calibrator Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia; Riess et al. 2022), used to anchor the SN Ia absolute luminosity. The ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset (Rigault et al., 2025) is the largest (O(3000)) SN Ia sample to date obtained with a single telescope. However, as emphasized in the data release, the absolute photometric calibration of the survey has not yet been established to the precision required for cosmological inference. The relative photometric zeropoint offset between the SH0ES and ZTF SN Ia DR2 samples, which is fully degenerate with H0, is therefore unknown and cannot be determined from publicly available data. The photometric corrections introduced in Karchev et al. (2026) do not address this global calibration offset. Consequently, their reported H0 determination is not supported by the available calibration information. We nonetheless share the excitement of pursuing state-of-the-art cosmology with ZTF and are actively working toward the release of a fully calibrated dataset

authors.name: Mickael Rigault, Brodie Popovic, Ariel Goobar, Suhail Dhawan, Marie Aubert, Marc Betoule, Umut Burgaz, Georgios Dimitriadis, Llu\'is Galbany, Tom\'as E. M\"uller Bravo, Antoine Gilles Lordet, Madeleine Ginolin, Young-Lo Kim, Marek Kowalski, Jakob Nordin, Nicolas Regnault, Mathew Smith, Jesper Sollerman, Jacco H. Terwel, Alice Townsend

papers.title: Cepheid Metallicity in the Leavitt Law (C-MetaLL) survey: X First spectroscopic characterization of Galactic Type II Cepheids and calibration of the Period-Wesenheit-Metallicity relations
papers.summary: Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are Population II pulsating stars that serve as distance indicators through their period--luminosity relation. Along with RR Lyrae stars and the tip of the red giant branch, they offer an independent route to the Hubble constant, helping assess systematic uncertainties in its determination. We aim to investigate the impact of chemical composition on T2Cs' period--luminosity relations by building a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of Galactic T2Cs with iron and oxygen abundances. We observed 80 Galactic T2Cs with UVES at the ESO Very Large Telescope. For 74 stars, we derived stellar parameters and iron and oxygen abundances through a self-consistent spectroscopic analysis based on equivalent widths of absorption lines. This sample nearly doubles the number of T2Cs with spectroscopic metallicity measurements available in the literature. We used these abundances to test theoretical predictions for the instability strip and, together with $Gaia$ parallaxes, to derive Period--Wesenheit--metallicity (PWZ) relations. In agreement with theoretical predictions, the metallicity coefficient ($\gamma$) is small and statistically consistent with zero in all relations, ranging from approximately $-0.02$ to $+0.17$ mag dex$^{-1}$. We also estimated distances to 22 Galactic Globular Clusters hosting T2Cs, finding agreement within uncertainties with independent literature estimates. Our results show that metallicity has, at most, a minor impact on T2Cs' pulsation properties and distance scale, supporting their reliability as Population II distance indicators.

authors.name: T. Sicignano, M. Romaniello, A. Bhardwaj, V. Ripepi, M. Rejkuba, M. Marconi, E. Trentin, G. Catanzaro, G. De Somma, R. Molinaro, S. Das, I. Musella, L. Salmeri, P. Nishad, S. Kar, S. Leccia

papers.title: GradFlex: a Gradient-Based Method for Weak Lensing Flexion Measurement
papers.summary: Flexion, the second-order gravitational lensing distortion, probes small-scale mass distribution and complement the cosmic shear measurement. However, its detection is highly challenging due to the faint signal and the contamination arising from the intrinsic galaxy morphology. In this Letter, we present GradFlex, a new method that extracts flexion from the gradient field of galaxy surface brightness distributions without assuming a specific point-spread function model or galaxy morphology. Using surface-brightness conservation, we relate the pre- and post-lensing gradient fields and derive flexion estimators from ensemble-averaged statistics of the corresponding spins. Tests on numerical simulations across diverse galaxy morphologies and multiple noise realizations demonstrate its reliability under realistic observing conditions. Combined with shear measurements, it could tighten constraints on cluster density profiles and enable more detailed studies of substructure than shear alone.

authors.name: Jiarui Sun, Jun Zhang, Toshifumi Futamase

papers.title: Design and Commissioning of the BURSTT-256 Main Antenna Array for the Fast Radio Burst Survey in the Local Universe
papers.summary: The Bustling Universe Radio Survey Telescope in Taiwan (BURSTT) is a radio interferometer array designed for surveying fast radio bursts (FRBs) in the nearby Universe with a wide instantaneous field of view (FoV) of $\approx$6000 deg$^2$ and precisely localizing them with sub-arcsecond angular resolution. The first phase of BURSTT, BURSTT-256, consists of a main antenna array comprising 256 log-periodic dipole antennas (LPDAs) observing at 400-800 MHz for real-time beamforming and FRB search, currently with 256 beams covering $\approx$ 3200 deg$^2$ FoV, together with several smaller outrigger stations with 16-64 antennas and separated by $\mathcal{O}(10^2 - 10^3)$ km baselines for joint observations to localize FRBs using very-long baseline interferometry. This work presents the design, deployment, and commissioning of the BURSTT-256 main array, including site selection, radio-frequency (RF) background characterization, receiver antenna array and RF front-end, as well as real-time, factorized digital beamforming backend that currently generates 256 beams. The system's on-sky performance, sensitivity, and beamforming fidelity have been calibrated through observations of bright celestial calibrators. The antenna array in the initial phase using commercial LPDAs has a system equivalent flux density of $\approx$11 kJy, and is expected to achieve $\approx$4 kJy using custom-design LPDAs after optimization in late 2026. BURSTT-256 serves as a critical pathfinder for future expansion of the array to 2048 elements and beyond, operating at 300-700 MHz with $\approx$6000 deg$^2$ FoV. It establishes the framework required to discover and localize nearby FRBs with sub-arcsecond precision. By substantially increasing the number of well-localized nearby FRBs, BURSTT will facilitate multi-wavelength and multi-messenger counterpart identification, helping to unveil the elusive origin of FRBs.

authors.name: Shih-Hao Wang, Kai-Yang Lin, Chao-Te Li, Chau-Ching Chiong, Jen-Chieh Cheng, Chung-Cheng Chen, Hsien-Chun Tseng, Shu-Hao Chang, Pai-An Chen, Ta-Shun Wei, Chin-Ting Ho, Vigo Feng-Shun Wu, Yu-Chieh Huang, Sujin Eie, Yao-Huan Tseng, Ue-Li Pen, Chih-Yi Wen, Homin Jiang, Andrew Wang, Bishnu Kumar Sharma, Tzu-Hong Chen Lin, Yuan-Wei Hu, Shih-Wen Chung, Chen-Hui Peng, Ming-Tang Chen, Pisin Chen, Jiwoo Nam, Tomotsugu Goto, Tetsuya Hashimoto, Chin-Ping Hu, Yuan-Chang Hou, Daniel Baker, Michael Chiang, Somnath Dutta, Sun-Kun King, Hiroto Masaoka, Chung-Yun Kuo, Che-Wei Pai, Decmend Fang-Jie Ling

papers.title: Multi-layer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
papers.summary: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry. Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations. The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3\deg\pm0.8\deg$ in the northwest to $162.2\deg\pm0.6\deg$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~\mu\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures. Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

authors.name: G. A. P. Franco, J. M. Girart, F. O. Alves

papers.title: Survey of Surveys Data Release 3. Homogenised stellar parameters across nine spectroscopic surveys
papers.summary: Large spectroscopic surveys have measured atmospheric parameters for millions of Milky Way stars, but differences in instruments, wavelength ranges, analysis methods, and assumptions introduce survey-dependent systematics that complicate their joint use. We aim to place effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity estimates from major spectroscopic surveys onto a common, externally validated scale, and to provide a homogenised catalogue for large-scale Galactic studies. We construct the calibration hierarchically. We first define an internal reference scale from the best-populated and best-overlapped surveys (APOGEE, GALAH, and LAMOST LRS), and model survey-to-reference corrections and their uncertainties with machine-learning regression. The scale is then extended to LAMOST MRS, Gaia RVS, RAVE, DESI, Gaia-ESO, and SEGUE, and anchored to high-quality measurements from the PASTEL database. The calibration reduces survey-to-survey offsets and improves consistency in independent overlap samples: independent calibration of GALAH and LAMOST LRS temperatures onto the APOGEE scale reduces their median offset from 44.5 K to 6.2 K. The final catalogue contains about 10.13 million stars, including 6.10 million in the recommended high-quality subset and 3.69 million in the metallicity-optimised subset. For the high-quality subset, Gaia benchmark stars give median residuals of 30 K in $T_{\rm eff}$, 0.03 dex in $\log g$, and $-0.02$ dex in [Fe/H]. The [Fe/H]-optimised subset gives median residuals of 0.003 dex against Gaia benchmark stars, 0.05 dex for globular clusters, and $-0.02$ dex for open clusters. As an example application, we confirm the presence of metal-poor stars on thin-disc-like orbits, including stars with [Fe/H] $< -2$, showing that the catalogue can be used to study rare Galactic populations on a consistent multi-survey scale.

authors.name: A. Avdeeva, E. Pancino, A. Turchi, P. M. Marrese, S. Marinoni, G. Fanari, D. Alvarez Garay, M. Echeveste, E. Leitinger, S. Nedhath, S. Rani, E. Reggiani, N. Sanna, S. Saracino, L. Steinbauer

papers.title: Mass loss in AF supergiants: At the verge of the Eddington limit and still with weak line-driven winds
papers.summary: We study global atmosphere models of AF supergiants. In agreement with previous studies, we found super-Eddington layers in the photospheres of these stars, which lead to density inversions. Our tests showed that the super-Eddington layers are caused by hydrogen ionization. The analysis of radial perturbations has not revealed any instability of such layers, but we show that super-Eddington layers in an optically thick environment are prone to instabilities due to nonradial perturbations. We predict the wind parameters of AF supergiants from our global wind code with a comoving-frame radiative force. Despite the existence of density inversions, the predicted mass-loss rates are significantly lower than those estimated from observations.
