Our results place recent numerical evidence for a gapless $Z_{2}$ Dirac spin liquid on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice within a controlled field-theoretic framework and demonstrate that fermionic deconfined criticality on the square lattice-including critical exponents and stability-extends to frustrated lattices with reduced symmetry.

authors.name: Andreas Feuerpfeil, Leyna Shackleton, Atanu Maity, Ronny Thomale, Subir Sachdev, Yasir Iqbal

papers.title: Deep-layered machines have a built-in Occam's razor
papers.summary: Many complex systems map vast numbers of microscopic descriptions onto far fewer macroscopic outcomes. Surprisingly, these input-output maps strongly favor simple outputs. In an exactly solvable deep-layered machine, we prove that simplicity bias strengthens with every layer. The probability of an output function $F$ approaches $\Pr(F)\propto 2^{-K(F)}$, where $K$ is the Kolmogorov complexity. Our results show that hierarchical composition alone can generate an intrinsic Occam's razor, suggesting a general mechanism for simplicity bias in learning and evolution.

authors.name: Thomas Fink

papers.title: Kelvin-Helmholtz and counter-superflow instabilities driven by differential effective rotation in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.summary: Interfacial hydrodynamic instabilities in multicomponent superfluids provide a versatile platform to explore nonequilibrium quantum dynamics beyond classical fluid analogues. We study dynamical interfacial instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional three-component Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a harmonic trap, where differential effective rotation between neighboring components is generated through selective phase imprinting. A component with an imprinted vorticity $l_j$ acquires an azimuthal phase winding $\phi_j = l_j\theta$, producing a superfluid velocity $v_\theta(r_j) = l_j\hbar/mr_j$ at interface radius $r_j$ and an effective angular velocity $\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} = l_j\hbar/mr_j^2$. The differential effective rotation $\Delta\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} = \Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} - \Omega_{j+1}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ between neighboring components constitutes the sole driver of interfacial shear and the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI). Three instability regimes are examined: KHI in the strongly immiscible limit, counter-superflow instability in the partially miscible regime, and a parameter window where both mechanisms coexist. A hydrodynamic pressure-balance model is derived, showing that the KHI onset condition depends only on $\Delta\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}}$. Time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii simulations and a Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis identify the dominant unstable modes, whose spatial structures are consistent with the observed density modulations. The dominant azimuthal mode is set by a competition between shear-driven destabilization and surface-tension stabilization, confirmed by numerical simulations with different imprinted vorticities. The results show that a three-component condensate with two tunable interfaces provides a controlled platform for studying multicomponent quantum hydrodynamics, with instability dynamics significantly richer than those of binary mixtures.

authors.name: Susovan Giri, Arpana Saboo, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Vipin, Sonjoy Majumder

papers.title: Scaling of Long-Range Loop-Erased Random Walks
papers.summary: We study the scaling properties of long-range loop-erased random walks (LR-LERW), where the underlying random walker performs L\'evy-flight-like jumps with a power-law step-length distribution $P(\mathbf{r})\sim |\mathbf{r}|^{-(d+\sigma)}$. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we measure the scaling relation $N \sim R^{d_N}$ between the loop-erased step number $N$ and the spatial extent $R$, and determine the geometric exponent $d_N$ for various values of $\sigma$ in spatial dimensions $d = 1, 2,$ and $3$, as well as at the marginal point $\sigma = 2$ in $d=4$ and $5$. We observe a continuous crossover from long-range (LR) to short-range (SR) behavior as $\sigma$ increases. Below the upper critical dimension $d<d_c=4$, for $\sigma < d/2$, loop erasure is asymptotically irrelevant and $d_N=\sigma$, consistent with L\'evy-flight scaling. For $d/2 < \sigma < 2$, loop erasure becomes relevant and $d_N$ varies continuously toward the SR-LERW value. At the marginal points with $\sigma=d/2$ or $\sigma=2$, clear logarithmic corrections are observed. At and above the upper critical dimension, $d \geq 4$, the scaling at $\sigma=2$ is found to be $N \sim R^2/\ln R$, consistent with that of the corresponding L\'evy flight. Our results provide a systematic numerical determination of $d_N(\sigma)$ for the LR-LERW across dimensions, and are consistent with $\sigma_* = 2$ as the boundary between LR and SR critical behaviors recently established in a broad variety of statistical models.

authors.name: Tianning Xiao, Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, Youjin Deng

papers.title: Conductivity of charge-neutral multicomponent 2D electron-hole system
papers.summary: The interplay between distinct carrier species in systems with broken Galilean invariance can give rise to a rich landscape of interaction-driven transport phenomena. Here, we develop a comprehensive theory of the electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional mixture of massless Dirac and massive fermions, a system realized in HgTe quantum wells tuned to the charge-neutrality point. In this regime, all carriers are thermally activated, enabling a self-consistent, temperature-dependent interplay between the two species. Crucially, the charge-neutrality condition ensures that the chemical potential is not externally pinned but is determined self-consistently, thereby making the system's transport response an intrinsic probe of inter-species quantum friction. We demonstrate that the conductivity changes with temperature : at low temperatures, transport is dominated by massless Dirac carriers, yielding a nearly temperature-independent conductivity reminiscent of the charge-neutrality point in pristine graphene. As the temperature rises, massive holes become thermally excited, and their mutual scattering with Dirac carriers induces a specific nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the conductivity in both clean and disordered structures. In particular, in nearly clean structures with strong screening modeled by a short-range interparticle interaction potential, the system's conductivity can exhibit an inverse-quadratic temperature dependence. Conversely, in disordered structures with a long-range interparticle interaction, it varies quadratically with temperature. Our findings establish HgTe quantum wells at charge neutrality as a clean, highly tunable platform for isolating and quantitatively studying interaction-driven transport in the absence of Galilean invariance, offering a direct pathway to explore regimes where interparticle collisions dominate over disorder.

authors.name: Yuping Huang, O. V. Kibis, V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko

papers.title: Pressure-Driven Activation of Semi-core p-Orbitals in Rb and Cs via Crystal-Field Splitting
papers.summary: High-pressure unconventional oxidation states are attributed to exceptional charge transfer, which is itself induced by the differential pressure response of atomic orbital energy levels. The high oxidation states observed in heavy alkali metals (Cs, Ba, Ra) exemplify this behavior, as their semi-core p-states surpass the valence orbital levels of oxidants, e.g., the 2p-orbital of F, at high pressure. However, semi-core p-electron activation in lighter alkali metals, such as Rb, is hindered because the relative orbitals lie at intrinsically lower energies due to their smaller radii, making pressure-induced upshift challenging. We demonstrate that crystal-field splitting of alkali-metal semi-core p-orbitals selectively elevates a portion of these states, substantially lowering the pressure threshold for their chemical activation. Here, our computations reveal that the semi-core 4p-electrons of Rb form weak metallic bonds with F in $P2_1/c$-RbBF5 at around 250 GPa, a pressure accessible in modern high-pressure experiments. Extending to Cs-B-F systems, the crystal-field splitting drives 5p participation in Cs-F bond formation in CsBF5. These findings unveil a new paradigm for semi-core or inner-shell chemistry, providing a unifying framework for semi-core electron activation and bonding. Crucially, they establish that semi-core electrons of light main-group elements, including Rb, are accessible at experimentally feasible pressures.

authors.name: Shuran Ma, Shuyang Sun, Dengyao Yu, Xue Cong, Yanchao Wang, Yuanzheng Chen, Zhen Liu

papers.title: Anomalous Low-temperature Magnetotransport in Kagome Metal CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ under Pressure
papers.summary: As a unique kagome superconductor displaying clear signatures of strong electronic correlations, CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ has drawn much attention. Its rich temperature-pressure phase diagram features intertwined orders including pressure-induced superconductivity and two density-wave-like phases, making it an outstanding platform to explore the complex coexistence and competition of multiple quantum orders. At around 30 K, which we designate as $T_3$, a possible anomaly manifesting as a hump in the resistivity has been observed, yet its nature remains largely unexplored due to limited supporting evidence from other probes. Here, we conducted systematic magnetotransport experiments under hydrostatic pressure to investigate the nature of this anomaly. Our results reveal an abundance of intriguing magnetotransport signatures below $T_3$, including a non-trivial temperature dependence of the Hall coefficient, multi-band characteristics, and pressure-enhanced anomalous-Hall-like effect. These signatures bear resemblance to those observed in many other correlated materials with distinct origins. These findings suggest the possibility of an additional electronic order in CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$, calling for further detailed investigations.

authors.name: Zikai Zhou, Wenyan Wang, Deng Hu, Zheyu Wang, Ying Kit Tsui, Tsz Fung Poon, Zhiwei Wang, Swee K. Goh

papers.title: Ground state of the Hubbard model with spin-dependent linear potential
papers.summary: We investigate the competition between attractive spin-spin interactions and spin-separating external forces in the ground state of a one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. We consider a lattice with open boundary conditions, subject to a linear external potential whose gradient is opposite for the two spin components, so that each spin species sees a potential minimum at a different end of the lattice. Using density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations, we map the ground-state density distributions and the number of doubly occupied sites as a function of the potential gradient $\beta$ and interaction strength. We identify three distinct regimes separated by critical threshold gradients: (i) a small-$\beta$ regime where fermion pairing remains robust against the external potential; (ii) an intermediate-$\beta$ phase-separated regime characterized by a staircase-like decrease in the doublon number, corresponding to the successive, one-by-one breaking of bound pairs; and (iii) a large-$\beta$ regime where the two spin components are completely spatially separated. We complement the numerical results with a phenomenological model and a local-density approximation analysis, from which we derive closed-form analytical estimates for these critical threshold values. We also verify that the staircase structure persists under additional harmonic confinement. Our results are directly testable in cold-atom experiments, and demonstrate that a spin-dependent linear potential enables precise, integer-level control of the number of bound fermion pairs.

authors.name: Jacek Dobrzyniecki, Thomas Busch

papers.title: Thermal bottleneck in a freely suspended superconducting island on InAs nanowire
papers.summary: We investigate the heat balance in superconducting islands (S-islands) formed in epitaxial Al/InAs nanowires (NWs) freely suspended above the substrate. We employ a Joule spectroscopy approach, which traces the superconductor-normal transition in the S-island mediated by heating of the neighboring InAs NW segments via transport current. The temperature of the surrounding 3He bath is varied with nearby mesoscopic heaters and controlled with the NW Johnson noise thermometry. The experiment reveals a substantial thermal relaxation bottleneck associated with the cooling via surrounding 3He, which gives rise to phonon heating in the S-island. Our results uncover the role of environmental cooling in non-equilibrium experiments in S-islands in NW devices.

authors.name: E. V. Shpagina, E. S. Tikhonov, D. Ruhstorfer, G. Koblmueller, V. S. Khrapai

papers.title: Anomalous thermal and elastic properties of an epitaxial NiTi film exhibiting R-phase
papers.summary: Shape memory alloys like NiTi are at the core of emerging thermal management applications, including elastocaloric refrigeration, thermoelastic harvesting, and latent heat storage. Most of these applications benefit from a small scale due to the accelerated heat exchange, but obtaining precise functional properties of films is challenging. Here we demonstrate that transient grating spectroscopy (TGS) enables characterization of elastic coefficients and thermal diffusivity of a 3 $\mu$m thick epitaxial NiTi film during a thermally induced phase transformation. The in-situ measurement of a complete austenite$\rightarrow$R-phase$\rightarrow$martensite$\rightarrow$austenite temperature cycle reveals that the elastic properties exhibit a crossover of the shear moduli (from $c^\prime c_{44}$ in martensite) and that the thermal diffusivity changes by a factor of {4.5} between the R-phase and austenite. This dramatic change, together with the absence of hysteresis between the R-phase and austenite, makes NiTi a promising material candidate for thermal switches. The results indicate that the change in thermal diffusivity originates from an anomalous heat capacity of the R-phase. Furthermore, our TGS study provides temperature-dependent thermal and elastic properties required for simulating thermal management microsystems using this material.

authors.name: Krist\'yna Rep\v{c}ek (Faculty of Nuclear Sciences and Physical Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague), Tom\'a\v{s} Grabec (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), David Mare\v{s} (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Pavla Stoklasov\'a (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Petr Sedl\'ak (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Jakub Ku\v{s}n\'ir (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Petr Ve\v{r}t\'at (Institute of Physics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Oleg Heczko (Institute of Physics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia), Sebastian F\"ahler (Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf, Dresden, Germany), Klara L\"unser (Institute for Energy and Materials Processes, Universit\"at Duisburg-Essen, Germany, Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems), H. Seiner (Institute of Thermomechanics, Czech Acad Sci, Prague, Czechia)

papers.title: Dynamic Eikonal Attenuation and Mutual Coherence of Quantum Particles due to Equilibrium Coulomb Fluctuations
papers.summary: We develop a dynamic theory of eikonal attenuation and mutual coherence for a quantum particle propagating through equilibrium Coulomb fluctuations. The one-particle length $\ell$ is the attenuation length of the ensemble-averaged retarded propagator, not an Anderson localization length or a transport mean free path. For a collisionless classical one-component plasma (OCP), the potential spectrum follows from the fluctuation--dissipation theorem and the RPA dielectric function. In suitable plasma parameter windows, both fast and slow probe regimes are physically meaningful. Fast probes recover the Coulomb logarithm with the dynamical infrared length $v/\omega_{\rm p}$. Slow probes yield $G(v)\propto v$ and, in the controlled weak branch, $\ell\propto k$. We derive an exact finite-thickness mutual-coherence expression and a closed slow-regime transverse scaling function. Within the controlled slow-OCP and thick-slab window, the logarithmic two-ray visibility scales as $v^{-1}$ at fixed transverse separation, in contrast to the $v^{-2}$ dependence for frozen finite-slab fluctuations. For a symmetric diffusive electrolyte, linearized stochastic density functional theory gives the exact on-shell result $G_{\rm el}(v)=(m^2C/\hbar^4)\operatorname{arsinh}[v/(2D\kappa)]$, where $C=k_{\mathrm B}Tq_0^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_b)$. For ordinary liquid electrolytes, the slow diffusive limit is inaccessible within the spatial eikonal regime and is therefore a formal asymptote. The physically relevant electrolyte limit is instead that of a fast probe, $v\gg D\kappa$, where the diffusive charge relaxation generates an intrinsic infrared length $v/(D\kappa^2)$ absent from the quasi-static theory.

authors.name: Yury A. Budkov

papers.title: Overview of the Theory of Extremely Correlated Fermi Liquids
papers.summary: The Extremely Correlated Fermi Liquids (ECFL) theory is reviewed as a framework for understanding the $t$-$J$ model in metallic systems close to the Mott insulating limit. This overview presents the underlying ideas and the resulting equations in a form accessible to nonexperts. We compare theoretical results with all available resistivity data for single-layer High-T$_{c}$ systems, and with some spectral data. The highlighted results include a density dependent quasilinear T-dependence in resistivity, an unusually small quasiparticle weight, and distinct low-temperature emergent scales that dominate transport, thermodynamics and spectral properties of single-layer High T$_c$ systems. Suggestions are made for further experiments to probe the physics of these challenging quantum many-body systems.

authors.name: B Sriram Shastry

papers.title: Coexistence of Donor and Acceptor Hydrogen States in n-Type InN
papers.summary: Hydrogen often exhibits amphoteric behavior in semiconductors, but its role is in n-type InN remains unresolved. Wurtzite InN is a narrow-gap semiconductor with high electron mobility and is therefore attractive for high-speed electronics and optoelectronic applications. Here we use hard x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (HAXPES) to probe hydrogen-related electronic structure in as-grown and post-annealed InN thin films prepared at different grown temperatures. Post annealing, which reduces the concentration of hydrogen impurities in the films, shifts the core-level spectra toward lower binding energy, consistent with a chemical-potential shift associated with the passivation of electron carriers. In the valence-band spectra, an acceptor-like in-gap feature near the valence-band maximum is suppressed after annealing. Together with the established donor-like behavior of hydrogen in InN, these results suggest that acceptor H- states coexist with donor H+ states in InN. The coexistence of these opposite hydrogen charge states provides a microscopic picture of hydrogen-driven compensation in InN and highlights the amphoteric nature of hydrogen even in a highly n-type semiconductor.

authors.name: Masaki Kobayashi, Yudai Yamashita, Kazuyuki Hirama, Yoshitaka Taniyasu

papers.title: Generalized Fourier's law in mesoscopic systems
papers.summary: Fourier's law fails when the mean free path of the energy carriers becomes comparable to the length and time scales over which the temperature field varies. We derive a thermodynamically consistent generalization in which the conductivity becomes a nonlocal memory operator $\mathbf{\kappa}_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{k},\omega)$, by combining mesoscopic nonequilibrium thermodynamics with the Mori--Kubo--Zwanzig projection-operator formalism. The Onsager kernel is a tensor sum over vibrational normal modes weighted by their Bose heat capacities and relaxation functions; it satisfies the second law for any closure consistent with the fluctuation--dissipation theorem and reduces, in the relaxation-time closure, to the nonlocal conductivity of the phonon Boltzmann equation. Two consequences follow. First, direction-dependent sampling of this tensor in a pump--probe experiment makes a nominally isotropic crystal exhibit apparent conductivities $\Lambda_z\neq\Lambda_r$. Second, the modulation frequency does not introduce temporal memory but sets the probed wavevector through the thermal penetration depth, so that the frequency-dependent suppression of the apparent conductivity measured by time-domain thermoreflectance on Ge and SiGe alloys is a spatial-nonlocality effect, with effective lengths of $0.25$--$0.4~\mu$m. With published mean-free-path spectra and no parameter adjusted to the thermoreflectance data, the kernel reproduces the spot-size dependence of Si, the frequency dependence of the apparent conductivity of Ge and Si$_{0.2}$Ge$_{0.8}$ and the rise of the apparent interface conductance of Al/Si$_{0.99}$Ge$_{0.01}$, and contains the two-channel ballistic/diffusive model as a two-sector projection.

authors.name: Luciano C. Lapas (Latin American Institute of Life and Natural Sciences, Universidade Federal da Integra\c{c}\~ao Latino-Americana, Foz do Igua\c{c}u, PR, Brazil)

papers.title: Specific absorption rate of uniaxial single-domain nanomagnets: stochastic spin dynamics versus linear response theory
papers.summary: We compute the specific absorption rate of a uniaxial single-domain nanomagnet driven by an alternating magnetic field by two methods: i) direct numerical integration of the stochastic (Langevin) Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation (the LLL approach), and ii) linear response theory (LRT) based on the Debye susceptibility with the N\'eel relaxation time $\ta$. We first analytically show that both methods are equivalent for small magnetic field amplitude, and then compute their deviation $\Lambda\equiv\SAR_{\LLL}/\SAR_{\LRT}-1$ as a function of the magnetic field amplitude for two temperatures chosen on opposite sides of the Debye resonance. One of the main results is that the sign and magnitude of $\Lambda$ are governed by the dimensionless product $\om\ta$, in addition to the linearity parameter $\xi=\mu_{s}B_{0}/k_{B}T$ for the easy-axis geometry considered here. Indeed, below resonance ($\om\ta1$, the regime typical of blocked nanoparticles) linear response theory can underestimate the specific absorption rate by up to $\sim70\%$ at $\xi\sim2$. We expect this work to provide a quantitative guidance for the use of linear response theory in magnetic hyperthermia and related nanoscale heat-transport problems, and to serve as a single-particle benchmark for extensions to many-spin and interacting systems.

authors.name: H. Kachkachi

papers.title: Monte Carlo solution of the Kondo model
papers.summary: The Kondo model is a paradigmatic quantum impurity problem realized in a wide variety of experimental platforms and central to the study of strongly correlated electrons. We introduce a discrete model that exactly reproduces the multichannel Kondo model and demonstrate that it can be simulated efficiently. Using cluster Monte Carlo algorithms, we completely eliminate critical slowing down, providing direct access to universal crossover functions and transport properties across a broad range of parameters. Remarkably, the same model captures both the weak- and strong-coupling regimes, unifying descriptions traditionally derived in complementary limits and revealing their common origin. Our method naturally accommodates large channel numbers, anisotropy, interacting one-dimensional leads, and channel asymmetry, yielding predictions for transport properties in charge-Kondo devices.

authors.name: Nicolas Paris, Oscar Bouverot-Dupuis, Christophe Mora

papers.title: Decoupling Strain-Rate Sensitivity and Deformation Length Scale Effects in Neutron-Irradiated Tungsten: A Coupled Nano-Indentation, HR-EBSD and Crystal Plasticity Study
papers.summary: Strain-rate-dependent deformation in spherical nanoindentation couples material rate sensitivity effects with the evolving contact radius, penetration depth and plastic-zone size. A rate-sensitive model where loading rate and indentation depth are prescribed independently allows their contributions to be disentangled. We study this in unirradiated and neutron-irradiated single-crystal tungsten, indented to the same final indentation strain at nominal strain-rates of 3.2e-5 to 3.2e-3 per second and reaching different final depths. Surface pile-up, residual lattice strain and dislocation distributions were measured by AFM and HR-EBSD. A rate-sensitive, strain-gradient crystal plasticity framework, incorporating thermally activated slip and irradiation hardening derived from measured defect populations, was calibrated at the highest strain rate and reproduced all these observables at the two lower strain rates without further parameter adjustment. The framework was then used to vary strain rate and depth independently. At fixed depth, strain rate over the experimental range changes the predicted peak load by < 1% and the pile-up by < 2 nm. At fixed strain rate, the experimental depth differences alone produce pile-up increases of ~ 90% and 130%, comparable to the measured 66% and 150% for unirradiated and irradiated tungsten. The measured differences between strain rate conditions therefore predominantly reflect the different depths reached; a 10% difference in final depth mimics more than an order of magnitude change in strain rate. Irradiation is seen to promote localisation, with its effect on pile-up increasing with depth up to ~ 500 nm, while remaining consistent with a common thermally activated deformation mechanism.

authors.name: Prashil S. Joshi, Bethany Jim, Chris Hardie, Angus Wilkinson, David EJ Armstrong, Suchandrima Das

papers.title: Inference Limits of Routine Cement Characterization for CEM I Performance: Evidence From a Multi-Producer Dataset
papers.summary: This study evaluates the prediction of 28-day compressive strength from routine cement characterization across independent producers. Industrial records from 23 European producers cover nearly three decades of testing in a single laboratory, encompassing 476 samples. The archive includes CEM I, CEM II, CEM III, and other blended cements, with the main analysis focused on CEM I. Chemistry and fineness descriptors were evaluated using linear and nonlinear models. Strength class and water demand were also examined as performance labels from standardized testing. Mean absolute errors in 28-day strength prediction were approximately 3 MPa, with linear models performing comparably to nonlinear models. Producer holdout tests assessed transfer to cements from producers excluded from training and yielded absolute errors of the same order. Equivalent alkali showed a consistent negative association with 28-day strength, with K$_2$O carrying most of this signal. Together, these results highlight the value of industrial data collected under common laboratory conditions for interpretable 28-day strength prediction, with potential to inform cement design targeting lower production costs and CO$_2$ emissions.

authors.name: Marchellino Ghorayeb, Christiane R\"o{\ss}ler, Horst-Michael Ludwig, Leon Herrmann, Stefan Kollmannsberger

papers.title: Dimensional crossover in ultradilute Bose-Bose liquid mixtures
papers.summary: We study ultradilute $^{39}$K Bose-Bose bulk mixtures and droplets in an external harmonic potential that confines them in one spatial direction towards the two-dimensional (2D) limit. Equations of state for several confinements are obtained with quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) at $T=0$, using interaction potentials that include information on the $s$-wave scattering length $a$ and the effective range $r_{\rm eff}$. Performing the calculations using two different interaction potential models we have determined the range of confinements for which equations of state are universal in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$. Based on the QMC equation of state, we develop a 2D QMC density functional for each confinement strength and use it together with the local density approximation to determine properties of the self-bound drops. For moderate squeezing, energies and droplet profiles obtained using the 2D QMC functional agree well with those obtained using 3D functionals, while offering a substantial reduction in computational cost, and a consistent approach in crossover to 2D. Noticeably, our results approach 2D mean-field (MF) + Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) predictions only for the most strongly confined systems for which universality in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ is observed. This implies a very narrow range of confinements for which 2D LHY functionals are applicable, which affects the study of vortices using 2D functionals.

authors.name: Leandra Vranje\v{s} Marki\'c, Ivan Popari\'c, Kre\v{s}imir D\v{z}elalija, Petar Stipanovi\'c, Jordi Boronat

papers.title: Updated Tkatchenko Scheffler method and assessment of dispersion methods for alkali-containing systems
papers.summary: The Tkatchenko-Scheffler (TS) pairwise method to calculate dispersion interactions is a widely used approach to incorporate missing long-range van der Waals contributions in semilocal and hybrid density functional calculations. Despite subsequent many-body extensions, this formulation remains widely used. In 2018, Fedorov et al. reported updated van der Waals radii to the seminal work published in 2009. The present work examines the accuracy of the TS method with updated van der Waals radii (TS_2018), coupled with the semilocal Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof density functional, for structural predictions of semiconducting and insulating materials. Special attention is paid to materials containing alkali elements, for which the TS_2009 method exhibits a large overbinding, associated with potentially large errors in predicted atomic structures. We also consider a narrower reformulation (TS_alkali) where only the the alkali atoms are corrected, so the method remains otherwise compatible with TS_2009. We compare these methods with a broader set of dispersion corrections--the DFT-D3 method, the exchange-hole dipole moment method, and the beyond-pairwise, nonlocal many-body dispersion method--for ionic and alkali-containing systems more generally. We examine equilibrium geometry predictions for 45 inorganic solid compounds as well as three Cs-containing halide perovskites, CsPb$X_3$ ($X$ = Cl, Br, I). Our results show that the updated van der Waals radii in the TS_2018 and TS_alkali methods resolve the overbinding that is present with TS_2009 in alkali-containing systems, bringing predictions into closer agreement with other dispersion methods. For the halide perovskites, method-dependent differences in predicted cell volumes and shapes persist, and no approach performs with perfect accuracy on all metrics for all three materials.

authors.name: Aaron M. Schankler, Ruyi Song, Sampreeti Bhattacharya, Ela Lucas, Lee Hampton III, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Yosuke Kanai, Volker Blum

papers.title: Spin-Chirality-Driven Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
papers.summary: The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.

authors.name: Dezhao Wu, Yong Xu, Meng Ye, Wenhui Duan

papers.title: EBSDmagus: Managing Multi-Stage Dynamical Electron Backscatter Diffraction Simulations
papers.summary: Dynamical electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) simulations increasingly support systematic studies of how material and experimental parameters affect diffraction patterns. Investigations that combine composition and crystal structure, including changes in atomic order, with accelerating voltage, temperature, and many orientations or detector conditions can require large sets of related calculations. Several packages provide dynamical EBSD simulation; we use the open-source, scriptable EMsoft programs because they are well suited to large studies on high-performance computing systems. An EMsoft investigation nevertheless spans separate configuration, structure, scattering, and orientation files and several dependent calculation stages. As variations multiply, manual preparation becomes difficult to check, interruptions obscure which results remain usable, and the origin of individual patterns becomes laborious to reconstruct. With EBSDmagus, researchers define fixed and varying parameters once. The software prepares the required EMsoft calculations, reuses compatible intermediate results, and checks that the generated files represent the requested investigation before execution. After execution, it checks the expected outputs and, following an interruption, resumes only unresolved calculations while preserving completed work. A portable run record links each output to its inputs and calculation history, providing the provenance needed when the results are deposited as findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) data. We assess this approach using a completed representative calculation, a larger study prepared and checked before submission, two observed cluster interruptions, and a controlled job cancellation. During recovery, EBSDmagus retained completed calculations and resubmitted only incomplete work.

authors.name: Ulrich Kerzel, Lukas Berners, Sanddra Korte-Kerzel

papers.title: High-pressure elastic properties of GeO2 polymorphs up to 120 GPa
papers.summary: We systematically investigated the phase stability, pressure dependence of the elastic properties, and elastic anisotropy of four GeO2 polymorphs: rutile-, CaCl2-, alpha-PbO2-, and pyrite-type phases using theoretical calculations based on density functional theory. The elastic constants were calculated at regular pressure intervals within the stability fields of each phase, as determined by static enthalpy calculations. We further employed a strain-coupled Landau free-energy expansion to describe the pressure evolution of the elastic response associated with the rutile- to CaCl2-type transition and elucidate the origin of the elastic softening near the transition. The rutile- to CaCl2-type phase transition is consistent with a Landau-type second-order transition. As the transition is approached, elastic softening develops in the rutile-type phase, resulting in anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk and shear moduli. The calculated elastic-wave anisotropy increases markedly near the transition, primarily due to the rapid reduction in shear-wave velocity, reaching a maximum of approximately 190% at 20 GPa. Following the transition, the anisotropy decreases sharply in the CaCl2-type phase and exhibits discontinuity at the CaCl2-type/alpha-PbO2-type phase boundary. The higher-pressure alpha-PbO2- and pyrite-type phases exhibit comparatively weak pressure dependence of anisotropy, with small discontinuities at their respective phase boundaries. The pyrite-type phase has the lowest anisotropy with AP = 4% and AS = 12% at 120 GPa, consistent with its high-symmetry cubic structure and nearly isotropic elastic-wave propagation.

authors.name: Gulshan Kumar, Sumit Ghosh, Sharad Babu Pillai, Rajkrishna Dutta

papers.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
papers.summary: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to achieve a specific local accuracy is only weakly dependent on the system size within the range of consideration. HPP provides a route toward linear-scaling electronic-structure calculations in which the computational effort for local observables can be matched to the required accuracy, offering an error-aware strategy for large-scale first-principles simulations.

authors.name: Tao Hu, Weiqing Zhou, Zhichang Fu, Yechen Chen, Shengjun Yuan

papers.title: Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network
papers.summary: Topological Deep Learning (TDL) is designed to learn features associated not only with nodes but also with edges, triangles and higher dimensional simplices. However, most TDL approaches, being based on boundary operators and Hodge Laplacians, have the limitation that features and signals cannot be lifted or lowered across more than one dimension per layer. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we propose the adoption of the cup and cap products. Specifically, we formulate the Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN), a topological deep learning architecture designed to learn node-based variables (or 0-cochains) by taking into account their many-body interactions (e.g. triangles) present in the data. We validate CCNN by assessing its performance on the TopoBench datasets, demonstrating its competitive performance with respect to other simplicial complex neural networks.

authors.name: Marta Niedostatek, Ferran Hernandez Caralt, Runyue Wang, Federica Baccini, Lorenzo Giambagli, Pietro Li\'o, Ginestra Bianconi

papers.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
papers.summary: We show that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph, generalizing the previously developed graph-theoretic framework for Markov networks. These representations yield asymptotic results, including the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.

authors.name: Julian Voits

papers.title: Microscopic Connection between Phonon Hall Viscosity and Acoustic Faraday Effect in Spin-Orbit-Coupled Magnets
papers.summary: The acoustic Faraday effect probes phonon Hall viscosity through the rotation of transverse acoustic polarization, conventionally interpreted in terms of circular birefringence. We show that magnetic order breaking rotational symmetry generates anisotropic phonon responses and elliptically polarized eigenmodes, so that Faraday rotation cannot be attributed to Hall viscosity alone. To elucidate their microscopic origin and consequences, we derive spin-strain couplings from a generic spin-orbit-coupled exchange model. We identify transverse strain couplings for propagation along the c-axis arising linearly from the changes in the bond-dependent interactions, along with strain-induced g-tensor contributions. Applying our theory to $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, we find that static strain responses modify the extraction of Hall viscosity from Faraday rotation, yielding a value significantly different from that inferred assuming rotational symmetry. Our results establish a microscopic connection between magnetic interaction, lattice dynamics, and phonon Hall viscosity in spin-orbit-coupled magnets.

authors.name: Antoine Matar, Haoting Xu, Hae-Young Kee

papers.title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction
papers.summary: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard global optimization methods. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory (EAT) into a genetic algorithm. HEAT combines EAT's continuous relaxation of atomic positions, species, and population with the global search capabilities of genetic algorithms. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing a 1150-atom interior region of twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ from experimental ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.

authors.name: Justin Tahmassebpur, Chia-Hao Lee, Crist\'obal M\'endez, Shake Karapetyan, Zixiao Shi, David A. Muller, Tom\'as Arias

papers.title: Layer-Parity Control of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Monolayer NbSe$_2$
papers.summary: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-$\mathbf Q$ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe$_2$. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which $C_3$ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}=0$ yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above $0.65$~meV at $0.58$~K. Magnetic layer parity thus selects between a helical and a trigonal diode channel. This trigonal channel provides a candidate intrinsic contribution to the field-free rectification reported in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$. The model predicts that two-sided out-of-plane proximity cancels it when antiparallel and, at the same exchange per layer, enhances it about fourfold when parallel, in the computed range.

authors.name: Yusuf Wicaksono, Toshikaze Kariyado

papers.title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum
papers.summary: We study a spinless $\pi$-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a $\Delta C=2$ chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle--hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. Finite odd-frequency correlations track holonomy and local splitting, while cylinder and ordinary-wall controls show that their presence is not specific to Klein gluing. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility, closed-surface seam spectra and finite correlations. The energy cost is evaluated for a fixed pairing background; neither a protected zero mode nor a self-consistent wall solution is claimed.

authors.name: Junhao (Eigen), Wang

papers.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
papers.summary: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.

authors.name: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

papers.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
papers.summary: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.

authors.name: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

papers.title: Why financial prices exhibit Brownian motion despite predictable order flow: An exactly solvable nonlinear price impact model
papers.summary: In econophysics, there are two enigmatic empirical laws of financial market microstructure: (i) the market-order flow has predictable persistence due to metaorder splitting by institutional investors, as formulated by the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model. However, this phenomenon seems paradoxical given the diffusive and unpredictable price dynamics. (ii) The price impact $I(Q_{\rm tot})$ of a large metaorder $Q_{\rm tot}$ follows the square-root law, $I(Q_{\rm tot})\propto \sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}$. In this Letter, we reveal why price dynamics follows Brownian motion despite predictable order flow by unifying these enigmas via an exactly solvable model. We generalize the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model to nonlinear price-impact dynamics, which is mapped to a solvable L\'evy-walk model. Our exact solution shows that the price dynamics remains diffusive under the square-root law, even under persistent order flow, reflecting the finite variance of metaorder impact; our model is thus a minimal representative of the universality class of nonlinear price-impact models with finite-variance metaorder impact. This work illustrates the crucial role of the square-root law in mitigating price movements by large metaorders, leading to Brownian price dynamics, consistent with the efficient market hypothesis over long timescales.

authors.name: Yuki Sato, Shunta Fujiwara, Kiyoshi Kanazawa

papers.title: Fractional Quantum Hall States: Infinite Matrix Product Representation and its Implications
papers.summary: We present a novel matrix product representation of the Laughlin and related fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions based on a rigorous version of the correlators of a chiral quantum field theory. This representation enables the quantitative control of the coefficients of the Laughlin wavefunction times an arbitrary monomial symmetric polynomial when expanded in a Slater determinant or permanent basis. It renders the properties, such as factorization and the renewal structure, inherent in such fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions transparent. We prove bounds on the correlators of the chiral quantum field theory and utilize this representation to demonstrate the exponential decay of connected correlations and a gap in the entanglement spectrum on a thin cylinder.

authors.name: Severin Schraven, Simone Warzel

papers.title: Parisi formula and large deviations for mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
papers.summary: We consider convex mean-field vector spin glasses perturbed by a general Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, where $m_N$ is a bounded vector-valued empirical average and $G$ is continuous. We prove a Parisi-type variational formula for the limiting quenched free energy and a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$, both at every temperature. The approach is simple and modular: the only model-specific spin-glass input is the variational formula for every linear tilt of $m_N$ together with differentiability of the resulting free energy. The classical G\"artner--Ellis, Varadhan, and Bryc transfers then treat an arbitrary continuous $G$. Thus the same argument applies to a broad class of empirical observables and Mattis potentials, without a separate constrained-free-energy calculation for each model. As a scalar specialization, the framework contains the Gaussian spin-glass surrogate used in mismatched rank-one matrix estimation.

authors.name: Hong-Bin Chen, Victor Issa

papers.title: High-temperature free energy for non-convex mean-field spin glasses with Mattis interactions
papers.summary: We study enriched mean-field vector spin glasses whose covariance function need not be convex. In a quantitative short-time regime, corresponding to sufficiently high temperature in the usual physical parameterization, we prove convergence of the quenched free energy to the differentiable solution of a infinite-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equation proposed for non-convex models. We identify that solution through its characteristics and a unique fixed point. The argument does not assume replica symmetry. We then allow a general continuous Mattis interaction $N G(m_N)$, obtain the corresponding variational formula, and prove a quenched large deviation principle for $m_N$. As an explicit application, we treat a bipartite model with Mattis fields, which is closely related to the Restricted Boltzmann Machine. The application requires neither a replica-symmetry assumption nor ellipticity or Nishimori identities; its restriction is the same quantitative high-temperature condition as in the general theorem.

authors.name: Hong-Bin Chen, Victor Issa

papers.title: Task-Aware Bitrate Thresholds for Codec-Robust Ultrasound Segmentation
papers.summary: Remote robot surgery and tele-ultrasound increasingly rely on real-time streaming under strict bandwidth constraints, making lossy compression unavoidable. Since the receiving end of these clinical pipelines is increasingly a machine rather than a human observer, codec selection must be guided by downstream task accuracy rather than perceptual fidelity. We evaluate three widely deployed codecs, H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1, on prostate ultrasound segmentation, reporting task-aware compression performance with region overlap (Dice) and boundary accuracy (HD95) as the quality metrics. To compare codecs fairly, we match their operating points at a common perceptual-quality (SSIM) level. We establish, per codec, the lowest bitrate that preserves acceptable segmentation accuracy, reporting the 5th-percentile Dice alongside the mean to expose worst-case degradation. All three codecs preserve segmentation quality (mean Dice $\geq$ 0.84) down to approximately 0.07-0.20 bits per voxel (bpv). Below this point, AV1's accuracy declines gradually, while H.264's drops sharply. As a result, H.264 needs 82% more bitrate than AV1 to reach the same region-overlap accuracy (Dice), and 104.7% more to reach the same boundary accuracy (HD95).

authors.name: Alireza Siyavashi, Arman Shirzad, Christian Herglotz

papers.title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
papers.summary: Background and Objective: Bridging kidney MRI with patient-specific computational biomechanics may enable accurate, noninvasive assessment of chronic kidney disease. To develop a finite element method (FEM)-based computational elastography framework for estimating renal biomechanical properties from conventional kidney MRI and to evaluate its ability to differentiate chronic kidney disease (CKD) from healthy controls. Methods: Kidney segmentation masks from healthy control and CKD subjects were converted into triangulated surface meshes, and watertight surfaces were tetrahedralized to create volumetric FEM meshes. Kidney tissue was modeled as a nearly incompressible Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic material. Harmonic wave propagation simulations were performed using FEM, followed by Helmholtz-based elastographic inversion to estimate complex shear modulus distributions. Derived biomechanical parameters were used for CKD classification using machine learning models. Results: FEM-derived stiffness estimates showed consistency with stiffness ranges previously reported in human renal MRE studies and also showed measurable differences between healthy and CKD groups. Machine learning models trained on FEM-derived features achieved classification performance up to 86.26% cross-validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.92. Conclusion: FEM-derived elastographic parameters showed potential for distinguishing CKD from healthy tissue and may provide an alternative for renal biomechanical assessment without dedicated MRE acquisition.

authors.name: A. Bhattacharjee, M. M. Rahman, A. Srivastava, E. H. Bhuiyan

papers.title: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements
papers.summary: Distance based formation control fixes the shape of a robot team but leaves its position and orientation unconstrained. We regulate all three for differential drive robots that have only one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body frame relative position measurements, and communication with their neighbors. We derive a two layer estimation control scheme directly from optimization. The first half of the result is a set of graph-proximal estimators that reconstruct the centroid, the anchor vector, and the centered coordinates. Exact proximal updates reach consensus in finitely many steps, and a finite number of primal dual iterations leaves a bounded reconstruction error. The controller combines proximal centroid and orientation steps with distance gradient shape regulation, and a finite rotation removes the orientation drift caused by the shape step. A discrete Lyapunov analysis gives local exponential convergence once the estimators have converged. We validate the method in ROS 2 Gazebo and in experiments with five physical robots.

authors.name: Thanacha Choopojcharoen, Erman Selim, Ramisha Anjum, Baris Fidan

papers.title: A Particle-Based Multiuser Communication with a Budget Limit
papers.summary: Multiuser networks can aggregate local observations through a shared receiver. In this paper, we study the particle budget required to recover the exact sum of binary inputs in a multiuser network. We show that, for the considered model, the minimum budget grows quadratically with the number of transmitters when the symbol duration and target error probability are fixed, even when the receiver observes all particle arrival times. Simultaneous on-off keying (OOK) achieves this quadratic scaling, while any slower budget growth makes the error probability approach one at a fixed symbol duration, regardless of the transmission and decoding scheme. We then examine how this particle requirement can be reduced by allowing longer symbol durations and more counting intervals. We develop a groupwise OOK counting (GOC) scheme with staggered group releases and sequential estimation of group input sums, accounting for delayed arrivals. Our bounds show that, when reception is based on interval counts, reducing the quadratic scaling requires both the symbol duration and the number of counting intervals to grow with network size. When both grow in proportion to network size, the minimum budget becomes proportional to the number of transmitters times its logarithm.

authors.name: Shaojie Zhang, Ozgur B. Akan

papers.title: State-Feedback Passivity Control for Synchronous Machine Systems
papers.summary: The passivity of a generating station enables network stability to be established from conditions verified locally at each station. For synchronous machines, however, passivity can only be certified under conditions on the operating point, and these conditions fail under heavy loading and weak damping. This paper develops a state-feedback controller that enforces passivity using a storage battery connected at the terminal bus. A bilinear term arising from the product of the rotor-speed and stator-current deviations is treated as a bounded uncertainty, leading to robust positive-real conditions that can be enforced by a state feedback control designed using a single algebraic Riccati equation. The resulting controller guarantees passivity whenever the Riccati equation admits a positive-definite solution, with no separate condition on the operating point. Numerical examples show that existing conditions certify passivity only up to a fraction of the rated current, whereas the proposed state-feedback approach certifies it at the rated operating point of the machine.

authors.name: Maryam Khodabakhshloo, Elizabeth L. Ratnam, Ian R. Petersen

papers.title: Few-Shot Beam Selection for Embodied AI via In-Context Learning and Conformal Prediction
papers.summary: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications are essential for supporting massive multimodal sensory data exchange in Embodied Artificial Intelligence (EAI) systems. However, fast and reliable beam selection for mmWave communication remains a critical bottleneck due to the prohibitive overhead associated with conventional beam training. Although location-aided beam prediction offers a promising alternative, its performance is often limited by localization errors and the need for extensive training data. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework termed In-Context Learning driven Cross-Validation Conformal Prediction (ICL+CVCP) for beam prediction. The proposed framework utilizes the training-free adaptation capability of ICL, enabling effective operation with only a small number of demonstration samples and eliminating the need for large-scale data collection and model fine-tuning. In addition, the CVCP module constructs compact, distribution-free candidate beam sets that provably contain the optimal beam with a user-defined probability. Experimental results confirm that ICL+CVCP consistently satisfies the desired empirical coverage while significantly reducing pilot overhead and computational latency, thereby meeting the stringent reliability and efficiency requirements of EAI applications.

authors.name: Weicao Deng, Ruihan Li, Feihang Xu, Min Li

papers.title: A Novel BVH-accelerated Dynamic Ray-Tracing Channel Model for Vehicular Communication Systems
papers.summary: Accurate and efficient channel modeling is critical for evaluating the sixth-generation (6G) networks, while dynamic ray-tracing (DRT) remains bottlenecked by its reliance on channel coherence time. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel bounding volume hierarchy-accelerated DRT (BVH-DRT), which introduces a mechanism shift from a time-driven update in DRT to a spatial-driven update. The proposed channel model clusters complex scatterers using the BVH method as pre-processing to establish a geometric coherence distance guided by transceiver kinematics, so that the ray update intervals in BVH-DRT can be autonomously adjusted to reduce the complexity. Furthermore, the non-stationary channel impulse responses are generated to evaluate delay-Doppler (DD) domain waveforms, including orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) and orthogonal delay-Doppler division multiplexing (ODDM). Validations in vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) scenarios demonstrate that BVH-DRT achieves spatial-temporal consistency with measurements and commercial software while significantly enhancing computational efficiency. Additionally, bit error rate (BER) evaluation highlights the severe impact of high-dynamic channels on waveform performance. The proposed framework is important for designing reliable communications and robust sensing in 6G networks.

authors.name: Songjiang Yang, Cheng-Xiang Wang, Yinghua Wang, Chen Wang, Jie Huang, Yunfei Chen

papers.title: A Framework for Guaranteed Active Fault Diagnosis with Applications to Aircraft Systems
papers.summary: Within the multiple-model framework, active fault diagnosis applies auxiliary control input signals to ex?cite the system such that fault modes are distinguishable. For aircraft systems, it has been pointed out by some rele?vant works that certain faults cannot be effectively detected and isolated in time without actively exciting the aircraft dynamics. However, existing works have not simultane?ously addressed the optimal auxiliary control design with theoretical guarantees and the FDI method with an effective mechanism for triggering the active fault diagnosis. Hence, we are motivated to propose a framework of active FDI for aircraft systems to explicitly address the aforementioned issue. Specifically, we first formulate a receding-horizon FDI scheme for estimating the likelihood of candidate fault modes with proved effectiveness, and then we propose a method for estimating mode probabilities, based on which a mechanism is designed for triggering auxiliary control for active fault diagnosis. The auxiliary control signal design is formulated such that the effectiveness for FDI is theoret?ically guaranteed and the disruption to nominal flight oper?ation is minimized. Numerical test results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

authors.name: Dawei Sun, Daochun Li, Koffi M. D. Motchon, Haoyuan Shao, Jinwu Xiang

papers.title: Distributed Robust Model Predictive Control for Optimal Consensus of Unknown Multiagent Systems with Event-Triggered Communication
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the optimal consensus problem for multiagent systems with unknown dynamics. We propose a robust model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes the control input and consensus sequences while enforcing state and input constraints. Within this framework, noisy offline data are used to construct nominal prediction models and quantify the associated uncertainty, which is explicitly incorporated into the robust MPC design. To solve the resulting optimization problem at each MPC update with reduced inter-agent communication, we develop a distributed gradient-projection alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm with an event-triggered information exchange mechanism and establish its convergence to the optimal solution. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are established to guarantee robust constraint satisfaction and practical consensus of the closed-loop multiagent system. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

authors.name: Shiyue Jia, Nan Bai, Dawei Shi, Ling Shi

papers.title: A Novel Asymmetric Distributed Voltage Regulation Scheme to Enhance the Utilization of Distributed Energy Resources
papers.summary: Passive voltage regulation in distribution grids using distributed energy resources (DERs) is becoming the standard for feeder voltage management in both under-voltage and over-voltage scenarios. Their simple control, ease of implementation, and fast response make them ideal for distribution feeders with high-DER penetration. This paper proposes a novel distributed voltage control for DERs based on the voltage at the point of common coupling, inverter rating, and operating active power. The proposed control is designed to utilize feeder inverters efficiently to reduce the burden on the inverters in both under-voltage and over-voltage operations and increase the fairness in reactive power ($Q$) support in over-voltage operations. The proposed control is implemented in static and dynamic simulations of a real feeder to validate the performance. Results for the under-voltage scenario are also presented in the paper.

authors.name: Madhura Sondharangalla, Dan Moldovan, Raja Ayyanar

papers.title: Safe Output-Regulation Flows for Constrained Optimization via Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Control-theoretic approaches to constrained optimization have been widely studied by interpreting optimization algorithms as dynamical systems. This paper formulates constrained optimization as an output-regulation problem with state constraints, where equality-constraint residuals are treated as regulated outputs and inequality constraints as state constraints. Proportional--integral feedback is employed to drive the equality-constraint residuals asymptotically to zero, while a control barrier function (CBF) safety filter is used to ensure inequality safety throughout the optimization process. We establish feasibility of the CBF filtering program throughout the inequality-feasible set and local exponential convergence of the resulting flow. Under stronger global conditions, we further prove convergence from an entire connected component of the inequality-feasible set. Since exact implementation of the flow requires solving a CBF quadratic program at each state, we further develop a flow that approximates the CBF solution through multiplier updates. Moreover, we provide a unified formulation encompassing the two proposed flows and projected primal--dual dynamics. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence, safety, and computational tradeoffs of the proposed flows.

authors.name: Zihao Ren, Bingqi Liu, Lei Wang, Hongye Su, Guodong Shi

papers.title: A Unified Multi-Encoder Framework for Music Lyric Intelligibility Assessment: Bridging Invasive and Non-Invasive Paradigms
papers.summary: Lyric intelligibility significantly impacts music engagement and comprehension, especially for hearing-impaired individuals. Existing speech intelligibility metrics perform poorly in musical contexts due to differences in prosody, timing, and spectral dynamics. We propose a unified multi-encoder framework that supports both invasive and non-invasive modeling for robust lyric intelligibility prediction. By capturing complementary local acoustic-semantic alignments, global musical semantics, and ASR-derived textual cues, our method achieves superior performance over baselines on the ICASSP 2026 Cadenza dataset, with the best model achieving 26.61 RMSE, a $9.2$\% improvement over the baseline, demonstrating its flexibility and robustness.

authors.name: Jing Yang, Shenghao Liao, Shuqing Zhang, Yongyi Deng, Pan Li, Zerui Han, Gongping Huang

papers.title: Simulation Modeling and Control of an Elastic Shaping Antagonistic Variable Stiffness Actuator
papers.summary: Position--stiffness regulation of antagonistic variable stiffness actuators (VSAs) involves coupled nonlinear dynamics, parameter uncertainty, and feedback states that are not directly measured. This paper addresses this challenge through a simulation-based workflow that integrates elastic shaping, model verification, and layered nonlinear control. This study builds on a previously developed actuator comprising two crossed four-bar compliant transmission elastic units. Its optimized elastic mapping provides the structural basis, with an ADAMS torque-curve root mean square error (RMSE) of $2.57\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm}$ against the target. A control-oriented analytical model is implemented in Simulink and compared with the independently executed ADAMS model under matched inputs. The maximum joint-angle RMSE across the tested cases is $4.66\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{rad}$. A layered controller combines extended Kalman filtering for state reconstruction, feedback linearization for nominal decoupling, and adaptive sliding-mode control for residual compensation. At the end of the nominal simulation, the joint-angle error is approximately $3.14\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad}$. The stiffness error is $3.07\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm/rad}$ relative to a target of $50\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm/rad}$. Parameter-variation and ablation tests assess tracking performance and the effects of the controller modules within the evaluated conditions. The resulting workflow links structural-response modeling, state estimation, and robust control assessment, supporting repeatable comparisons beyond nominal tracking alone.

authors.name: Yuanlong Ji, Ruizhe Jiang, Dongrun Jin, Xiangyu Xie, Junheng Lin, Xingbang Yang

papers.title: Sharp Minimum-Rate Guarantees for Power-Based Discrete RIS Design
papers.summary: We characterise when desired-power optimisation guarantees the minimum user rate (MUR) in discrete reconfigurable intelligent surface systems with fixed precoding. For the weighted sum of desired powers, a bounded channel exists whose exact maximiser starves a user: no positive guarantee exists. For the minimum desired power, the retained fraction of the optimal MUR is at least a sharp constant set by the phase's power quality and residual interference. A semidefinite dual certifies it without enumerating phases. Minimum-power phases keep 88% of the optimum under weak reflection and about half under strong reflection; omitted interference causes most of the loss.

authors.name: Hernan X. Cordova

papers.title: FUSEMOS: Perceptual Evaluation of Text-to-Music Generation with Dual-Encoder Fusion and Ranking-Aware Composite Loss
papers.summary: Perceptual evaluation of generated music is essential for developing text-to-music (TTM) generation systems. Existing automatic music perceptual evaluation methods rely solely on the contrastive language audio pretraining (CLAP) model to extract both audio and text features for predicting human-annotated mean opinion scores (MOS), particularly for overall musical impression (OMI) and textual alignment (TA). However, CLAP is limited in capturing fine-grained musical attributes such as timbre and expressiveness \emph{etc}. To address this, we propose FUSEMOS, a dual-encoder fusion framework that integrates CLAP with MERT, a self-supervised model pretrained on large scale music audio, to better capture both high level semantic alignment and detailed musical characteristics for more accurate OMI and TA estimation. Furthermore, to overcome the limitations of conventional regression losses in measuring human preferred relative ranking of music segments, we design a novel ranking-aware composite loss function. Experiments conducted on the MusicEval benchmark demonstrate that our approach outperforms the existing SOTA methods in both mean squared error and rank correlation metrics by a large margin.

authors.name: Jing Yang, Haoyu Wang, Ningning Pan, Zhao Wang, Jianxuan Yang, Gongping Huang

papers.title: dynamicalnodes: Block Diagrams to ROS2 Graphs
papers.summary: Here we introduce dynamicalnodes, a framework for rapid iterative prototyping of control and estimation algorithms within the Robot Operating System, or ROS. The framework leverages the theory of discrete-time dynamical systems to encode each component of a feedback system (e.g. reference generator, controller, plant, observer) as a pair of functions, denoted $(f,\,h) $, where $f$ is an evolution function and $h$ is an output function. With appropriate choice of domain and codomain, the $ (f,\,h) $ pairs can be composed to form feedback systems of arbitrary complexity. Moving from theory to practice, the user implements each $(f,\,h)$ pair in Python and encapsulates them in objects that facilitate composition and simulation. ROS executables are generated from these objects via rclpy, where relevant metadata such as network topology and publishing frequency are written automatically. The final result is a collection of rclpy files from which validated feedback systems can be spun up as live ROS graphs. We discuss the relevant theory behind the framework and then demonstrate the prototyping workflow applied to a canonical controls problem, a car with cruise control.

authors.name: Nehal Singh Mangat, Humberto Ramos, Floris van Breugel

papers.title: When Does Inter-BS Interference Hurt Sensing in ISAC? An Exact Fisher Information Analysis under Finite-Alphabet Interference
papers.summary: In networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), a base station (BS) performing sensing using its own downlink signals is subject to interference from the downlink transmissions of neighboring BSs. This paper investigates the impact of the signal constellation and waveform on the sensing performance in the presence of such inter-BS interference. For any linear receiver, we show that the mean-squared cross-ambiguity between two random ISAC signals is invariant to the modulation bases and constellations. We then derive the exact Fisher information under finite-alphabet interference with a flat-fading link, which equals the interference-free Fisher information scaled by $1-\gamma\,\mmse_{\C}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ denotes the interference-to-noise ratio (INR) and $\mmse_{\C}$ is the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) in estimating an interfering data symbol from its noise-corrupted observation at the sensing receiver. Consequently, Gaussian interference is the worst case and corresponds to the CRB loss of the matched filtering, whereas finite-alphabet interference induces a non-monotonic CRB loss that peaks at intermediate INR and vanishes at high INR. The loss is waveform-independent for the flat-fading BS-BS link, and an expectation-maximization (EM) interference-cancellation receiver approaches the theoretical bound for delay estimation.

authors.name: Kawon Han, Kaitao Meng, Fan Liu, Christos Masouros

papers.title: Re-Planning Budgets under Admission Control in Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access
papers.summary: Reordering low-Earth-orbit (LEO) beam-hopping visits can reduce grant-free update delivery even when each region receives the same service time. We derive the largest limit on inter-frame position changes that meets a prescribed delivery-rate loss tolerance when every group is visited once per frame. The guarantee concerns a protected beam's spatially averaged long-run delivery rate relative to optimized periodic service under exogenous re-planning. Fixed admission can favor irregular visits, whereas admission optimized for each revisit interval makes the per-visit reward concave under sufficient conditions on transmission success. Periodic service is then optimal at a fixed mean interval. The shortest and longest allowed intervals determine the exact worst-case loss, attained by feasible alternating visit orders that respect every group's displacement limit. The resulting budget requires no estimate of the revisit-interval distribution and extends to independent stationary renewal updates. In a collision example with 40 groups and 40 resources per slot, increasing the loss tolerance from zero to 1% raises the limit from 17 to 24 positions.
