With independent priorities, the latter retains over 90% of the priority-weighted waiting-cost reduction achieved by unrestricted ordering. Received-power simulations under Rayleigh fading support the predicted loss.

authors.name: Joon-Young Park, Young-Chai Ko

papers.title: Auditory and Visual Virtualization in 6DoF XR: Effects on Plausibility and Dynamic Auditory Distance Perception
papers.summary: Extended reality (XR) enables controlled yet naturalistic multisensory experiments, but its validity depends on whether virtualized cues are perceptually plausible and lead to behavior comparable to the real world. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to perceptually evaluate a six-degree-of-freedom (6DoF) XR system that combines real-time room acoustic simulation, binaural rendering, and an audio-visually matched virtual replica of a large laboratory room in terms of both plausibility and behavior. In two experiments with 45 participants, we investigated how auditory and visual virtualization affect plausibility and dynamic auditory distance perception (ADP). A plausibility experiment compared real and virtual sound sources in audio-augmented reality (AAR) and virtual reality (VR), while a locomotion-based ADP experiment assessed distance-judgment accuracy, signed error, and task effort across four virtualization conditions. The system produced plausible binaural rendering in both AAR and VR, with higher plausibility in VR, indicating that perceptual requirements for XR audio depend on the visual reference frame. In the ADP task, any form of virtualization reduced accuracy and increased effort, although performance remained high overall. Virtual audio produced a bias toward nearer perceived source distances, whereas visual-only virtualization reduced accuracy without a significant directional bias. These effects did not add up in full VR. Overall, the findings demonstrate the strong potential of current 6DoF XR systems for interactive perceptual research, while revealing that task-specific behavioral validation may be necessary.

authors.name: Johannes M. Arend, Christian Scheer, Melissa Ram\'irez, Stefan Weinzierl, Fabian Brinkmann

papers.title: A Conformal Transmit-Reflect Array Enabling Multifunctional Bidirectional Beam Switching for Emergency Communication System
papers.summary: This article presents a conformal transmit-reflect array (CTRA) that enables bidirectional multibeam switching through a single metasurface aperture for emergency communication applications. To realize reconfigurable bidirectional beam switching, a transmit-reflect integrated element (TRIE) is developed by combining a polarization-selective transmissive structure with a complementary-symmetric reflective structure. The proposed element enables independent control of the cross-polarized transmission and reflection phases while exhibiting stable performance under oblique incidence. To support practical conformal implementations, a geometrical-optics-based phase compensation method is applied to cylindrical geometries, enabling effective wavefront control across the conformal aperture. By incorporating a polarization-switchable feed array (PSFA), multifunctional beam switching is achieved in the forward, backward, and bidirectional operating modes. The PSFA is configured as a nonuniform curved linear array near the focal region, enabling feed-selective beam switching within $\pm 30^\circ$ in both the $+z$ and $-z$ directions through selective excitation of the corresponding feed elements. The full-wave simulation results agree well with the measurements. The proposed CTRA achieves peak gains of 24.1 and 24.8 dBi in the forward and backward modes, respectively. The maximum aperture efficiencies in the forward and backward operating states are 28.4$\%$ and 33.4$\%$. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed CTRA, making it a promising candidate for adaptive emergency communication systems.

authors.name: Yifei Liu, Fan Qin, Chao Gu, Wenchi Cheng, Steven Gao

papers.title: Joint Flexible Beamforming, Resource Allocation, and Task Buffering for Movable-Antenna Enabled MEC Systems
papers.summary: The proliferation of computation-intensive applications, such as generative artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy services, demands mobile edge computing (MEC) systems that are both energy-efficient and adaptable to highly dynamic workloads. However, conventional MEC architectures rely on fixed-position antennas with limited spatial flexibility and rigid single-slot task execution models, which fail to accommodate bursty traffic and time-varying channels. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel MEC framework empowered by movable antennas (MAs) and task buffering. Unlike traditional approaches, our system enables continuous antenna repositioning to maximize array gains and decouples task generation from immediate execution via buffer queues, allowing for flexible multi-slot scheduling. We formulate a stochastic optimization problem to minimize long-term energy consumption by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, MA positions, and computing resources. Leveraging Lyapunov optimization, we transform the long-term problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and develop an efficient alternating optimization algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of energy consumption, while maintaining stable task queues under unpredictable traffic conditions.

authors.name: Hao Wang, Chunjie Wang, Lingtong Ma, Wenchao Liu, Kan Yu, Jinke Ren, Yanyan Shen, Xuhui Zhang

papers.title: SVM + CFAR + OR: A Hybrid Machine-Learning-CFAR Receiver for Low-False-Alarm PRACH Preamble Detection in 5G NR and Beyond
papers.summary: The physical random access channel (PRACH) enables initial access between user equipment and the base station, making reliable preamble detection essential for cellular networks. Growing device density in 5G and beyond-5G networks, massive machine-type communication, and the shift towards machine-learning-driven radio interfaces challenge conventional analytical detectors, particularly in complex radio environments and at low signal-to-noise ratios. This article formulates preamble detection as a 64-class classification problem and introduces two model-agnostic contributions: a robust adaptive threshold implementing the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) principle in the classifier decision-score domain (MAD-CFAR), and a hybrid receiver combining a learned detector with a conventional power-delay-profile CFAR detector through a logical OR rule. The learned branch is evaluated using two models trained on the same GPU-generated dataset: a support vector machine (SVM) with principal component analysis and a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN). On a held-out test set, the SVM achieves 98.58% accuracy (macro-AUC 0.9991), while the CNN reaches 99.29% accuracy (macro-AUC 1.0000) at lower inference cost and memory footprint. MAD-CFAR reduces the learned branch's false alarm rate to near zero on the noise calibration campaign. The OR hybrid retains the analytical detector's low, standard-compliant false alarm rate while extending detection capability. Across six propagation channels and 258 conformance-style tests, the SVM-based hybrid improves low-SNR sensitivity by several decibels without increasing missed detections relative to the analytical detector. Under the same false alarm constraint, the CNN is competitive in some channels but currently trails the SVM in high-delay-spread multipath conditions.

authors.name: Filip Ferenc, Michal Szczachor

papers.title: A Cost-Effective Submodule with Fault-Blocking Capability for Modular Multilevel Converters
papers.summary: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has become an attractive technology for high-power electronics applications thanks to its high energy efficiency, high power rating, high modularity, flexible scalability, and superior output waveform quality. It has attracted considerable research attention, and numerous submodule (SM) variants have been developed for different objectives. Among them, the half-bridge SM (HBSM) is the most widely adopted thanks to its simplicity, but it cannot interrupt DC-side short-circuit currents. Various SM topologies with fault-blocking capability have been proposed. These SM topologies contain additional switches and passive components compared to the HBSM, leading to higher capital and operating costs. Aiming at these issue, an SM topology capable to block DC-side fault-currents with a reduced component count is proposed in this paper. The proposed SM includes two variants, one employs only two fully-controlled switches. An operation and control scheme for the proposed SM are also developed and presented in the paper. The functionality of the proposed SM is validated by experiment, and the value of the SM is demonstrated through a test simulation for an high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) transmission system.

authors.name: Yu Liu, Shengbo Zhang

papers.title: Towards Track Height Control in Additive Manufacturing on Porous Substrates: An Approach for System Identification and Controller Selection
papers.summary: Additive manufacturing is transforming the creation of materials and parts, enabling the design and manufacturing of multifunctional parts with tailored properties. One compelling example is the combination of a porous core and a non-porous surface, which offers significant advantages in terms of weight reduction, material efficiency, strength and wear resistance. Directed Energy Deposition (DED) processes enable the transition from porous core to non-porous part surface by closing the pores. However, the surface-layer of porous substrates presents a substantial challenge to achieving consistent track heights during DED, directly impacting the final part geometry and performance. Therefore, precise control of the deposition process is crucial for realising the full potential of the multifunctional parts. In order to address this challenge, this work presents a conceptual approach for track height control during Laser-based Directed Energy Deposition (DED-LB) on porous substrates. First, the DED-LB process and the associated measurement setup are explained, along with a discussion of their limitations. The focus then shifts to the control problem, beginning with system identification to characterise the process dynamics. Subsequently, a selection of control strategies is investigated, as well as their compatibility with the process. This research provides a foundational step toward reliable additive manufacturing on porous substrates, and thus toward producing multifunctional parts.

authors.name: Amelie Schatull, Torge Kolditz, Simon Kleinschmidt, Annika Raatz, J\"org Seewig

papers.title: Copula-Based Dependence Modeling for Resilient 6G Multi-Hop Wireless Networks
papers.summary: Reliable operation of multi-hop wireless networks requires accounting for statistical dependence among link failures caused by common propagation conditions and shared network components. This paper develops a copula-based framework for modeling node-induced dependence among link-level signal-to-noise ratios and quantifying its effect on end-to-end outage. By separating marginal fading distributions from the dependence structure, the framework captures nonlinear and tail-dependent coupling beyond conventional correlation-based models. Exact outage expressions are derived for primary-backup configurations involving edge-disjoint paths and paths with shared links. We then characterize the conditional outage probability of each candidate backup path given a primary-path failure, jointly accounting for node-induced dependence and shared-link failures. In high-reliability regimes, we derive a first-order score that decomposes conditional outage into terms associated with marginal path outage, shared links, and node-induced dependence, enabling efficient dependence-aware backup-path selection. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the first-order and exact selection rules identify the same backup path. Numerical results validate the analysis and show that copula families with the same Kendall's $\tau$ can yield markedly different outage behavior because of their different tail-dependence properties. In particular, lower-tail dependence and path overlap can substantially reduce redundancy gains and reverse rankings based only on marginal outage probability.

authors.name: Ali Izadimoein, Prathapasinghe Dharmawansa, Nurul Huda Mahmood, Eduard Axel Jorswieck

papers.title: Uplink Enhancement for Low-Altitude UAVs via Active RISs Under Existing Cellular Infrastructure
papers.summary: The proliferation of low-altitude aerial Internet of Things applications, such as UAV-based sensing/monitoring, demands high-performance uplinks, yet terrestrial-optimized cellular networks with downtilted base station (BS) antennas form coverage holes that severely degrade aerial uplink. To address this challenge without modifying infrastructure, active reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are introduced. Unlike existing studies with complicated active RIS optimizations, we conduct a detailed noise analysis to simplify the transmission design. By deploying one active RIS per BS sector to fully exploit multi-sector reception, we develop a joint sector maximal signal combining scheme that improves signal quality through diversity gain. Active RISs introduce amplifier noise, raising questions about their net benefit. We derive an upper bound on the power ratio between RIS-introduced noise and BS-inherent noise, revealing that the impact of RIS noise is negligible under typical operating conditions. Based on this insight, we maximize a derived lower bound of the received signal-to-noise ratio by sequentially designing the amplitude and phase of reflection coefficients with closed-form expressions. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis on negligible RIS-introduced noise in typical systems and demonstrate that under the same array gain, a larger RIS size rather than a higher reflection gain is preferred for enhancing the low-altitude uplink transmission.

authors.name: Weicong Chen, Chao-Kai Wen, Wankai Tang, Yiping Zuo, Xiao Li, Shi Jin

papers.title: Data-driven current control of modular multilevel converter-based HVDC transmission system
papers.summary: Model-based design (MBD) is a mature framework for designing the current controllers of modular multilevel converters (MMCs) in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems. In MBD, linear state-space models are preferred for their good trade-off between accurate dynamics prediction and simplicity. However, first-principle derivations often neglect relevant MMC dynamics, which can hinder controller performance. Data-driven (DD) methods can deliver less biased models that capture parameter uncertainties, control-loop interactions, and grid dynamics, yet they remain under-exploited for controlling MMC currents. This paper studies DD current control method based on integral Subspace Predictive Control (iSPC), synthesized directly from input--output data measured in a high fidelity real-time digital simulator (RTDS), and proposes an initial guideline outlining the main steps for its systematic application to MMC current control. The proposed iSPC is compared against state-of-the-art DD solution, and the findings are validated through simulation studies in MATLAB/Simulink.

authors.name: Victor D. Reyes Dreke, Rahul Rane, Aleksandra Leki\'c

papers.title: Generalized Frequency-Domain Stability Analysis Formulation for Multi-Terminal HVDC Systems
papers.summary: The integration of offshore wind farms (OWFs) and the interconnection of different transmission networks are key drivers for multi-terminal DC (MTDC) systems. Bipolar high-voltage direct current (HVDC) employing dedicated metallic return (DMR) are attractive due to their increased availability, which co-exist with monopolar and rigid bipole configurations. While existing works focus on symmetric operation and particular configurations, we present a unified framework for MTDC stability analysis valid for both symmetric and asymmetric conditions. The formulation uses the minimum number of variables without loss of information, and combines the analytical network representation with black-box converter models, thereby enabling sensitivity studies. In addition, a closed-form expression guiding the stability improvement is presented, which requires minimal data exchange between involved parties. The framework is demonstrated on several case studies of increasing complexity, which highlight the importance of considering intra-station converter couplings and possible uncertainty of network parameters.

authors.name: Francisco J. Cifuentes Garcia, Thomas Roose, Luis M\"uller, Jef Beerten

papers.title: Fast and Convergent Alternating GPI Precoding for Self-Backhauled Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose a precoding framework for an integrated satellite terrestrial self-backhauled (ISTS) system, where a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite transmits a backhaul stream to an earth station (ES), and the ES forwards its payload to the base station (BS) serving the users. We formulate a user sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem subject to a self-backhaul constraint, which ensures that the user data forwarded by the BS do not exceed the data delivered to the ES. We then reformulate the resulting non-convex precoding problem into a form amenable to generalized power iteration (GPI). The GPI update is reinterpreted as projected preconditioned gradient ascent, revealing that its fixed step size may cause overshooting and non-monotonic behavior. Building on this interpretation, we first develop an alternating convergent GPI (AC-GPI), in which the fixed step is replaced by an Armijo backtracking rule, and show that a single Armijo-accepted step per block already guarantees sufficient ascent. This leads to the fast alternating convergent GPI (FAC-GPI), which performs one Armijo-accepted satellite update followed by one BS update in every round. Unlike existing backtracking-based GPI methods, whose convergence has not been established, we establish finite backtracking termination, monotone ascent, convergence to stationary points, along with a global stationarity-rate guarantee. Simulation results demonstrate stable and fast convergence as well as performance gains over existing methods.

authors.name: Seokjun Park, Jongsoo Baik, Hyoungtae Kim, Joohyun Son, Jinseok Choi

papers.title: Geometry-Evolving Barrier Functions for Safety Evaluation in Dynamic Environments
papers.summary: Autonomous systems operating in dynamic environments often involve multiple interacting agents, giving rise to high-dimensional safety evaluation problems. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides rigorous finite-horizon safety guarantees, but solving a global HJ partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire state space leads to prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we introduce Geometry-Evolving Barrier Functions (GEBFs), a novel representation for dynamic safety evaluation that propagates local safety geometry of the solution to a terminal-value HJ PDE. By evolving the value, gradient, and curvature information along a Hamiltonian-induced reference trajectory, GEBFs provide a compact representation of the local HJ safety landscape. Under suitable local regularity assumptions, we establish consistency between the GEBF and the value, gradient, and Hessian of the HJ solution along an HJ-optimal characteristic. Building on these theoretical results, we develop an iterative algorithm that couples local geometric propagation with trajectory refinement. We further establish a trajectory-wise one-sided relationship between the GEBF and HJ value function, together with a fixed-point consistency result for the iterative scheme. Experiments on widely adopted agent--obstacle collision-avoidance benchmarks, across low- and high-dimensional systems, demonstrate that GEBFs accurately capture the evolution of dynamic safety boundaries, while achieving substantially lower computational cost than conventional HJ reachability.

authors.name: Zhi Zhang, Francesco Belardinelli, Alessandro Abate

papers.title: Power-Swing Blocking Scheme Based on Continuous and Higher-Order Incremental Quantities for Systems with Inverter-Based Resources
papers.summary: Conventional power-swing blocking (PSB) schemes for distance protection face new and emerging challenges as the penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs) increase. Several papers highlight interoperability issues concerning faster power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories. Revised relay settings are proposed in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance trajectory over the tiny region between the blinders, making it difficult to distinguish between fast swings and faults. Moreover, blinders have the inherent limitation that they cannot operate if the measured impedance is inside the blinders when the fault is cleared and immediately enters the distance zones during the first swing cycle - an issue often overlooked in the current literature. This paper proposes a novel PSB scheme based on higher-order incremental quantities (IQs) for difficult swing scenarios with IBRs and synchronous generators (SGs). PSCAD/EMTDC simulations of an SG and an implemented grid-forming (GFM) inverter validate its superior performance compared to conventional dual-blinder PSB schemes. The impacts of GFM inverters on the impedance measured by distance relays during the fault-to-swing transition and first power swing cycle are also discussed.

authors.name: Henrik Johansson, Qianli Xing, Nathaniel Taylor, Xiongfei Wang

papers.title: Reliable Bistatic Ranging With Unreliable Communication Payloads
papers.summary: This paper addresses a key challenge in bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC): \textit{How to achieve reliable ranging using communication data signals that cannot be reliably recovered?} In modern communication systems, data payloads typically occupy far more time-frequency resources than pilots, offering substantially more observations to improve sensing accuracy. Exploiting them requires recovering the transmitted symbols to form sensing references. However, propagation and reflection losses can severely weaken target echoes. The sensing receiver may therefore be unable to recover data transmitted at a high rate selected for communication users. We first show that, at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), using hard symbol decisions as sensing references can introduce a persistent bias in the estimated channel impulse response (CIR). This bias produces an error floor and spurious peaks in the power delay profile (PDP) that persist even after coherent accumulation over a large number of observations. To address this limitation, we develop a pilot-initialized expectation-maximization (EM) estimator that iteratively refines the CIR using posterior symbol moments. Under local regularity conditions and successful initialization, we establish that the EM method converges to the local maximum-likelihood (ML) solution for a sufficiently large number of OFDM data symbols. The converged estimator is asymptotically unbiased, where the CIR estimation mean-square error (MSE) at each delay bin decays as $O(1/M)$ by accumulating $M$ data symbols. Thus, estimation error can vanish through sufficient accumulation even while symbol recovery remains highly unreliable. Numerical results validate the proposed method, demonstrating substantially higher target detection probabilities than pilot-only and hard-decision-based bistatic ranging under the same low-SNR conditions.

authors.name: Fangping Yu, Fan Liu, Yifeng Xiong, Jie Yang, Lei Xie, Shi Jin

papers.title: Sparse Bayesian Sensing for Antenna Arrays with Per-Element Gain, Phase, and Position Errors
papers.summary: The sensing capabilities of 6G wireless communication systems rely on accurate models of phased-array antennas. However, hardware imperfections can introduce a mismatch between the assumed and the actual array response, leading to performance degradations. To prevent these, we propose a parametric, model-based sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) channel estimation algorithm with integrated self-calibration, which accounts for antenna-position deviations as well as gain and phase offsets. The algorithm learns channel parameters such as delay and direction-of-arrival (DoA), together with per-antenna complex weights and position deviations based on fast variational SBL with dictionary refinement. We derive a marginal-likelihood-based cost function for the antenna position update. The sensing performance is evaluated in terms of the optimal subpattern-assignment (OSPA) metric of the delay and DoA. The proposed method approaches a benchmark based on the derived hybrid Cram\'er--Rao lower bound (HCRLB) in the considered single-snapshot sensing scenarios. Finally, we investigate the influence of the detection threshold using synthetic and measurement data. On single-snapshot measurements, our algorithm reduces the position OSPA from about 6 m to 0.2 m for an appropriately chosen threshold.

authors.name: Patrick H\"odl, Erik Leitinger, Klaus Witrisal

papers.title: Scenario-aware Adaptive Neuromorphic Intelligence for multimodal sensor fusion
papers.summary: Multisensory Physical AI systems operating in isolated conditions must make timely and reliable decisions within strict energy and hardware budgets. In this context, the present analytical study investigates the feasibility of reliable multimodal sensor fusion using a neuromorphic approach based on memristor-based Integrate-and-Fire neuron circuits driven by aggressively compressed representations of sensory information. Rather than relying on fixed processing and learning parameters, the proposed framework introduces scenario-dependent adaptability into individual stages of the neuromorphic decision-making pipeline, including sensor-data compression, nonlinear spike encoding, reliability assessment, and memristive learning-forgetting dynamics. By coupling multiple sensor inputs through adaptive memristive synapses, the framework investigates how reliable and correlated observations can strengthen learned associations, while weak or obsolete relationships gradually decay through nonlinear forgetting. The resulting neuronal responses are evaluated across ten representative driving scenarios derived from the NuScenes dataset by comparing their encoded output patterns with predefined synthetic ground-truth codes representing the expected actuator responses. The simulations demonstrate that scenario-adaptive activity-vector sizing achieves a 61.5% reduction in retained sensory information, while improving mean bit-wise agreement from approximately 55% to 61.2% compared with a fixed maximum-resolution configuration. These findings highlight the potential of introducing scenario-aware adaptability directly into the building blocks of a neuromorphic system, providing a foundation for future hardware implementations that could significantly transform the capabilities of Physical AI systems operating under stringent resource and environmental constraints.

authors.name: Kapil Bhardwaj, Tauseef Ejaz, Sayani Majumdar

papers.title: From Choirs to Solos: Reducing Multi-Cell Cooperation via Pinching Antennas
papers.summary: This article investigates the potential of the pinching-antenna system (PASS) to reduce multi-cell cooperation requirements. Flexible pinching-antenna (PA) placement can enhance desired channel gains and reduce the required transmit power, which consequently alleviates inter-cell interference and the need for cooperative transmission. A two-cell PASS is considered, where the cooperation cost is quantified by the number of additional base station-user data associations. The cooperation cost is minimized subject to user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio requirements and individual transmit-power constraints. Joint PA placement and transmission designs are developed using alternating optimization and second-order cone programming, while low-complexity zero-forcing-based alternatives are also proposed. Numerical results demonstrate that PASS substantially reduces cooperation requirements compared with the conventional fixed-antenna system. These findings highlight the potential of PASS to transform cooperative multi-cell ``\emph{choirs}'' into independent ``\emph{solos}''.

authors.name: Zhenqiao Cheng, Chongjun Ouyang, Zhiguo Ding

papers.title: Spatial Reuse in Multi-Cell Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.summary: In this paper, spatial reuse in a multi-cell pinching-antenna system (PASS) is investigated, where each cell employs a dielectric waveguide with one activated pinching antenna (PA) to serve a single user. Spatial reuse refers to the simultaneous use of the same time-frequency resource block (RB) by multiple spatially separated cells. Due to inter-cell interference (ICI), simultaneous transmission by all cells on the same RB may be infeasible, and multiple RBs may be required to serve all users. The spatial-reuse capability is thus characterized by the minimum number of RBs required to satisfy all users' signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) targets under per-cell power budgets. Flexible PA placement can enhance the desired-link gain of each user and reduce the required transmit power of its serving cell, which in turn mitigates ICI and allows more cells to share the same RB. To exploit these benefits, a joint optimization problem of RB allocation, PA placement, and power control is formulated. For the two-cell case, the globally optimal PA placement is determined by minimizing the peak transmit power required by the two cells. A one-dimensional special case is further analyzed to derive analytical expressions for the average RB requirement and its scaling laws with respect to cell length under different PA-placement strategies. For the general multi-cell case, the optimal two-cell solution is exploited to construct a weighted compatibility graph, whose edge weights represent the minimum peak transmit powers required for feasible pairwise RB reuse. Based on this graph, a greedy RB allocation algorithm with minimum-weight pair initialization and element-wise PA-placement optimization is developed. Numerical results validate the analytical findings and demonstrate that PASS significantly reduces the required RBs compared with conventional fixed-antenna systems.

authors.name: Zhenqiao Cheng, Chongjun Ouyang, Zhiguo Ding

papers.title: Angle Estimation for Initial Access in True-Time-Delay Systems: Communication and Sensing Tradeoff
papers.summary: In joint communication & sensing (JCNS) the data signal is used to obtain parameter estimates. An example is the angle of arrival (AoA) which can be used to solve the initial access problem of beam selection. true-time delay (TTD) arrays are attractive for this purpose, as their frequency-dependent response encodes the angle information in the receive signal power spectrum. This work investigates the tradeoff between angle estimation accuracy and achievable data rate for uplink signals in a TTD array. The Fisher information (FI) for the angle is used to find the bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) under the assumption of a raised cosine distributed angle prior. Maximization of the FI under a data rate constraint is solved by waterfilling power per frequency bin dependent on sensing weights. Compared to a frequency flat signal, the optimized power allocation increases the FI \approx 4.9 dB at 5% rate loss for prior width of \pm 10{\deg}. Numerical simulations show that the derived BCRLB can be attained by a maximum likelihood (ML) estimator above an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold, confirming that the FI underlying the waveform design is attainable.

authors.name: Carl Collmann, Ahmad Nimr, Gerhard Fettweis

papers.title: Joint Higher-Order Low-Rank Tensor Decompositions for Multichannel Acoustic System Compression
papers.summary: Multichannel room impulse responses (RIRs) in acoustics are often long and therefore the sample count becomes large if seen as finite impulse response (FIR) filters, making storage and real-time convolution costly. Pole-zero (PZ) models are an established way to represent RIRs compactly as infinite impulse response (IIR) transfer functions. We show that a PZ model implies a low-rank canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) of tensorized RIRs: the early reflections form a sparse rank-1 sum, while the late reverberation admits a CPD with factors determined by the poles. This motivates higher-order-tensor-based compression of RIRs via the block term decomposition (BTD), a generalization of the CPD. We propose two multichannel compression schemes: (i) a stacked multichannel block term decomposition (SMCBTD) applied to a (D+1)-mode tensor of RIRs, and (ii) a joint multichannel block term decomposition (JMCBTD) that shares subsets of factors across channels discovered by spectral clustering on factor-subspace affinity graphs. Both are optimized by an alternating higher-order orthogonal iteration (HOOI) procedure. On simulated rooms as well as measured datasets, the proposed methods achieve consistently lower reconstruction error at equal compression ratios compared to separate single-channel decompositions and a generalized low-rank approximation of matrices (GLRAM) baseline. The largest gains occur with scalar cores (i.e., CPD), supporting the PZ-to-CPD modelling link. We also find D = 3 to be a practical sweet spot, offering most of the achievable gain at moderate compute/memory cost. The compressed models enable efficient downstream multichannel convolution.

authors.name: Matthias Blochberger, Filip Elvander, Jan {\O}stergaard, Toon van Waterschoot

papers.title: Extensions to the Dubins Airplane Method - Flight Performance Constraints in Uniform Wind
papers.summary: This paper extends the Dubins Airplane Method to generate trajectories for fixed-wing aircraft that remain within flight performance limits in the presence of uniform wind. Within the field of runtime-efficient trajectory generation for fixed-wing aircraft, the Dubins Airplane Method represents a well-received and widely adopted compromise between algorithmic complexity, runtime efficiency, and solution quality. However, its simplistic kinematic model restricts its ability to generate safe and feasible trajectories, especially in the presence of wind. As a mathematical foundation to overcome these limitations, a set of closed-form equations are derived that relate flight performance constraints to kinematic constraints. Building upon existing methods that use trochoids for planning of 2D trajectories in uniform wind, this paper presents a set of iterative algorithms for planning versatile 3D trajectories composed of trochoidal or circular turns and straight flight segments, with constant vertical speed, constant thrust or smooth longitudinal transitions. The presented methods comprise a flexible and modular framework for runtime-efficient generation of performance-aware trajectories based on parametric curves without the need for numerical trajectory representations.

authors.name: Simon Schopferer

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Channel Aging in MIMO Systems: When Is Kronecker Separability Enough?
papers.summary: This letter investigates when Kronecker-separable spatial correlation approximates the covariance of multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels. We propose a geometry-aware channel model in which the same propagation environment determines both the Weischelberger spatial coupling matrix and the temporal correlation coefficient. The propagation environment follows a 3GPP-inspired clustered channel model. We consider a MIMO system affected by symbol-level channel aging caused by the user equipment's mobility. We schedule both uplink and downlink pilots, thereby deriving the respective spectral efficiencies (SEs) in the presence of imperfect channel state information. Numerical results show that channel aging's magnitude is strongly geometry-dependent, with diffuse propagation inducing greater temporal decorrelation and SE degradation than concentrated scattering. The results also identify regimes where Kronecker separability can be applied and regimes where geometry-aware Weischelberger coupling is needed.

authors.name: Steven Rivetti, Gabor Fodor, Emil Bjornson, Mikael Skoglund

papers.title: Types of Bursting with a Two-Block Spiking Primitive
papers.summary: Excitable spikers are attractive systems for sparse, event-driven computation. A spiking primitive composed of a linear frequency selector closed in positive feedback around a high-gain saturating nonlinearity has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable system. This paper asks which bursting classes that primitive can produce with two elementary selectors: a first-order high-pass filter, and a second-order resonant band-pass filter. The nonlinearity decides whether the system fires, and where the rheobase sits. The selector decides whether rest and repetitive firing can coexist, and therefore which bursting class is available. We show that the high-pass never makes rest and firing coexist, whatever the nonlinearity, and that no linear slow feedback branch can then produce bursting. With a piecewise linear nonlinearity, it gives type I excitability, and a second copy of the primitive gives parabolic bursting. The resonant band-pass gives a Hopf, type II excitability, and a subcritical onset above a computable gain, hence a window where rest and firing coexist. A single additional slow linear feedback then gives elliptic bursting. We also show that the resting point is unique for both selectors, which makes square-wave bursting structurally unavailable. Closed-form thresholds, firing rates, and criticality conditions are given and validated numerically.

authors.name: Arthur Fyon, Julien Brandoit, Loris Mendolia, Pierre Sacr\'e, Guillaume Drion, Alessio Franci, Christian Fernandez Lorden, Gustave Bainier

papers.title: On the Minimal Controllability of Boolean Networks With $k$-Regular Dependency Graphs
papers.summary: Boolean networks (BNs) are widely used to model gene regulatory networks and other biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the minimal controllability problem for BNs subject to degree constraints. We first establish three new best-case upper bounds for XOR-BNs whose dependency graphs are $k$-regular. We then introduce classes of BNs that are invariant under cyclically partite transformation (CPT-invariant) and prove theorems connecting BN controllability with the surjectivity of vector-valued Boolean functions. Finally, by combining an analysis of this surjectivity with a probabilistic argument, we derive a new general lower bound on the minimum number of control nodes required for majority-type threshold BNs with $(2k+1)$-regular dependency graphs.

authors.name: Christopher H. Fok, Chi-Wing Wong, Wai-Ki Ching

papers.title: A Hybrid UKF with Explicit Drivetrain Modeling for Low-Velocity State Estimation of Electric Vehicles
papers.summary: Longitudinal velocity is a core input for vehicle control, driver-assistance, and automated driving functions. Production wheel-speed sensors deliver only a few pulses per revolution, so they lose resolution below 1 km/h, the regime in which automated parking and traffic-jam assistance operate. The motor speed from the electric machine's resolver stays finely resolved down to standstill but reaches the wheels only through a compliant drivetrain. We therefore estimate the longitudinal velocity with an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) on a double-track model adapted to low velocities and incorporate the motor speed along two routes, one purely physical and one hybrid. The first augments the model with an explicit torsional spring-damper drivetrain, making the motor speed a state of the estimator. The second feeds the output of a neural network-based virtual wheel-speed sensor into the UKF as a pseudo-measurement. Both routes are compared against two baselines, a wheel-speed-only configuration and one that adds the motor-speed sensor but treats the driveline as rigid. Because the model is numerically stiff near standstill, the comparison rests on a systematic study of explicit and semi-implicit discretization schemes. All four configurations are evaluated against an inertial reference in real-world test drives with two distinct series-production electric vehicles, anonymized as Vehicle A and Vehicle B for confidentiality. Below 1 km/h, both proposed estimators lower the velocity root-mean-square error by at least 54% and 45% against both baselines on Vehicle A. Carried over zero-shot to Vehicle B without re-tuning on target-vehicle data, they lower it by at least 41% and 51%. Both estimators therefore carry across vehicles without a new identification campaign.

authors.name: Hendrik Sch\"afke, Daniel O. M. Weber, Thomas Seel, Askar Vagapov, Jannes Iatropoulos, Christoph Schweers, Ahmed Trabelsi, Roman Henze, Simon F. G. Ehlers

papers.title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion
papers.summary: This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.

authors.name: Jo\~ao T. Diz, Paulo Rosa, Pedro Simpl\'icio, Paul Acquatella, Erik-Jan van Kampen, Spilios Theodoulis

papers.title: SubRoformer: Subband Time-Domain Representation for Music Source Separation
papers.summary: Music source separation extracts vocals and instruments from a mixed recording, enabling remixing, content production, and music analysis. Existing systems commonly operate on waveforms or full-band spectrograms. Waveform inputs contain many samples even in short segments, whereas a single spectrogram resolution imposes a shared time-frequency resolution trade-off across frequency ranges. We propose SubRoFormer, a Transformer-based system comprising a subband module and a residual RoFormer module. The subband module decomposes the mixture into frequency-localized, lower-rate signals for separation. It then reconstructs the target waveforms from the estimated subbands. The residual RoFormer module models temporal and cross-band relationships on temporally compressed features. It combines this context with fine-rate features through gated residual fusion to estimate source-specific complex masks. On the MUSDB18-HQ test set, training only on MUSDB18-HQ yields an average signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) of 10.63 dB across four stems using target-specific models, achieving state-of-the-art performance among the compared systems without extra training data. With 500 additional training songs, a single model jointly separating all four stems achieves an average SDR of 11.59 dB, establishing state-of-the-art performance among the compared single-model multi-stem systems trained with extra data. Code and checkpoints are released at https://github.com/ArchiMickey/SubRoformer.

authors.name: Chunyat Wu, Chuang Ding, Paris Smaragdis, Qiuqiang Kong

papers.title: Structured Agentic Learning for Persistent Spatial Acquisition in RDT-TAIS-Assisted Communications
papers.summary: Persistent TAIS operation can reduce repeated radio-information acquisition by reusing environmental knowledge across control intervals. This knowledge changes with radio-environment evolution and current communication task. This paper studies persistent spatial knowledge maintenance for TAIS control and formulates it as a sequential information-acquisition problem that maximizes effective communication performance while accounting for physical-acquisition overhead under an outage-reliability constraint. We develop structured agentic spatial intelligence (ASI), which realizes a communication-oriented agent that maintains persistent spatial knowledge, forms beliefs from radio and context observations, and adapts physical information acquisition through closed-loop interaction with the radio environment. By jointly exploiting radio-consistent context inference, temporal knowledge-sufficiency assessment, graph-structured regional reasoning, and predictive outage-risk feedback, structured ASI determines when additional acquisition is needed, where it is directed, and how much physical information is sufficient before stopping or escalating to full radio-environment reacquisition. Numerical results show that structured ASI improves the effective rate by 2.59% while reducing acquisition overhead by 25.0% at six structural changes per 100 control intervals, and achieves a 2.82% effective-rate gain with a 41.8% overhead reduction over a heterogeneous 400-interval mission.

authors.name: Bin Liu, Wei Ni, Tommy Svensson, Sofie Pollin

papers.title: Improving the Clinical Generalizability of Machine Learning-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection Across Domains and Modalities: A Comprehensive Review
papers.summary: Objective: This review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of domain adaptation (DA) and domain general- ization (DG) strategies for AD detection. It focuses on their potential to improve the robustness, generalizability, and clinical reliability of ML-based diagnostic systems. Methods: We conduct a comprehensive scoping review of existing DA and DG approaches across multiple data modalities. The reviewed studies are organized according to data modality, algorithmic framework, adaptation strat- egy, clinical relevance, and reported cross-domain performance. Key methodological trends, performance gains, limitations, and remaining challenges are analyzed to identify future research directions. Results: DA and DG approaches have demonstrated encouraging improvements in cross-domain performance and model robustness. Emerging modalities, such as speech-based approaches, EEG and eye-tracking data, show great po- tential for early, accessible, and non-invasive cognitive assessments. However, important limitations remain, including insufficient external validation, limited interpretability, computational complexity, privacy concerns, and challenges in scaling to routine clinical practice. Conclusion: DA and DG provide important methodological pathways for developing more generalizable ML-based systems for AD detection. Future research should prioritize explainable, computationally efficient, privacy-preserving, and clinically validated DA/DG techniques. Strengthening these aspects will be essential for translating robust AI- based AD detection tools into clinically deployable solutions.

authors.name: Yingchao Huang, Yuhan Su, Xin Wang, Shanshan Yao

papers.title: Optical Network Digital Twin: From Digital Coherent Transmission to Intelligent Network Operations
papers.summary: Optical Network Digital Twins (ONDTs) are emerging as a key framework for representing, synchronizing, and utilizing the physical state of optical networks for quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, optimization, and intelligent operation. This survey provides a comprehensive view of ONDTs, spanning digital coherent transmission and physical-layer observability to intelligent network operations. We systematically organize ONDT technologies from ecosystem, functional, control, and implementation architecture perspectives and review the enabling technologies required to construct, synchronize, and utilize digital representations of physical optical networks. As a unifying framework to describe both ONDT design and validation, we introduce a categorization based on the following figures of merit: Fidelity, Dynamicity, and Deployability (FDD). In particular, we emphasize fit-for-purpose Fidelity, where modeling effort focuses on the physical effects of components rather than solely maximizing model accuracy, favoring scalability and generalizability. Furthermore, experimental and field validations are examined to evaluate the practical applicability of ONDT technologies. We further examine experimental and field validations, from physics-based QoT estimation and measurement-informed model refinement to field synchronization, service provisioning, multi-domain observability, and infrastructure characterization. Finally, we discuss the complementary roles of ONDTs and AI agents toward autonomous optical networks and identify key research directions for practical deployment.

authors.name: Hideki Nishizawa, Enrico Miotto, Andrea Rosso, Takahito Tanimura, Zehao Wang, Mingzhe Han, Hiroyuki Ishihara, Andrea D'Amico, Agastya Raj, Rocco D'Ingillo, Takeo Sasai, Giacomo Borraccini, Toru Mano, Renato Ambrosone, Behnam Shariati, Oscar Gonz'alez-de-Dios, Arturo Mayoral L'opez de Lerma, Jun-ichi Kani, Manabu Yoshimoto, Tingjun Chen, Marco Ruffini, Daniel Kilper, Vittorio Curri

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of Sparse Bipartite Graphs via the Line-Graphon
papers.summary: Pure point spectral convergence is generally unavailable for sparse graph sequences, where Laplacian eigenvalues may remain unstable under graph growth. This poses challenges for analyzing spectral operators underlying many graph-based learning methods, including graph neural networks. We identify a class of sparse bipartite graph sequences for which eigenvalue-level spectral convergence can be recovered. Focusing on graphs with strong degree heterogeneity, we exploit the convergence properties of their line-graph sequences. Using a spectral correspondence between bipartite graph Laplacians and line-graph adjacency operators, we transfer convergence guarantees from dense line-graphs back to the original sparse graphs. This framework yields eigenvalue-level spectral convergence for a class of deterministic sparse graph sequences. We further analyze superlinear preferential attachment trees, establishing convergence to an infinite-dimensional limit operator. Numerical experiments empirically support our spectral convergence results.

authors.name: Roxanne Holden, Luana Ruiz

papers.title: Wireless Link Scheduling with Graph Signal Diffusion
papers.summary: We solve long-horizon wireless link scheduling with per-link minimum transmission constraints. Fair distribution of resources across links and time steps requires stochastic scheduling, motivating a diffusion framework. Via imitation learning, we train a diffusion model to sample scheduling decisions, conditioning generation on the network topology and constraint levels. The parameterization is achieved through a U-Graph Neural Network (U-GNN) to leverage the relationship between graphs and wireless networks for learning. Our approach achieves near-optimal performance, maximizing sum rate while distributing allocations across different links over time horizons. The U-GNN-based diffusion model generalizes to requirements and network sizes unseen during training, demonstrating the robustness of the approach.

authors.name: Teresa Shang, Romina Garcia Camargo, Yi\u{g}it Berkay Uslu, Alejandro Ribeiro

papers.title: Electromagnetically Consistent Monostatic ISAC Beamforming: Mutual Coupling, Active Mismatch and Tx-Rx Leakage in Compact Dipole Arrays
papers.summary: Beamforming for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is usually designed on ideal array manifolds with a norm constraint on the transmit signal. In a compact monostatic transceiver this hides three antenna effects: distorted embedded patterns, beam-dependent active mismatch at the power amplifiers, and transmit-to-receive leakage that raises the radar noise floor. We build a multiport scattering model of a shared-aperture dipole array directly from method-of-moments simulations and use it to formulate a Cramer-Rao bound minimizing ISAC beamformer with multiuser SINR constraints, per-port active reflection constraints and a leakage budget, solved as a semidefinite program with a one-dimensional budget search. Full-wave evaluation shows that coupling-unaware designs miss their SINR targets by up to 6.2 dB and drive amplifiers to an equivalent VSWR above 3.3 at small spacings. For spacings from 0.3 to 0.5 wavelengths, the proposed design meets all targets with an equivalent VSWR below 2 and lowers the root Cramer-Rao bound by 32 to 53 percent for 80 dB of self-interference cancellation and by a factor of 3.4 to 5.6 for 70 dB. An independent finite-difference time-domain model of the final layout in openEMS confirms that the leakage null and the ranking of the designs are preserved.

authors.name: Stylianos D. Asimonis, Christos Tselios, Dimitrios Tyrovolas, Ilias Politis, George K. Karagiannidis

papers.title: Output-Feedback Integral Sliding-Mode Extremum Seeking with Super-Twisting Differentiation
papers.summary: This paper develops a dither-free output-feedback extremum-seeking controller for pre-stabilized nonlinear dynamic systems with unknown steady-state performance maps. The controller uses only the measured performance, the applied parameter, and internal states. Within a local state--parameter domain, integral sliding mode enforces equality between the applied parameter rate and a prescribed nonzero search velocity after finite-time capture under bounded matched rate-channel perturbations. This motion lets a super-twisting differentiator and rate normalization recover a gradient-sign surrogate without demodulation or averaging. A ramp-corrected moving-equilibrium coordinate cancels the first-order ramp-induced plant term and yields explicit flow, reversal, recovery, and dynamic-remainder bounds. The resulting local state--parameter tube supplies the regularity needed for finite-time exact differentiation. Combined with a deadbanded hybrid relay, these results establish local practical convergence to an explicit neighborhood of the unknown optimum. An 80-state tubular-reactor benchmark and paired held-out Monte Carlo tests compare a causal sampled realization with perturbation ESC and a rate-informed super-twisting comparator. The proposed realization succeeds in all 200 held-out cases and attains the smallest upper-tail objective gap under the stated tuning protocol. A matched-rate sweep connects performance degradation to applied-rate mismatch, near-stall motion, reversal, and regularization attenuation.

authors.name: Hyuntae Kim

papers.title: Estimating Distribution Grid Upgrade Costs based on County-level Building Electrification Projections
papers.summary: Building electrification projections are typically developed at aggregated geographic levels to support bulk power system analysis, even though a significant portion of the infrastructure investments required to accommodate electrification occurs within distribution systems. Existing methodologies to disaggregate load growth projections onto distribution networks are based on context-specific analyses that require detailed data on building electricity consumption, distribution feeders, and geographic parcels, which are often proprietary and unavailable for policy and economic impact studies. This paper presents a methodology to disaggregate county-level building electrification projections onto representative distribution feeders and evaluate their impact on distribution upgrade costs. The proposed approach combines bulk system end-use electrification projections with representative feeder sets to generate building-level electrification measures. These measures are then used to create load profiles that are consistent with county-level projections while preserving the spatial diversity of electrification demand required for distribution infrastructure analysis. Using a case study of Genesee County, in Michigan, the results show that the proposed methodology is able to capture a diversity of feeder-level responses to electrification and represent the different realities that building electrification produces within the distribution system. This allows to represent localized load variations and capture more realistic distribution system upgrade costs driven by electrification.

authors.name: Miguel Heleno, Albane Seres

papers.title: Core-Lock Scheduling for 5G NR LDPC Decoders
papers.summary: Accelerating iterative LDPC decoding while preserving error-correction reliability is a critical challenge in latency-constrained 5G New Radio (NR) and non-terrestrial networks. This paper proposes a hardware-efficient core-lock scheduling mechanism that evaluates the core syndrome weight after each layer update to selectively bypass extension layers. With the selected threshold $\theta{=}0.20$, the mechanism reduces decoding latency by up to 31.3\% when integrated with static schedules, and by up to 45.5\% compared to alternative dynamic schemes utilizing the full parity-check matrix, without block error rate (BLER) degradation. Compared with an estimated fully parallel full-matrix checker, the core-only approach yields a 76\% reduction in shifter network area and a 73\% reduction in XOR gate count. For decoders with existing early termination, the proposed mechanism requires only a compact adder tree and a comparator.

authors.name: N. Papageorgiou, V. Paliouras

papers.title: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
papers.summary: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.

authors.name: Unnikrishna Pillai

papers.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
papers.summary: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods. This paper proposes a real-time BESS dispatch framework using polynomial diffusion models (PDMs) to forecast both electricity prices and DC loads. Leveraging the closed-form conditional expectations of PDMs, the forecasts are integrated into a dynamic programming (DP) framework to minimize electricity procurement costs. Across the evaluated BESS configurations, the proposed approach achieves 2.63 times the cost savings of a rule-based (RB) strategy.

authors.name: Matthew Van Ham, Yiping Liu, Xiaozhe Wang

papers.title: A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis
papers.summary: Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework in which a text-based corpus identifies the leading factors of a failure mode. Physics-based models then quantify how likely that failure is at a stated operating point. Ordered causal chains extracted from 56{,}202 American accident reports with a local large language model aggregate into a causation knowledge graph. On an evaluation sample of 2{,}000 reports, the chains recover 90.8\% of investigator-flagged causes. Each physical factor whose drivers the record carries receives an occurrence model calibrated to the accident population. A leaky noisy-OR fitted to the corpus combines the factors into a failure mode probability that supports intervention. For engine power loss, the carburetor icing model separates 1{,}205 icing accidents from other accidents using temperature and dewpoint alone, reaching 0.61 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve against a density ratio ceiling of 0.64. Routine weather hours give no valid control, because flying concentrates in fair weather. On later years the physics adds 0.03 to that area for occurrence and nothing for severity, so its value lies in interpretability. On four named accidents, abduction gives a probability of necessity of 0.29 to 0.50 for the heat omission, under monotonicity. The Fast Causal Inference algorithm does not license the largest backdoor adjustment on the learned networks.

authors.name: Yutian Pang, Yifang Tian, Xinyu Zhao, Jueming Hu, John-Paul Clarke, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

papers.title: Noether's Second Theorem and the Pareto Front Structure in Multi-Criteria Variational Problems
papers.summary: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between Noether's second theorem and the structure of Pareto fronts in multi-criteria variational problems. We prove that for a family of functionals invariant under a common gauge Lie group, the regular part of the Pareto front is contained in the union of solutions to weighted Euler--Lagrange equations, and that on Pareto-optimal sections, combinations of Noether currents are conserved. Gauge symmetries are shown to impose additional constraints on the Lagrange multipliers via Bianchi-type identities, reducing the dimension of the admissible weight space. Two practical approaches are derived from this result: dimensionality reduction via gauge fixing and scalarization with penalty terms. The theory is validated on three classical problems: the linear-quadratic regulator with two criteria, a model predictive control problem with a minimax criterion, and the double integrator with control constraints. In each case, the Pareto front is shown to satisfy an exact conservation law, and the analytical structure of the front is recovered from the symmetries of the problem. The results demonstrate that gauge functions (null Lagrangians) can restore invariants even when the dynamics break the symmetry, and that control constraints do not destroy the underlying conservation laws but merely restrict the admissible set. The proposed approach yields a Pareto front with minimal deviation from the theoretical curve, outperforming known multi-objective algorithms, and provides a new foundation for the analytical treatment of multi-criteria optimization in nonlinear dynamics and control.

authors.name: Evgeny Nikulchev

papers.title: An Ordering Optimization for Fruit-Vegetable in High-Density Environment based on Genetic Algorithm
papers.summary: This paper presents a robotic harvesting method that combines RGB-D fruit localization, GA-based harvest ordering, and waypoint-based robot motion in dense and unstructured crop environments. The global RGB-D camera provides 3D fruit positions for ordering, while the end-effector-mounted camera provides close-range observation during execution. The GA determines the harvesting sequence, and static or dynamic waypoints define the intermediate robot motion. The method was evaluated in a controlled laboratory testbed and in four-, five-, and six-fruit field conditions. GA solutions were compared with exhaustive enumeration, and both waypoint offsets were examined by parameter sensitivity analysis. Continuous execution reduced unnecessary Home-return motion, while the dynamic waypoint changed with the remaining fruit distribution without changing the GA sequence. In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy produced 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 collision events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint continuous strategy.

authors.name: Jaehwi Seol, Jeonghyeon Pak, Hyoung Il Son

papers.title: A Synchronized Tri-Modality Wireless System for Multi-Point Non-Contact Cardiac Monitoring
papers.summary: Cardiac physiological monitoring is fundamental to evaluating cardiovascular health and diagnosing related diseases. Non-contact radar sensing can capture chest-wall vibrations with spatial specificity, enabling localized physiological monitoring and cardiac assessment. Progress, however, has been limited by the absence of a reliable, research-grade hardware platform for rigorous validation of radar-based methods. Prior systems typically pair radar, namely Doppler cardiography (DCG), with only electrocardiography (ECG) or other coarse references, providing no direct mechanical ground truth and thus constraining fine-grained evaluation of radar outputs. We present a tri-modality wireless system that integrates ECG, seismocardiography (SCG), and DCG under a unified acquisition and control framework for time-aligned recording and analysis. The tri-modality system combines miniaturized wearable ECG/SCG modules with a high-resolution mmWave radar module, supporting spatially resolved sensing and subsequent feature extraction. To our knowledge, this is the first integrated ECG--SCG--DCG hardware system for comprehensive cardiac monitoring; it enables multi-point thoracic acquisition, achieves precise cross-modal synchronization, and maintains specifications suitable for wearable operation. Experiments on a linear-motion platform show close agreement between DCG- and SCG-derived displacements, confirming accurate displacement measurement. Human-subject studies further demonstrate cross-modal consistency and robust extraction of feature points, establishing ECG as the electrical anchor and SCG as the mechanical ground truth for DCG. Overall, the system provides a rigorous, spatially resolved validation platform that advances non-contact cardiac sensing and supports next-generation radar-based monitoring.

authors.name: Wei Ren, Kaili Zhao, Huansheng Yi, Miaoyang Hu, Jianqi Wang, Canhua Xu, Fugui Qi

papers.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers
papers.summary: Replay attacks are difficult to detect in vision-based control systems because previously recorded observations can remain plausible while the physical system follows a different trajectory. This paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers. A private Gaussian watermark is added to the nominal control input, and a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) predicts the corresponding evolution in a compact latent space learned from image observations. Attack evidence is obtained from the discrepancy between the predicted latent response and the latent representation of the received image observation. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts the watermark covariance using the latent state and detector confidence, thereby balancing attack detectability, watermark energy, and control distortion. A Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs is included during training to limit the adverse effect of the excitation. The framework is evaluated on a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task in which the robot reaches a target while avoiding a moving human arm under nominal and replay-attacked observations.

authors.name: Aditya Parameshwaran, Navid Aftabi, Abhishek Hanchate, Satish T. S. Bukkapatnam, Dan Li, Yue Wang

papers.title: ProCraft: Instruction-Driven Music Production from Free-Form Text
papers.summary: Music production typically involves multiple editing operations that each require specialized tools and expertise. Existing text-guided music editing systems support few operations or instruments, operate on short clips, or handle only one operation per instruction, unlike real workflows where several changes are requested at once. Here, we present ProCraft, a lightweight 0.5B-parameter autoregressive codec language model that edits 30s music excerpts end-to-end from free-form instructions, including compound requests. ProCraft supports seven operations across eight instruments, from tasks with a unique target (e.g., track removal) to creative ones (e.g., accompaniment generation). We align intermediate representations with pretrained music embeddings and pitch and instrument targets to preserve content outside the edit, and gated cross-attention in every decoder layer to keep generation tied to the instruction. To train on compound requests, we introduce On-the-fly Editing-pair Synthesis, which generates paired instructions and audio combining track-level operations with effect changes. ProCraft performs competitively against task-specific systems on single-task editing, and outperforms four free-text editors on compound instructions for track removal, extraction and denoising on real (MoisesDB) and synthetic (Slakh) recordings. In a user study (16 listeners), ProCraft was rated highest on removal and denoising and on-par with a 16-times larger model on extraction and instrument transfer. Ablations further show that representation alignment and cross-attention reduce leakage from unwanted tracks and raise editing success rates, especially on out-of-domain data.

authors.name: Yuan-Chiao Cheng, Yi-Hsuan Yang, Vincent K. M. Cheung

papers.title: Kinematic analysis of a double-closed-loop four-bar chain-based leg for a multimodal quadruped-pentarotor robot
papers.summary: This paper presents the kinematic modeling and singularity analysis of a three-degree-of-freedom, double four-bar closed-loop quadruped leg mechanism. This leg is essential for transitioning between the two operational modes; therefore, it is examined in both joint and task spaces, leading to the development of its Jacobian matrix, which is vital for designing the gaits required for terrestrial mode and mid-air aerial reconfiguration (for aerial mode). Various gaits are devised for the system's motion in the MATLAB simulation, and their practical implementation on the single-leg test rig is demonstrated.

authors.name: Prashant Raturi, Santhakumar Mohan

papers.title: Training-Independent Validation of a Learning-Based Controller for Stunt Maneuvers
papers.summary: Learned controllers for vehicle maneuvers are usually validated under the conditions and objective used to train them, where they appear highly reliable, yet the parameters that change on real roads are often not those the model was trained on. We argue that validation must be independent of training: it should vary physical parameters that training kept fixed and use acceptance criteria absent from the training objective. A learning-based control policy, G-Maneuver, with 90.11% success is tested for stunt-level maneuvers. A looser terminal-heading score ranked the worst setting as the best. Because real stunt tests are safety-critical, a simulation-to-reality-to-simulation (Sim2Real2Sim) loop uses the simulation to select safe zones for real-vehicle trials with 16.9% acceptance. Automotive safety analysis frameworks are used to identify parameters for validation using coverage tests. We demonstrated that the kinematic stunt-driving indicators, namely heading change, sideslip, and speed-normalized yaw rate, match between simulation and the real world, while force and roll indicators do not, which identifies the indicators that can support safe deployment. A video of the experiments is available at https://youtu.be/dN1Oes8pNIo.

authors.name: Kiruthiga Chandra Shekar, Aliasghar Arab, Jingang Yi

papers.title: Unified Overview of Safety Certificate Functions: Techniques from Hamilton--Jacobi Reachability and Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Safety is a central concern in modern autonomous systems. Safety certificates---functions whose existence guarantees that a system meets its safety specification---have long been used as a principled tool for rigorously reasoning about safety. Methods for synthesizing such certificates are scattered across research areas, with little guidance on when to use a particular approach. This tutorial provides a holistic treatment of safety certificate synthesis centered on two widely used families: Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis and control barrier functions (CBFs). For each family of methods, we first introduce its general formulation, along with classical and learning-based tools for certificate synthesis. Next, we introduce two benchmark problems consisting of vehicle systems of differing complexity to assess the certificate quality of different synthesis methods and their effectiveness in safety-critical control. We use these benchmarks to compare various methods and provide practical guidance for selecting an approach.

authors.name: Hao Wang, Max Cohen, Zeyuan Feng, Donggeon David Oh, Oswin So, Songyuan Zhang, Javier Borquez, Chuchu Fan, Jaime Fern\'andez Fisac, Haimin Hu, Jason J. Choi, Somil Bansal

papers.title: K-subareas partitioning subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas
papers.summary: A method for the problem of partitioning an area into K subareas subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas is presented. The given area may be non-convex and may additionally include obstacle areas. The proposed hierarchical method involves three steps: repeated bisection splitting, merging and the solution of traveling salesman problems. Geographic real-world outdoors areas data is used for the evaluation of the method. The benefit of computational simplicity at the cost of imbalanced subarea sizes is highlighted.

authors.name: Mogens Plessen

papers.title: Online Optimization for Controlling HVAC Systems
papers.summary: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a significant portion of buildings' energy consumption, motivating the design of energy- and cost-efficient control strategies. However, conventional strategies employ simple, reactive control, without incorporating a model. Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.

authors.name: Tong Wu, Dominik Baumann, Angela Fontan, Nicola Bastianello

papers.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition
papers.summary: Tactile sensing provides information about object properties that can improve robotic grasping and manipulation. However, accurate object recognition during the early stages of grasping remains challenging, particularly under strict real-time constraints. This study presents a flexible, distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing system for early-stage object recognition. The system was experimentally evaluated using six everyday objects and three recognition approaches: feature-based classification using support vector machines (SVMs), raw-signal classification using 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) and convolutional recurrent neural networks (C-RNNs), and spatiotemporal heatmap classification using a 2D-CNN. The effects of sensor count and temporal window size on recognition accuracy and real-time feasibility were systematically investigated. Increasing the number of sensing elements improved recognition performance across all approaches. The best-performing method, based on spatiotemporal heatmaps and a 2D-CNN, achieved F1-scores of 0.9796, 0.9846, and 0.9903 using 16, 24, and 32 sensors, respectively. The optimal configuration, comprising 32 sensors and a 100-ms temporal window (50 samples), was deployed on an embedded edge platform, achieving an end-to-end recognition latency of approximately 101 ms from contact onset and an energy consumption of 63.8 microjoules per inference. These results demonstrate the potential of distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing for accurate, energy-efficient, and real-time object recognition during robotic grasping.

authors.name: Razan Khalifeh, Mohamad Yaacoub, Christian Gianoglio, Moustafa Saleh, Maurizio Valle, Yahya Abbass

papers.title: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking
papers.summary:
We study how the spectral geometry of the mixing matrix enters the convergence of decentralized stochastic gradient tracking (GT) for smooth strongly convex problems. General bounds contain the factor $\Delta_\lambda^{-3}$ in the higher-order stochastic term, where $\Delta_\lambda$ is the absolute spectral gap. We show that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, the exact steady-state mean-square disagreement scales as $\alpha^2\sigma^2\Delta_\lambda^{-3}$ as the nontrivial eigenvalue approaches $-1$, provided the stepsize $\alpha$ is sufficiently small relative to the gap.
